**Stage 3 (E18, path patching) — real-checkpoint run completed 2026-08-23.**
Built `hooks.py::path_patch_delta` (the two-forward primitive: patch `src`'s
o_proj-input slice to a replacement value, capture the induced delta at
`dst`'s own slice, with no causal-order check needed — a `dst` that executes
at or before `src` in the forward pass necessarily sees an unperturbed
input, which 4 new synthetic unit tests in `tests/test_path_patch.py`
confirm directly rather than trusting the argument) and
`seasonality_circuit.py::path_decompose_head`/`path_patch_circuit` (per-head
decomposition into `effect_direct` — noise `src` alone, with every other
selected-set member explicitly frozen to its own clean value, so none of
`src`'s effect can be credited via a path through them — plus a per-other-
member `effect_via`, and the conservation check `effect_direct +
sum(effect_via) ≈ effect_total`). New standalone CLI
`run_seasonality_circuit.py` (repo root of `tsfm_lens/`, following the
`run_layer_screen_bakeoff.py`/`run_crosscoder_stage0.py` pattern — not a
pipeline stage). 4 + 4 new tests, full `test_seasonality_circuit.py` +
`test_path_patch.py` suite green at 30/30 both before and after the
real-checkpoint run.

A first real-checkpoint attempt found and fixed a genuine bug in the new
CLI, caught only by a live run (the 26+4 unit tests call the underlying
functions directly, never the CLI): `run_seasonality_circuit.py` called
`save_json(result, out_path)`, but `save_json`'s actual signature
(`utils.py:158`) is `save_json(path, obj)` — the two positional arguments
were swapped, so the CLI crashed on its own output-writing step *after* the
whole Stage-3 computation had already completed successfully for both
models (confirmed since attempt 1's traceback originates inside
`save_json`, not inside `path_patch_circuit`). Fixed
(`save_json(out_path, result)`); a second real GPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6`)
was needed for Chronos-T5-Base only because GPU 0 on that box was ~93%
consumed by another user's unrelated processes at the time — not caused by
this session's code. Re-run after the fix succeeded for both models; the
canonical `runs/medium_run_chronos_base` directory was verified byte-for-
byte untouched (md5sum snapshot before/after) aside from a new, previously-
empty `seasonality_circuit/` subdirectory holding the two output JSONs.

**TimesFM** (degenerate 1-head set, `stacked_xf.6#4`), 24 series, wall-clock
8.47s: `effect_total = -0.0016414519632235`, `effect_direct` identical (no
other set members to freeze against — `effect_direct` is definitionally
`effect_total` when `others` is empty), `sum_paths` identical,
**`conservation_gap = 0.0`** exactly. This is a correctness check on the
degenerate-case code path (§2.5's "degrade gracefully" — verified exact by
construction, not merely close), not an informative test of the primitive
itself, since there is nothing to decompose.

**Chronos-T5-Base** (5-head set spanning `encoder.block.{4,7,8,9,10}#5`),
24 series, wall-clock 76.9s: `mean_abs_effect_total = 0.0107781`,
`mean_abs_conservation_gap = 0.0238143` — **the mean conservation gap is
more than double the mean effect size it is decomposing.** Per-head detail,
all five `src` values quoted exactly:
- `block.10#5` (the deepest head in the set): `effect_total = -0.0066883`,
  `effect_direct` identical, every `effect_via` entry **exactly 0.0**
  (`block.7#5`, `block.9#5`, `block.4#5`, `block.8#5` all `0.0`),
  `conservation_gap = 0.0` exactly. This is not a coincidence: every other
  set member sits at a shallower block, so `path_patch_delta`'s own
  causal-order guarantee (a `dst` that runs before `src` in the forward
  pass sees an unperturbed input) forces every one of those deltas to be
  exactly zero, which collapses `sum_paths` to `effect_direct` and closes
  the loop — a real-data confirmation of the exact same zero the synthetic
  unit tests already proved.
- `block.7#5` (2nd-shallowest): `effect_total = 0.0000820`
  (essentially zero — noising this head alone barely moves seasonal power),
  `effect_direct = 0.0206991`, `effect_via = {block.10#5: 0.0199338,
  block.9#5: 0.0155753, block.4#5: 0.0 (shallower than block.7 — the same
  causal-order zero as above), block.8#5: 0.0183793}`, `sum_paths =
  0.0745875`, **`conservation_gap = 0.0745055`** — roughly 900× the size of
  `effect_total` itself.
- `block.9#5`: `effect_total = 0.0197517`, `effect_direct = 0.0115162`,
  `sum_paths = 0.0147358`, `conservation_gap = -0.0050159`.
- `block.4#5` (shallowest): `effect_total = 0.0136183`, `effect_direct =
  0.0119839`, `sum_paths = 0.0438390`, `conservation_gap = 0.0302207` —
  over 2× `effect_total`.
- `block.8#5`: `effect_total = 0.0137503`, `effect_direct = 0.0056829`,
  `sum_paths = 0.0230798`, `conservation_gap = 0.0093296`.

**Verdict: the roadmap's own stated acceptance test for this stage — "the
path decomposition must sum to approximately the total effect... because a
wrong path primitive is otherwise nearly undetectable" — is NOT met for the
one non-degenerate case tested.** Read honestly rather than declared a pass
by fiat (`CLAUDE.md` §2.6): this is a genuine near-miss against the
pre-stated bar, not a rounding-level discrepancy. But three independent
pieces of evidence point at the cause being real nonlinear path interaction
in Chronos's circuit, not a bug in `path_patch_delta` itself: (1) every
`effect_via` value that the primitive's own causal-order argument requires
to be *exactly* zero (a `dst` shallower than `src`) came back exactly
`0.0` in this live run, not approximately zero — a bug in the delta
computation would have no reason to hit machine-zero on that subset only;
(2) `block.10`'s full-precision `effect_direct == effect_total` and
`conservation_gap == 0.0` emerged automatically from the general code path
with no special-casing, exactly as its position (deepest in the set, so no
other member can carry any of its effect) predicts; (3) the 4 synthetic
`test_path_patch.py` unit tests already pin the identical causal-order
property (nonzero for a genuine downstream pair, exactly zero same-block,
exactly zero upstream-`dst`, exactly zero for a no-op patch) independently
of any checkpoint. What conservation failing *does* mean: `effect_direct`
(measured with every other member frozen to clean) and each `effect_via`
(measured one `dst` at a time, with every *other* member also frozen to
clean) are each well-defined marginal measurements, but they do not sum
linearly to the effect measured when `src` is noised with nothing else
constrained — the paths through `block.7`'s noise interact with each other
(and/or with paths this decomposition doesn't isolate) rather than
contributing independently. This is a known, expected limitation of a
first-order additive path decomposition through a nonlinear (attention +
MLP) network with more than one interacting downstream path, not evidence
against the mechanism this repo built — but it does mean this specific
5-head circuit's `effect_direct`/`effect_via` split should be read as
"marginal, one-path-at-a-time effects," not as an exact attribution that
sums to the whole. TimesFM's 1-head set has no such structure to fail
(nothing to decompose), so its exact-zero conservation is a construction
check, not independent evidence the primitive scales cleanly to multi-path
sets — that question is answered, in the negative, only by the Chronos run.
Stage 4's report section (next) should state this distinction explicitly
rather than quote either model's conservation number as if it were a
general validity check on the method.

**Stage 4 (report section and writeup) — DONE 2026-08-23, closing H8.**
Built `report/report.py::_sec_seasonality_circuit(run_dir, model_colors,
findings)`, added right before `_sec_internals` and wired into the
`builders` list as a new "Circuit" section (`requires=[]`,
`config_attr="seasonality_circuit"`, mirroring the Fairness section's own
precedent for a report section with no backing `PipelineConfig` field —
`seasonality_circuit/` is written by the standalone
`run_seasonality_circuit.py`, not a pipeline stage, so there is no
`cfg.seasonality_circuit.enabled` to read). Degrades to `""` (logged) when
`seasonality_circuit/` doesn't exist or holds no `*_stageN_*.json`
artifacts, and degrades **per model and per stage within a model** — a
model with only Stage 3's conservation table (no Stage 1/2 trace) still
renders that table, and vice versa. Renders, per model: the Stage 2 greedy
restoration trace against the random-set null band with the selected-set
size marked, a necessity/sufficiency two-bar chart against the clean/
corrupted reference lines, and the Stage 3 per-head conservation table

#### Stage 1 · Single-component reproduction — the conservation gate `[x]` — ~0.2 session — DONE 2026-08-21 (see the Findings above, before this header, for the real-checkpoint numbers); this header's own checkbox had gone stale and is corrected here rather than left to mislead a future reader

Before any set search, score **every** candidate head one at a time on the
new metric and check the result against machinery already trusted:

- Ablation ΔMASE per head must reproduce `attention/meta.json`'s existing
  `head_delta` bit-for-bit when run at the same seed/rows (the same-inputs
  check `CLAUDE.md` §11.24 asks for; anything else means the new harness is
  not measuring what the old one did).
- The per-head *seasonal-power* ranking is then a genuinely new number, and
  its top entries should overlap `top_periodicity_heads` — **but a
  disagreement is a finding, not a failure**: the taxonomy scores *attention
  mass at seasonal lags*, this scores *causal effect on the forecast's own
  seasonal power*, and the taxonomy's own §18 F5 lesson is that a plausible
  head ranking can be an artifact of the axis it was computed on. Record the
  rank correlation either way.
- **Candidate set** = union of `top_periodicity_heads` (native resolution —
  legitimate here because H8 is **within-model**, which is precisely the case
  §18 F5's `resolution_mode` guidance exempts; state it explicitly in the
  artifact so it is not read as a cross-model claim) and the top `top_k`
  heads by single-head seasonal-power effect. Cap at `C ≤ 12`.

#### Stage 2 · The minimal set, with a null `[x]` — ~0.7 session — CLOSED 2026-08-21: both models clear their random-set null on the genuinely-minimal (trimmed) sets; see the Findings above for the missing-stopping-rule fix and the real-checkpoint numbers

- **Greedy forward selection** over the candidate set: at each step add the
  head whose addition most raises sufficiency restoration; stop when
  restoration ≥ `tau` (pre-register `tau = 0.8`) or when the best remaining
  addition improves it by less than the null's own spread. Report the whole
  greedy trace, not just the final set — where the curve saturates *is* the
  answer, and a set that never reaches `tau` is a reportable negative.
- **Necessity**: ablate exactly the selected set → seasonal power must fall
  to near the corrupted level. **Sufficiency**: patch exactly the selected
  set on a corrupted forward → restoration ≥ `tau`. Both are required; either
  alone is the weaker claim this item exists to stop making.
- 🔴 **The random-set null is mandatory and is the acceptance criterion.** A
  size-m set of *randomly chosen* heads, at ≥5 draws, gives the floor;
  report the selected set's restoration as a gap against that floor with a
  cluster bootstrap CI over **series** (invariant 2). §18 F6's precedent
  applies directly: a restoration gain not stated against a measured floor is
  not a result. `layer_screen_bakeoff.py`'s random-null design is the
  template — reuse its shape rather than inventing a second one.
- **Pre-registered abort:** if the selected set's restoration CI overlaps the
  random-set floor's, H8 stops here and is written up as a negative — *no*
  variant search, *no* re-tuning `tau`, and Stage 3 does not run. This is the
  §6.2.1 Stage 1c rule applied in advance, which is the only time it works.
- **Scope stated up front, not discovered later**: attention heads only.
  MLP paths need `mlp_info`, which **TimesFM does not have** (its
  feed-forward is two bare `nn.Linear`s, `CLAUDE.md` §6.2) — so an MLP result
  would be Chronos-only unless `timesfm_adapter.py` gains a hard-coded
  `mlp_info` the way `sundial_adapter.py` already did (~10 lines, tracked
  under E18's Gap 2, not here).

#### Stage 3 · E18 · Path patching, inside the found set only `[x]` — CLOSED 2026-08-23, see the Findings above (before Stage 1) for the exact numbers

Built and run against both real checkpoints. `hooks.path_patch_delta` (the
two-forward primitive) plus `seasonality_circuit.py::path_decompose_head`/
`path_patch_circuit`. TimesFM's degenerate 1-head set conserves exactly
(`conservation_gap = 0.0`, a construction check). Chronos-T5-Base's 5-head
set does **not** conserve on average (mean |gap| 0.0238 vs. mean |effect|
0.0108) — the stated acceptance bar is not met — but every causally-ordered
sub-effect the primitive's own logic requires to be exactly zero came back
exactly zero on real data, and the 4 synthetic `test_path_patch.py` unit
tests independently pin the same causal-order property off any checkpoint,
so the non-conservation is read as genuine nonlinear multi-path interaction
in Chronos's circuit, not a broken primitive. Full detail, per-head numbers,
and the three-part case for that reading are in the Findings block above.

#### Stage 4 · Report section and writeup `[x]` — CLOSED 2026-08-23, see the Findings above (before Stage 1) for what was built and the real-report numbers

- One report section (`report.py::_sec_seasonality_circuit`), rendered only

  convention: a `Finding` per claim with `evidence_class="causal_within_model"`
  (patching is within-model — invariant 5 is untouched here, and the section

**Total: ~2 sessions**, matching §20's original estimate — but now front-loaded

### H9 Analysis card export `[x]` · **DONE 2026-08-21**

A one-page, citable Markdown/PDF card per analyzed model: identity and
checkpoint digest, tier, F9's fairness rows, headline L0/calibration/cost
numbers, coverage, confirmed-vs-exploratory findings, corpus digest, library
versions, and the run's git SHA. Trivially built on E6's `findings.json` +
F9's `card.json`, and it is what someone actually attaches to a paper or a
decision memo. **Cost:** ~0.5 session.

**Findings (2026-08-21, cron loop).** Built as a pure reduction over already-
written artifacts, matching `report/meta_report.py`'s relationship to its own
inputs rather than adding a new report-stage measurement: new
`report/analysis_card.py` (`build_analysis_card(run_dir) -> dict`,
`render_analysis_card_markdown(card) -> str`) + CLI `run_analysis_card.py
--run <dir> [--out <stem>]`, writing `<stem>.md` and `<stem>.json`. Reads
`run_manifest.json` (provenance: git SHA/dirty, tsfm_lens version, packages,
corpus digest, config hash, per-model adapter/checkpoint/hf_revision),
`tiers.json`, `fairness/card.json` (F9), `l0/summary.json` (+ whether
`l0/calibration.json` exists), `budget/model_budget.json`,
`confirm/confirmation.json`, `report/coverage.json`, `report/findings.json`
— nothing is measured, no model is loaded. A missing artifact (report/
confirm/budget never run, or a tier-0 model's `unmeasurable` budget map)
renders a stated "Not available"/"not measurable" line rather than crashing,
omitting the section, or rendering a fabricated `0` (`CLAUDE.md` §2.5) —
the tier-0 case matters specifically because a silent `0` there would make
the *least*-measured model read as the *cheapest* one. 3 new tests
(`tests/test_analysis_card.py`, all synthetic fixtures, no GPU): a full run
populates every section correctly, a partial run (only `run_manifest.json`/
`tiers.json`) degrades every missing section to an explicit "Not available"
line (≥3 occurrences asserted), and a tier-0/black-box model's budget entry
renders "not measurable" rather than a fabricated zero. Live-verified against
the real `runs/smoke` mock pipeline run (not just synthetic fixtures):
`python run_analysis_card.py --run runs/smoke` produced a correct one-page
card — 2 models with real parameter/FLOP/coverage numbers, the 8-row
fairness table, L0 headline MASE/sMAPE/pinball plus strengths, confirm's
"5 of 17" replication line, findings count "47 total... 2 pre-registered...
45 exploratory," and the report-coverage summary line, all pulled correctly
from the run's real artifacts with no hand-editing needed. Test suite: 20
passed (`test_analysis_card.py` + `test_meta_report.py` +
`test_report_legibility.py` + `test_smoke.py`). **Not wired into
`pipeline.py`** — deliberately a standalone CLI over an already-completed
run's artifacts, matching `meta_report.py`/`scaling_ladder_report.py`'s
precedent, not a new pipeline stage. PDF export (the item's own "/PDF" in
its title) was not attempted — Markdown is directly citable and convertible
by any standard tool (`pandoc`), and adding a PDF renderer as a new

### H12 Deterministic-replay and result-provenance mode `[x]` · **DONE 2026-08-21** (partial scope — see Findings)

An honesty feature aimed squarely at reproducibility problems this repo has
already paid for three times (`CLAUDE.md` §11.13's golden-hash mystery,
§11.24's config-meaning drift, §11.25's stale zarr store). One flag records,
per run: every library version, the git SHA, CUDA/driver versions, the resolved
config *after* defaults, corpus digest, every RNG seed actually drawn, and a
digest of the activation store — written to `provenance.json` and rendered in
the report. Then `run.py --verify-provenance <run_dir>` re-checks the current
environment against it and reports every difference.

**Why it earns a live slot:** §11.24 cost a full investigation session that a
single "these two runs differ in these 3 ways" diff would have closed in a
minute, and that failure mode gets *more* likely as background-agent workflows
(`CLAUDE.md` §2.8) become the norm. **Cost:** ~1 session. Composes with A3's
config fingerprint and A7's provenance record (both already built) — extend
them rather than adding a parallel mechanism.

**Findings (2026-08-21, same cron loop, picked up after J4).** Built the
`--verify-provenance` half of the spec, extending A7's already-recorded
`run_provenance()` (`utils.py`) exactly as this item's own text asked, rather
than adding a parallel mechanism: `manifest.py::verify_provenance(run_dir)`
loads a run's saved `run_manifest.json["provenance"]`, reloads that run's own
frozen `config_resolved.yaml` (never the live `--config` path, which may have
moved on — the whole point is comparing against what *this run* actually saw),
recomputes today's environment via the same `run_provenance()` call, and diffs
`tsfm_lens_version` / `git_sha` / `git_dirty` / `python_version` / `packages` /
`device` / `config_hash`. Wired into the CLI as `tsfm-lens --verify-provenance
<run_dir>` (`run.py`; `--config` is now conditionally required — not needed
for this mode, since the config comes from the run directory itself). Also
added a cheap **activation-store fingerprint**: `ActivationStore.summary()`
(`extraction/store.py`) reads only zarr array *metadata* (shape/dtype per
model/layer, `n_series`/`n_windows`/`window`/`context_len`/`schema_version`)
— never the underlying activation content, so it's safe on a many-gigabyte
real store — merged into `provenance` right after extraction completes
(`extraction/extract.py`, same `record_extra` pattern already used for
`corpus_digest`). `verify_provenance` reopens the live store and compares its
current summary against the recorded one, flagging `store_summary_changed`
without hashing gigabytes of content. Live-verified end to end, not just via
pytest: built a fresh smoke run, confirmed `--verify-provenance` reports
"no differences found" against its own just-written manifest, then hand-mutated
the manifest's `git_sha`/`packages`/`store_summary.models.patchy.n_layers` and
confirmed all three differences are correctly reported (with the store one
naming `CLAUDE.md` §11.15/§11.25 directly in its message) — then confirmed a
genuinely untouched run still reports clean. 9 tests in `tests/test_provenance.py`
(4 pre-existing + 5 new): `ActivationStore.summary()`'s shape/dtype correctness
on a synthetic store, a real built run finding no diffs against itself, a
mutated-environment-field run correctly flagging exactly the mutated keys (and
*not* flagging unrelated ones — the negative that matters most for a diff
tool), a mutated-`store_summary` run flagging `store_summary_changed`, and a
run with no recorded provenance raising a specific `FileNotFoundError` rather
than a confusing `KeyError`. Full suite re-run after the `extract.py`/`store.py`
change: `test_manifest_fingerprint.py` + `test_smoke.py` + `test_nonfinite.py`
+ `test_sae_encode_store.py` (24 tests, chosen because they exercise
`extract.py`'s write path most directly) all green, no regression from the new
`store_summary` merge into every run's provenance record.

**Not built, and named as a real scope cut rather than left implicit:**
(1) **CUDA/driver versions** are already recorded by A7's existing
`run_provenance()` (`device.cuda_version`/`driver_version`) but are *not* in
`_PROVENANCE_DIFF_KEYS` — deliberately, since a driver/CUDA version
legitimately differs across the machines this repo has already run on in one
session (`CLAUDE.md` §6.2's Sundial session, the RTX 5070 vs. 8×A5000 sessions)
without indicating a reproducibility problem, and diffing it by default would
make every cross-machine verification noisy for no benefit; both values are
still visible side by side in the raw `saved`/`current` dicts the function
returns, just not auto-flagged. (2) **`hf_revision`/checkpoint drift** is
likewise computed by `run_provenance()` but excluded from the auto-diff,
because `_hf_revision()` makes a network call per invocation — imposing that
cost on every `--verify-provenance` call (a diagnostic meant to be cheap and
frequent) was judged the wrong default; a future pass could add an opt-in
`--verify-provenance --check-checkpoints` flag. (3) **"Every RNG seed actually
drawn" is not implemented at all** — the single largest scope cut. Doing this
properly means instrumenting every `np.random.default_rng`/`torch.manual_seed`
call site across generators, corruptions, bootstraps, and SAE/crosscoder
training with a shared seed-recording sink, which is invasive, cross-cutting,
and touches code this cron loop judged too high-blast-radius to change
unreviewed (`CLAUDE.md` §2.1's "what does this break three stages downstream"
question has a much larger answer here than for the rest of this item). Left
open for a future, explicitly-scoped session rather than attempted piecemeal.
The item is marked done on the strength of the environment-diff + store-
fingerprint half, which is also the half `§11.13`/`§11.24`/`§11.25` (the three
incidents this item's own motivation cites) would each actually have been
caught by — none of those three incidents involved an undocumented RNG seed.
them rather than adding a parallel mechanism.

### H6 Fine-tuning plasticity — which layers move `[x]` — un-parked and CLOSED 2026-08-21, as a negative result

**Un-park trigger fired for real.** §22.5 parked this on "§6.3.1 Option E
happening for its own reasons" — Option E's fine-tuned children
(`runs/lineage_pair_children/{child_light,child_drifted}`, two disjoint-data
fine-tunes of `amazon/chronos-t5-small`, item 12 in §0.5, done 2026-08-20)
now exist, so this ~0.5-session item was free to build and run.

**Mechanism** (`tsfm_lens/analysis/finetune_plasticity.py` +
`run_finetune_plasticity.py`, no pipeline stage — a standalone report tool in
the `run_error_fingerprint.py`/`run_agreement.py` family): per-block L2
weight-delta norm between a parent checkpoint's state dict and a fine-tuned
child's, computed by diffing two already-saved HF checkpoints directly (no
forward pass, no benchmark corpus, no GPU) — a training signal with zero
mechanistic overlap with CKA, decodability probes, or the layer-screen
bake-off's SAE-mass gold ranking, since it never runs the model at all.
Spearman-correlates each child's per-encoder-block delta against the
bake-off's `gold_score` and every selector's `score_per_layer`
(`layer_screen_bakeoff.py`'s existing `runs/layer_screen_bakeoff_v4.json`,
`CLAUDE.md` §9's re-verified, corpus-sampling-noise-fixed artifact).
Degrades to `rho: None` with a stated reason below 2 points (`CLAUDE.md`
§2.5); a genuine shape mismatch or an empty requested stack raises rather
than silently returning zero mass (`CLAUDE.md` §2.5's other half).

**Sanity check passed:** `child_drifted` (400 fine-tune steps) shows
**~4.2-4.6× larger** per-encoder-block deltas than `child_light` (50 steps)
at every one of the 6 blocks (e.g. block 0: 12.586 vs. 3.403; block 3: 12.864
vs. 3.198) and a **~4.8×** larger decoder total (154.66 vs. 31.98) — the
mechanism responds to the manipulation in the expected direction before any
interpretability comparison is trusted.

**The cross-validation itself did not materialize — reported straight, per
this repo's convention for `error_fingerprint`/`agreement`-class negative
results.** Neither child's per-block plasticity ranking significantly
matches `gold_score` or `work_bend`'s `score_per_layer` at the only sample
size available (n=6 encoder blocks — Chronos-T5-Small's full captured
surface, `CLAUDE.md` §12 item 1's encoder-only asymmetry applies here too,
so there is no decoder-side gold score to correlate against):

| vs. | child_light rho (p) | child_drifted rho (p) |
|---|---|---|
| `gold_score` | −0.486 (0.329) | −0.086 (0.872) |
| `work_bend` | **−0.771** (0.072) | −0.543 (0.266) |
| `coverage` | +0.270 (0.604) | +0.676 (0.140) |
| `factor_emergence` | +0.714 (0.111) | **+0.771** (0.072) |

Nothing clears p<0.05 at n=6 (an inherently underpowered test — 6 points
caps Spearman's exact p-value resolution at 2/6!=1/360 in principle, but the
*effect sizes* themselves are what's inconclusive here, not just the
significance test). Two things worth naming rather than averaging away:
(1) the sign is **negative** against both `gold_score` and `work_bend` (the
production selector) at both children — if anything, a very weak,
non-significant trend in the *opposite* direction from "the blocks that
moved most during fine-tuning are the blocks work_bend already flagged as
task-relevant"; (2) the strongest trend of the four, `factor_emergence`
(+0.71/+0.77), is the selector `CLAUDE.md` §11.18 already found to be an
early-layer-biased, not-production-ready selector — so even the best-looking
number here does not read as support for the *validated* selector.
**Verdict: H6 does not sharpen `work_bend`'s production status.** It also
does not contradict it — a null result at n=6 is exactly what "descriptive,
inconclusive" looks like, not evidence against `work_bend`. `work_bend`'s
own validation continues to rest on `CLAUDE.md` §6.1.1's bake-off alone, and
that section's existing "provisional single-corpus, single-checkpoint-pair"
caveat already covers this — no `CLAUDE.md` claim needs updating.

**Scope, stated rather than hidden:** one checkpoint family
(Chronos-T5-Small only — Option E did not fine-tune TimesFM/Sundial
children), one parent, 6 encoder blocks. A future fine-tune of a second
model family would let this be re-tested with real statistical power, but
building one purely to re-run this diagnostic was judged not worth a fresh
session (this item's whole premise was "for free, ask... as a by-product").

**Tests:** `tests/test_finetune_plasticity.py`, 8 new — a planted single-block
weight delta correctly attributes to exactly that block (every other block
exactly zero, not just small), a genuine shape mismatch raises, an empty
requested stack raises, `per_block`'s dict keys are plain strings (a real
bug caught before landing: the first version used `(stack, idx)` tuple keys,
which `json.dumps` rejects outright — found by actually running the JSON
`--out` path, not by reading the code, `CLAUDE.md` §2.4's own discipline),
the correlation degrades gracefully below 2 points, a planted perfectly
monotone relationship recovers rho=1.0 exactly, and an end-to-end
`plasticity_report` against two tiny in-memory-saved toy T5 checkpoints
round-trips through `json.dumps` with no bakeoff entry and with one. Full
`tsfm_lens` suite re-run after landing — see this session's log entry in
§14 for the exact count.

## 21. Two audiences — a beginner on-ramp and an advanced methods spine (added 2026-08-12)

> **The problem (§17.1 G-V).** This repo's output currently assumes its reader
> already knows what CKA is, why a stitching gain over a baseline matters, and
> what "relative depth" means. That reader exists and is well served. Two others
> are not: the practitioner who wants to know which model to use and whether to
> believe the answer, and the sceptical expert who wants each estimator's
> assumptions stated in one place before reading any result.
>
> **The design principle: one document, layered — not two documents.** Two
> documents drift (this repo has already paid for that with `CLAUDE.md` vs.
> `ROADMAP.md` staleness, corrected repeatedly in both files' headers). Layering
> means every claim has a one-sentence plain reading, a normal-depth reading,
> and a methods reading, and the reader chooses the depth.

### J1 The three-layer claim contract ✅ `[x]` — DONE 2026-08-18

Extend E6's `Finding` dataclass with three text fields instead of one:
- `plain: str` — one sentence, no jargon, no numbers beyond one. *"TimesFM
  handles trending data better than Chronos here."*
- `text: str` — the current register: effect size, CI, correction, evidence
  class. (What exists today.)
- `caveat: str` — auto-composed, not hand-written: the evidence class, whether
  registered or exploratory, whether it cleared its noise floor (F6), which
  fairness rows qualify it (F9), and coverage (F4).

The report renders `plain` at headline size, `text` beneath, and `caveat` in the
existing collapsed `<details>` mechanism. **`caveat` must be generated** —
`CLAUDE.md` invariant 8's lesson is that author discipline decays while
generated text does not. **Cost:** ~1 session, together with E6.

**Findings — 2026-08-18.** Built by a background agent (`CLAUDE.md` §2.8),
independently re-verified rather than taken on its report alone (§2.4) —
and that verification caught something real: the agent's own claimed example

- **`plain`**: all 36 call sites got a genuinely jargon-free one-sentence

omits. Source of truth: a single `stage_docs.py` dict consumed by both the
report and the docs, so they cannot drift. **Cost:** ~1 session; mostly writing,
and much of the content already exists scattered across `_note()` blocks —

assumed (§2.4), since a `[ ]` next to working code is exactly as misleading

### J3 Glossary and the worked example ✅ `[x]` — DONE 2026-08-19

- A glossary of the ~25 recurring terms (window, relative depth, evidence class,
  crystallization depth, stitching gain, fingerprint, effective dimensionality,
  noise floor, tier, coverage fraction, dead feature, …), each in one sentence
  plus a pointer to the figure where it is used. The report's per-figure
  `_note()` blocks are contextual and stay; this is the lookup table for someone
  reading out of order.
- **One worked example, end to end**: a real report, read paragraph by paragraph
  in the docs — *this* is the number, *this* is why the CI matters here, *this*
  is the caveat that changes the conclusion, *this* is the finding I would not
  act on and why. This teaches the reading skill nothing else in the repo
  teaches, and it doubles as the regression test for whether the report is
  actually legible. **Cost:** ~1 session.

**Findings — 2026-08-19.** Both halves built, in the shape J2 had already
established for its own docs so the two cannot drift apart differently.

- **Glossary: `tsfm_lens/glossary.py`, 32 terms** (J3 asked for ~25). A frozen
  `Term(term, definition, where)` dataclass; `where` names a **report section
  or artifact, never a source file**, because the reader this exists for is
  someone who arrived at one section from a deep link, not a maintainer.
  Rendered by two surfaces from the one dict, exactly like `stage_docs.py`:
  `report/report.py::_glossary_block` (collapsed under the "How to read this
  report" preamble — a lookup table is consulted, not read, and 32 open
  definitions ahead of the first number would push every result below the
  fold) and `render_glossary.py` → `README.md` with a `--check` stale gate.
- **A deliberate editorial rule, written into the module docstring** so a
  later session extends rather than dilutes it: *the limitation goes inside
  the definition* wherever the term is routinely over-read. "Relative depth"
  without "a convention, not a claim that the same fraction is the same
  computational stage" is worse than no entry, because it licenses precisely
  the misreading `CLAUDE.md` §12 item 4 already records as a real problem.
  Same for "stitching gain" (the gain, never the raw R²), "linear CKA" (both
  models seeing the same input inflates it on its own), "noise floor" (under
  ~2× is not interpretable), and "captured FLOP fraction".
- **Worked example: `tsfm_lens/docs/worked_example.md`, 308 lines**, written
  against the **real** `runs/medium_run_chronos_base` artifacts
  (TimesFM-2.5-200M vs. Chronos-T5-Base, 288 series) and quoting them, not
  illustrative values — it walks the report in its own section order,
  fairness card → L0 → cost → lens → L1 → L2 → L3 → confirm.
- **The part J3 said matters most — "the finding I would not act on" — is a
  real one from that run, not a constructed teaching example**: L0's
  `mixture` family gap is **0.010 MASE**, against Chronos-T5-Base's own
  **±0.160** repeat-run noise floor from the fairness card. Sixteen times
  under its own floor. The page says plainly that this is not a small effect
  but *no measurement at all*, and that the only reason to mention it is to
  say so. Two more of the same kind: L3's **overall** agreement (0.356)
  averages a per-corruption set running from **+0.964** (`level_shift`) to
  **−0.953** (`spike`) and describes none of its rows; and L2's direction
  with the *higher* raw R² (0.545) has the *lower* gain (0.318), so anyone
  quoting the R² is quoting mostly the benchmark.
- **The example also carries a methodological lesson this repo paid for
  once**: comparing against a null run means matching the **layer**, not the
  peak — the §16 E9 history where a peak-vs-peak comparison produced a wrong
  "indistinguishable from null" verdict for L2 is retold in place, since a
  reader with no roadmap access would otherwise repeat it.
- **11 new tests (`tests/test_worked_example.py`) make the doc a regression
  test rather than prose**, which was J3's own stated ambition for it. The
  artifact-backed ones re-derive L0's overall MASE, L1's peak CKA + null +
  both layer names, **both** L2 directions' best gains, the confirmation's
  mean/CI/family/n, and that **every** corruption present in `l3/meta.json`
  appears in the doc's breakdown table (the doc's own argument — that the
  overall number hides sign changes — only holds if the breakdown is
  complete). They `pytest.skip` when the gitignored run directory is absent,
  the pattern `test_stage0_winner_config.py` already set. Structural tests
  (report-order, "names a finding it would not act on", scope limits, no
  placeholders, every cited artifact path exists) do not skip.
- **One test was written, failed, and was replaced rather than accommodated**
  (§2.4): a "no hand-rounded 1-decimal values" precision guard fired on
  legitimate content — parameter counts (`231.3M`), percentages (`28.2 pt`),
  purity (`1.0`). A test that fails on correct content is noise, so it was
  replaced by one that checks every `**Artifact:**` path the doc hands the
  reader actually exists in the run it quotes — a citation that reads as
  verifiable and isn't is worse than no citation.
- **7 new tests for the glossary** (`tests/test_glossary.py`): README
  non-staleness (the only check that actually prevents drift), one-sentence
  definitions, all three fields populated, alphabetization for lookup rather
  than dict order, loud `KeyError` on an unknown term, and that **every**
  term reaches the rendered HTML — a "does the page contain the word
  glossary" test would miss a silently truncated table entirely.
- **Live-verified, not only unit-tested**: regenerated `runs/smoke`'s report
  through the real CLI (`--stages report --force report`) — 13 sections, 45
  findings, the glossary `<details>` present and all 32 terms in the HTML.
- **Full `tsfm_lens` suite: 491 passed, 0 failed** (up from 466).

### J4 Progressive disclosure in the report (= H10) `[x]` — done 2026-08-21

A three-position control at the top: **Headline** (fairness card, L0, confirmed
findings, recommendation) · **Standard** (today's report) · **Methods**
(everything plus per-figure estimator details, seeds, sample counts, null
comparisons). Implement as CSS classes toggled by one small inline script — no
new dependency, and the file stays self-contained (an existing hard constraint).
Default to **Standard** so no current reader's experience changes. **Cost:**
~0.5 session.

**Findings (2026-08-21, same cron loop, picked up after §0.5's queue emptied).**
Built exactly as specced, reusing two mechanisms `report.py` already had rather
than inventing new ones: J1/J7's existing `<details class="note">` (the
"What does this mean?" dropdown) and `<details class="coverage">` are what
**Methods** mode reveals — a tiny inline `<script>` (`tsfmSetDetail`) sets
`document.body.dataset.detail` and, on switching to `methods`, forces every
`<details>` element on the page open (`querySelectorAll('details').forEach(d
=> d.open = true)`) — so no per-figure content had to be re-authored, exactly
the design shortcut this item's own spec implicitly invited. **Headline** mode
is pure CSS keyed off `data-detail`: `section:not(.sec-headline){display:none}`
hides every section except the three tagged `sec-headline` in the template
(`s.eyebrow in ('Fairness', 'L0', 'Confirm')` — Confirm stands in for "the
recommendation," since no separate recommendation object exists in this repo;
`ROADMAP.md`'s own H2 practitioner-recommender item is parked, so headline mode
surfaces the closest existing thing rather than fabricating a field), and
`.findings li:not(.registered){display:none}` hides every exploratory finding,
leaving only `Finding.registered=True` ones (in practice, Confirm's own
findings — the same field J1 already populates, reused rather than duplicated).
A `.fgroup-block:not(:has(li.registered)){display:none}` rule (CSS `:has()`,
supported in every evergreen browser this Plotly-dependent report already
requires) hides a per-stage finding group header entirely when none of its
items survive the headline filter, so a reader in headline mode does not see
ten empty section headers. **Standard** is the unchanged default — the three
toggle buttons render with only "Standard" pre-marked `.active` and no
on-load script runs, so a reader who never touches the control sees exactly
today's report, byte-for-byte identical apart from the new control bar and the
(cosmetically invisible) `registered`/`exploratory` `<li>` classes.
One existing test needed updating, not because the feature broke anything but
because it had hardcoded the exact markup this item changed on purpose:
`tests/test_smoke.py`'s `findings.json`-vs-rendered-`<li>`-count check counted
bare `<li>` tags, and every finding `<li>` now always carries a
`registered`/`exploratory` class (needed for the headline CSS rule above) — so
the count read 0. Fixed to count both class variants; the assertion's actual
intent (findings.json entries == rendered `<li>` findings) is unchanged and
still holds (43/45/47 across the three configs re-run). New
`tests/test_progressive_disclosure.py` (5 tests) pins: the toggle exists and
defaults to Standard (checked structurally — only the `standard` button's
markup carries `class="active"`, no script runs on load); the headline CSS
scopes to exactly `{Fairness, L0, Confirm}` (parsed out of the template source
itself, so a future edit that quietly widens or narrows the set fails this
test rather than silently changing behavior); Methods mode's script targets
the generic `details` selector rather than new per-site markup; and, against a
freshly regenerated `runs/smoke/report.html`, that exactly `{fairness, l0,
confirm}` carry the `sec-headline` class and every findings `<li>` is tagged
one of the two classes with none left bare. Live-verified via the real CLI
(`python run.py --config configs/smoke.yaml --stages report --force report`):
regenerated report has `detail-toggle` (1), `tsfmSetDetail` defined and called
4 times, 3 `sec-headline` sections (fairness/l0/confirm), 13 `fgroup-block`
wrappers, and findings split 2 registered / 45 exploratory — matching the
pre-existing, unrelated 47-finding smoke baseline exactly. Full
`tsfm_lens` suite green after the fix (`tests/test_smoke.py` +
`tests/test_report_legibility.py` + `tests/test_progressive_disclosure.py`:
17 passed; full-suite rerun in progress at write time, see the session log for
the final count). **Not built, and stated as a real gap rather than
implied-covered**: there is no persistence (`localStorage`) of the chosen
mode across a page reload — J4's own spec asked only for a session-local
toggle, and browser-storage persistence was judged out of scope for a
~0.5-session item; a future pass could add it cheaply if a reader finds
re-selecting Headline mode on every open annoying.

### J7 The report states its own conclusion, and every figure is labelled `[x]` — done 2026-08-20

**The gap this closes.** J1 gave every *finding* three registers (`plain`,
`text`, `caveat`). Two legibility gaps survived it, both found by a user
reading a rendered report rather than by reading the code:

1. **Every figure's subject line was collapsed.** `_note(purpose, reading,
   limitations)` rendered all three fields inside one `<details>`. A reader
   scrolling thirteen sections will not open a dropdown under every figure, so
   in practice each chart was unlabeled beyond its `<h4>` — and the failure is
   invisible, because the HTML renders perfectly.
2. **The report had no answer, only evidence.** It is organized by *method*,
   which is right for an evidence document and wrong as an opening: a reader
   met the evidence ladder, then a flat wall of 40+ findings, and had to
   reconstruct the conclusion themselves.

**What was built.**
* `_note` now renders two registers: `purpose` as an always-visible `<p
  class="figcap">` caption directly under the figure, and only *how to read a
  value* and *limitations* — the two questions a reader asks **after** deciding
  a chart is relevant — inside the collapsed block, now labelled uniformly
  **"What does this mean?"**. **Every call site is unchanged** (same three
  strings, same order), so ~46 existing figures gained a visible caption with
  no per-figure editing and no risk of a caption drifting from its detail.
* The four figures that had **no explanation at all** got one: the budget
  section's *Compute completed by depth* and *Quality per unit of compute*, and
  the layer-screen profile. (The fourth, L3's verbose case studies, turned out
  to already open with a subsection-level note — a second per-figure note there
  would have been duplication, so it was reverted rather than added.)
* New **"Bottom line"** block, rendered above everything: five or six plain
  sentences composed from the run's own artifacts — who is more accurate and
  whether the advantage is family-specific, whether the two models share
  structure and whether that survives the input-feature baseline, where the
  forecast crystallizes, whether accuracy was bought with compute, how much of
  each model is observable, and how many findings survived the held-out test.
  Each line reads one artifact and **drops independently** when that stage did
  not run, so the block can never claim more coverage than the run has; with no
  artifacts at all it renders nothing rather than an empty box.
* The findings list is **grouped by stage** with a per-stage subhead and a count
  in the heading. Nothing is hidden or reordered within a stage.

**Findings (2026-08-20).** Verified through the real CLI on
`configs/smoke.yaml`, not only pytest: 13 sections / 47 findings, with
`class="figcap"` × 50, `What does this mean?` × 49 and `class="plotly-graph-div"`
× 46 — so **every figure has both registers**, and the surplus captions are
tables and subsection intros. One bug caught by inspecting rendered output
rather than the diff: the bottom line's held-out-test sentence read the wrong
key (`verdict` instead of `confirmed`) and reported **0 of 4** where the
artifact says **3 of 4** — a wrong number stated more prominently than any
other number in the report, which is exactly the risk of adding a summary
layer. A second one was caught by a test: with no artifacts at all the block
still emitted its "everything here is exploratory" line, i.e. a Bottom-line box
whose only content was a disclaimer about claims it did not contain.

7 tests (`tests/test_report_legibility.py`), including three negatives: a
`_note`'s detail must **not** repeat its caption, the bottom line must drop the
lines it has no artifact for, and it must render **empty** rather than
confident when nothing ran. One test reads the *source* to assert every
`summary=` override still starts with "What does this" — the uniform-affordance
property is the kind that decays one well-meaning edit at a time. Full suite
**629 passed** (up from 622).

**Second Findings block — the live full-feature run (2026-08-20), which found
a real gap the mock run could not.** `configs/full_report_run.yaml`, all 15
stages against `google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch` + `amazon/chronos-t5-base` on
an RTX A5000 (~41 min), then rendered with the new code: **14 sections / 48
findings**. Every headline number reproduces the recorded
`medium_run_chronos_base` values bit-for-bit — L1 peak CKA **0.3812**
(`stacked_xf.4` ↔ `encoder.block.10`) against a **0.0359** null, L2 gain
**0.4132** Chronos→TimesFM and **0.3179** the reverse, TimesFM 231,289,280
params / 59.39 GFLOPs forward / **42.55%** captured, Chronos-T5-Base
201,374,976 params / 774.76 GFLOPs forward against 5398.28 GFLOPs per forecast
/ **14.35%** captured, crystallization 0.947 vs 0.348.

**The gap:** this run has `report.verbose: true`, and verbose mode renders
**70** figures where the mock smoke run renders 48. At 53 captions against 70
figures, **17 were bare** — the 24 L3 per-series case-study panels and the
per-family exemplar panels, all of which sit under a *subsection-level* note
that a reader has scrolled past long before reaching panel 20. The
count-based assertion written the same morning (`n_caps >= n_figs`) **passed**
on the mock report and would have passed on this one too, because a handful of
sections carry captions on tables and intros and the surplus masked the
deficit. Fixed by adding `_figcap` — the visible half of `_note` alone, for
exactly the gallery case where every panel needs a *label* but the same
"how to read it" text 24 times is what teaches a reader to stop reading notes
— applied at six sites, and by rewriting the test to walk the document in
order and require a caption immediately after each figure. Both reports are
now at **zero** bare figures (70/70 and 48/48). Two grammar defects in the
Bottom line were fixed from the same rendered output ("1 of the data family
tested", "Of 15 finding(s) … 1 of 1 testable ones held up").

### J5 The advanced methods appendix `[x]` — DONE 2026-08-23

One always-rendered appendix stating, per estimator, the things a reviewer asks
for and no current document collects: the estimator and its exact form (linear
CKA, ridge with which regularization selection, banded DTW with which band), the
resampling unit and design (cluster/paired/held-out-series), what the null is
and why *that* null, the known failure modes, and the assumption that would
invalidate it. Roughly one paragraph each for CKA, RSA, ridge stitching, the
tuned lens, MASE/sMAPE/pinball, the bootstrap designs, AMI, catch22 features,
SAE fidelity, and `relative_decoder_norm`.

**This is the cheapest credibility item in the whole file** — the content is
already known to whoever wrote each module, it is currently distributed across
module docstrings, and its absence is the first thing a sceptical reader
notices. Generate it *from* the module docstrings where possible so it cannot
drift. **Cost:** ~1 session.

**Findings (2026-08-23, cron loop, picked up after a fresh queue audit found
§0.5's own 13-item queue fully closed).** Built `tsfm_lens/methods_appendix.py`
(`MethodEntry`/`build_methods_appendix()`) and wired it into `report.py` as
`_methods_appendix_block()`, rendered unconditionally after every result
section (an appendix, not a per-run claim), collapsed by default, matching
`_glossary_block()`'s own "consulted, not read" placement and CSS class.
**One correction to this item's own spec, made rather than forced:**
"catch22 features" does not belong in this appendix — `tsfm_lens` (the
model-comparison pipeline this report documents) does not use catch22 or
any other named feature extractor anywhere in its own source; catch22 is
`benchmark_validation`'s corpus-diversity metric, a different package with
its own README, not an estimator this report's reader will ever see a
number from. Forcing in a paragraph about a method the report never uses
would be exactly the kind of appendix padding a skeptical reviewer notices,
so it was left out rather than fabricated, and CKA+RSA were consolidated
into one entry (both are documented together in one module docstring, and
a reviewer reading them as two unrelated rows would be misled into
thinking they're independently computed). **8 entries, not 10:** 6 pulled
**verbatim** from the named module's own docstring at report-build time
(`l1_geometry.py` — CKA+RSA, `l2_stitching.py` — ridge stitching,
`lens.py` — skip+tuned lens, `l0_behavioral.py` — MASE/sMAPE/pinball,
`stats.py` — the bootstrap designs, `clustering.py` — AMI), so an edit to
any of those six docstrings changes the rendered appendix on the next
build with no second file to remember to update, exactly this item's own
"generate it from the module docstrings so it cannot drift" ask. The
remaining 2 (SAE fidelity/dead-feature-rate, `relative_decoder_norm`) are
hand-written per the spec's own "where possible" qualifier — their source
functions (`sae/eval.py::reconstruction_fidelity`/`dead_feature_rate`,
`sae/crosscoder.py::relative_decoder_norm`) carry only one-line docstrings,
too thin to state a resampling design or failure mode on their own — and
each cites a **real, already-measured** failure this repo found rather
than a generic warning: the SAE entry cites the 94.5–97.3% dead-dictionary
finding (`CLAUDE.md` §13) and the window-vs-token-granularity
forecast-preservation confound (+3.9 ΔMASE resolving to +0.25 under
token-level re-measurement); the `relative_decoder_norm` entry cites

### 22.0 🔬 Is TopK feature death an importance filter? — and why the best SAE recipe is model-dependent

> **First in this list by user instruction (2026-08-31), and the only entry
> here that is a research question rather than a feature.** The instruction
> was explicit about ordering: *"First I want the SAE to work, then test out
> the research question."* So this is parked **behind §25**, not beside it —
> it consumes §25's Component A as its instrument and cannot be run before
> that instrument exists. It is recorded at the top because it is the most
> interesting thing this repo could ask next, not because it is next.

**Un-park trigger:** §25.9 Stage 2 exits positive — i.e. Component A's
causal battery is built and at least one feature clears the
random-direction null on at least one channel, on at least one target. That
is the minimum condition for the question to be *askable*; before it, there
is no causal readout to grade dictionaries with, and grading them
correlationally is what §25.20(c)–(d) showed does not work.

🔔 **The trigger fired 2026-08-31 (§25.23).** Stage 2 is now built and run
against Chronos-T5-Base `encoder.block.10`: 23 of 39 candidates clear the
random-direction null on at least one channel, with 72 clearing (feature,
channel) cells against a chance-expected 17.55 — decisively past the
minimum condition stated above. **This item is un-parked, but not yet
started** — running it is a distinct piece of work from building the
instrument that makes it askable, and specifically needs Q1's per-feature-
vs-per-role comparison (dead vs. revived dictionaries, both directions) and
Q2's within-TimesFM-depth ladder, neither of which the Stage 2 verification
run above computed (it ran the battery on one dictionary at one target,
not the dead/revived pair this question needs). Recorded here rather than
silently promoted to "in progress," per this file's own discipline that a
checkbox only moves when the described work is actually done.

🔬 **Q2's within-TimesFM depth sweep specifically has now been run — see
the Findings block at the end of this section (2026-09-02).** Q1's
per-feature-vs-per-role comparison (dead vs. revived, both directions) has
**not** — this section's "un-parked, but not yet started" status still
applies to Q1 in full.

---

#### The question, in two halves

**Q1 — Does TopK-induced feature death act as a useful importance filter?**
A 96%-dead dictionary's surviving 4% are not a random 4%: they are the
directions that kept winning the TopK competition across training, i.e. the
highest-utilization ones. So death may be an implicit, free importance prior
rather than pure waste. §25.20's within-model measurement is consistent with
that for one model and not the other, and is *correlational*, so it cannot
settle it:

| | dead | revived | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| TimesFM `stacked_xf.18` — gap over null | +0.1665 (417 alive) | +0.1086 (1591 alive) | death **helps** |
| Chronos-T5-Base `encoder.block.6` — gap over null | +0.2294 (160 alive) | +0.2362 (157 alive) | death **irrelevant** |

The two live explanations make **opposite causal predictions**, which is
what makes this answerable rather than a matter of taste:
- **Death-as-filter:** the dead dictionary's survivors should have *larger*
  individual causal effects (steeper dose–response, larger null-normalized
  channel effects, cleaner necessity/sufficiency splits) than the revived
  dictionary's typical feature. Fewer, stronger knobs.
- **Feature splitting:** the revived dictionary's 1591 features carry the
  *same or more* total causal effect, divided into finer, individually
  weaker pieces. Then the right comparison is not per-feature but
  **per-dictionary** — the union of a role's member atoms — and the revived
  dictionary should win on that while losing per-atom.

**The discriminating statistic falls straight out of Component A and needs
no new primitive:** per-feature effect size (does death select stronger
knobs?) *and* per-role aggregate effect over member atoms (does splitting
preserve the total?). Death-as-filter predicts the first goes up and the
second is flat; splitting predicts the first goes down and the second is
flat or up. Both being flat is a third, boring, and perfectly publishable
outcome: revival is free, take the smaller dictionary.

**Q2 — Why is the best recipe model-dependent, and what does that mean?**
The user's second instruction, and the more consequential half. Three
measured points, one axis:

| target | `effective_dim` | dead rate under production recipe | revival's effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| TimesFM `stacked_xf.18` | **2.66** | 0.959 | **hurts** (+0.1665 → +0.1086) |
| Chronos-T5-Base `encoder.block.6` | **8.67** | 0.974 | **neutral/helps** (+0.2294 → +0.2362) |
| Chronos-2 `encoder.block.6` | **44.26** | **0.012** | **unnecessary — already alive** |

Three hypotheses, and the point of writing them down before running anything
is that they are separable:
- **H-A (intrinsic dimensionality).** Revival's benefit scales with the
  layer's `effective_dim`. At eff-dim 2.66 there are barely any real
  directions to occupy, so forcing 1591 atoms alive necessarily splits or
  duplicates; at eff-dim 44 there is genuine structure for 6000 atoms and no
  intervention is needed at all. This is the same axis §25.16(c) found
  governs the alive ceiling (`alive ∝ effective_dim^1.02`), which is why it
  is the leading candidate — one quantity would then explain both *how many*
  atoms live and *whether reviving more of them helps*.
- **H-B (over-completeness ratio).** What matters is `dict_size /
  effective_dim`, not `effective_dim` alone.
- **H-C (tokenization).** TimesFM's 32-step patch embedding and Chronos-T5's
  per-timestep quantization produce structurally different activation
  sparsity, and the recipe interacts with that rather than with any
  dimensional quantity.

🔴 **The clean experiment that separates H-A/H-B from H-C already has its
axis inside a single model, and this is the design worth keeping.**
`effective_dim` varies **12-fold within TimesFM across depth** on a fixed
corpus — 31.65 at `stacked_xf.2`, 22.02 at `.6`, 15.42 at `.10`, 6.41 at
`.16`, 2.49 at `.18` (`runs/full_report_run_large`). Running the
dead-vs-revived A/B at all five depths of **one** model holds architecture,
tokenizer, corpus, recipe and step budget fixed and varies only the quantity
under test. **H-C predicts no depth trend** (one model, one tokenizer, so
the recipe's ranking should not move); **H-A predicts a monotone one**, with
revival flipping from harmful to helpful somewhere in the middle. That is a
five-cell, cached-activation experiment against a store that already exists,
and it is decisive between the two leading explanations. Chronos-T5-Base's
own depth range then replicates or refutes it in a second architecture.

**What it means if H-A holds, and this is why the question is worth more
than the config decision it settles.** Three consequences, in increasing
order of how much they change:
1. **"Dead features are bad" becomes conditional.** Every existing mechanism
   for eliminating them — resampling, ghost grads, AuxK, BatchTopK — is
   built on the premise that death is pathology. If death is instead
   *selection* below some intrinsic-dimensionality threshold, then applying
   those mechanisms at a low-eff-dim layer is actively harmful, and the
   field's default is a default rather than a finding.
2. **SAE recipe selection becomes per-layer and predictable**, keyed on a
   quantity this pipeline already computes for free in `internals`. That
   replaces §23.2 A1's 8–40-training ladder search with a prior, and it is
   the practical payoff.
3. 🔴 **It becomes a *fairness* problem, which is this repo's home ground.**
   §18's whole doctrine is that a cross-model number must sit on an axis
   both models genuinely share, or be rendered beside the measured size of
   the asymmetry. If the optimal SAE recipe is model-dependent, then
   **comparing two models' SAEs trained with one fixed recipe systematically
   disadvantages whichever model that recipe suits less** — a new instance
   of exactly the problem F1 solved for depth and F2 for compute, in a
   subsystem where nobody has looked for it. Every cross-model SAE number in
   this repo (§16 E16's matching, §6.2.1's crosscoder scorecard, and §25's
   own Components C and E) would inherit it. This is the finding that would
   most change what the repo does next, and it is the reason Q2 is not
   subordinate to Q1.

---

#### Why this is novel — stated as a claim with its own falsifier

Documented as novel per the user's instruction, and therefore held to §2.6's
standard: **what is established, what is new, and what would retire the
claim.**

**Established, and not claimed here.** Dead/inactive latents are a
well-documented SAE pathology, and the mechanisms for eliminating them —
neuron resampling, ghost gradients, the AuxK auxiliary loss, BatchTopK — are
standard; this repo implements several (`sae/models.py`, §6.2.1 Stage 0).
**Feature splitting** — larger dictionaries decomposing one coarse feature
into several finer ones — is also established, and is Q1's null hypothesis
rather than its contribution.

**What is new, to our knowledge (as of 2026-08-31, and see the falsifier
below).**
1. **The inversion itself.** The literature treats death as waste to be
   minimized and reports it as a hygiene metric. Asking whether the *rate*
   is doing useful selection — whether the survivors are systematically the
   important atoms — inverts the premise. Every dead-feature mechanism cited
   above is evidence that the inverse question is not the default one.
2. **A causal grading criterion for dictionaries.** Dead-feature arguments
   are settled on reconstruction loss, loss-recovered, or downstream
   probing. Q1 grades two dictionaries of the same activations by the
   **measured causal effect of their features on the model's own output**,
   against a random-direction null of matched norm (§25.4). §25.20(d) is the
   evidence this matters rather than being a stylistic preference: the
   obvious correlational alternative gives a randomly-initialized network
   0.565 against the real one's 0.567 and therefore cannot grade anything.
3. **Exact generative ground truth instead of human or LLM judgment of
   max-activating examples** (§2.1). The importance of an atom can be
   checked against a known data-generating process — this is the repo's
   standing methodological edge, applied to a question the SAE field
   normally has to argue about qualitatively.
4. **Q2 has no counterpart we know of.** SAE recipes are proposed as
   universal improvements. "Which recipe wins is a function of the layer's
   intrinsic dimensionality, and is therefore a cross-model fairness
   confound" is a different kind of claim, and the within-model depth sweep
   above is a cheap way to test it that the single-model-single-layer
   convention of most SAE work does not naturally suggest.
5. **The setting.** Time-series foundation models, where the output is a
   forecast rather than a token distribution, so a feature's causal effect
   is measurable as a *shape change in the forecast* — trend, seasonal
   magnitude, dispersion — rather than as a logit shift. That is what makes
   (2) legible at all.

**Falsifier for the novelty claim itself, and it must be run before the
claim is published anywhere outside this file.** A systematic literature
check — dead/inactive latent rate as a *selection* mechanism; causal or
ablation-based comparison of dictionaries at matched activations; SAE
hyperparameter sensitivity as a function of activation intrinsic
dimensionality or participation ratio; any SAE work on time-series
foundation models. **If any of these already exists, the correct action is
to cite it and narrow the claim to whatever remains**, not to drop the
experiment: the measurement is worth making regardless, and a replication in
a new setting is a legitimate contribution. Record the search terms and the
date, so the claim carries its own provenance the way every number in this
file does.

---

#### Cost, and one confound in the existing data

**Cost:** Q1 is one extra training run per target (cached activations, no
extraction, no checkpoint reload) plus Component A over both dictionaries.
Q2's depth sweep is five cells against a store that already exists. Neither
needs new data or a new corpus. This is cheap *because* §25 will already
have built the instrument — which is exactly why it is parked behind it
rather than merged into it.

⚠️ **The `k=48` runs are not clean intermediate points and must not be used
as such.** `runs/medium_run_chronos_base_auxk` varies **both** the sparsity
budget (`k` 32→48) and `aux_k`, so its dead rates (0.778 TimesFM / 0.908
Chronos) do not sit on the same one-dimensional axis as the dead-vs-revived
pair. Chronos's gap at that point (+0.1324) is *below both endpoints*, which
looks like a non-monotonicity and is more likely just a different axis. A
real dose–response in dead rate needs `k` held fixed while only the revival
knobs move — worth designing in from the start, since it converts Q1 from a
two-point comparison into a curve.

---

#### Q2's within-TimesFM depth sweep — run 2026-09-02, findings

Run against a background agent per `CLAUDE.md` §2.8, exactly the design
above: dead-vs-revived A/B at TimesFM's `stacked_xf.2/.6/.10/.16/.18`
(`effective_dim` 31.65/22.02/15.42/6.41/2.49), holding architecture,
tokenizer, corpus and step budget fixed, reusing `runs/full_report_run_large`'s
already-extracted store with no re-extraction. The "revived" recipe is
`configs/sae_revival.yaml`'s §23.2 A1 fix (`aux_k: 64`, `min_train_steps:
720`, `aux_dead_steps_frac: 0.028`, `dict_size_policy: search` over ladder
`[128, 176, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048]`, `max_dead_rate:
0.30`, `dict_size_search_seeds: 3`, `min_fidelity: 0.5`), at `n_seeds: 1`
(exploratory, not §23.2's 5-seed acceptance protocol — read this as a
depth-trend measurement, not a formal per-depth verdict). Written to a new
`runs/sae_q2_depth_sweep/`, never touching `full_report_run_large`.

**Results (gap over null = `mean_abs_rho_matched −
permutation_null.mean_abs_rho_null_mean`):**

| layer | `effective_dim` | dict_size chosen | dead rate | alive | fidelity | gap (revived) | gap (dead, re-verified) | delta = revived − dead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stacked_xf.2` | 31.654216431131854 | 2048 | 0.0625 | 1920 | 0.9267593640754328 | 0.10038802483917628 | 0.13038344597409834 | **−0.029995421134922068** |
| `stacked_xf.6` | 22.023873519231856 | 2048 | 0.0625 | 1920 | 0.8411752566700494 | 0.06085501803242739 | 0.141223803517661 | **−0.08036878548523362** |
| `stacked_xf.10` | 15.419448090077212 | 2048 | 0.04345703125 | 1959 | 0.8245337974765432 | 0.048463687638741135 | 0.12996829484821532 | **−0.08150460720947418** |
| `stacked_xf.16` | 6.411146354072659 | 2048 | 0.0205078125 | 2006 | 0.8462353015636963 | 0.05558444776631223 | 0.18792864208078752 | **−0.1323441943144753** |
| `stacked_xf.18` | 2.4877076624885297 | 2048 | 0.306640625 | 1420 | 0.9252050299411234 | 0.08758743507418353 | 0.20207106988329016 | **−0.11448363480910663** |

The dead-side column was independently re-derived from
`runs/full_report_run_large/sae/meta.json` rather than trusted from this
section's own earlier table, and matches it exactly at all 5 depths.
`min_fidelity: 0.5` clears comfortably everywhere (0.82–0.93). The
`max_dead_rate: 0.30` gate **passes at 4 of 5 depths and fails at
`stacked_xf.18`** — its 3-seed search-time estimate at dict 2048
(0.295898) barely cleared, but the single training seed actually used drew
0.306640625, over the bar. `stacked_xf.18` is the single least stable point
in this table for that reason.

**Every one of the 5 depths chose `dict_size = 2048` — the ladder's own
maximum entry, not an interior optimum.** Dead rate was still rising with
size at the top of the ladder at all 5 depths (e.g. `.18`: 0.0000 → 0.0019
→ 0.0104 → 0.0039 → 0.0165 → 0.0306 → 0.0534 → 0.1592 → 0.2632 → 0.2959
across 128→2048), and the three shallowest layers (`.2`/`.6`/`.10`) were
nowhere near tripping the 0.30 bar even at 2048. **So this comparison holds
dictionary size fixed at the ladder's ceiling, not at an eff-dim-adapted
size** — a taller ladder is untested and could show a different pattern,
especially at the shallow end where the search never had to work to pass.

**Direction: `delta` is negative at all 5 depths — revival hurts
ground-truth alignment across TimesFM's entire measured depth range,
never flipping sign**, including at `stacked_xf.2` (eff-dim 31.65), which
is *higher* than the eff-dim (8.67) at which the cross-model Q1 table above
shows revival reading neutral/positive for Chronos-T5-Base. So sign alone
does not cleanly track `effective_dim` across models — only magnitude does,
within this one model.

**Magnitude does track `effective_dim`, with one non-monotonic pair.**
Ranking `effective_dim` ascending gives ranks `.18,.16,.10,.6,.2` =
1,2,3,4,5; ranking `delta` ascending (most harmful → least harmful) gives
`.16,.18,.10,.6,.2` = 1,2,3,4,5 — a single adjacent swap between `.16` and
`.18`. **Spearman rho = 0.9 exactly** (sum of squared rank differences = 2;
`rho = 1 − 6·2/(5·24) = 0.9`). scipy's asymptotic p (0.0374) is not trusted
at n=5, per this repo's own small-n convention (§20 H1); the **exact
permutation test over all 5! = 120 orderings** gives two-sided p = 10/120 =
**0.08333333333333333** and one-sided p (rho ≥ 0.9, H-A's own directional
prediction) = 5/120 = **0.041666666666666664**, against a p-floor at n=5 of
2/120 = 0.016666666666666666.

**Verdict: directionally consistent with H-A, not a clean confirmation, and
not a resolution of H-A vs. H-C vs. H-B.** A flat H-C world predicts rho
near 0; rho=0.9 with one-sided exact p=0.0417 (below the conventional 0.05,
well above the strict 2/120 floor) argues against pure tokenization-only
noise and for *something* tracking depth/dimensionality governing how much
revival hurts. But the one real non-monotonicity (`.16`/`.18`) lands
exactly on `stacked_xf.18` — the one depth whose revival recipe failed its
own stability gate at the final seed — so part of what rho=0.9 is fitting
may be recipe instability at a boundary case rather than eff-dim signal.
And the fact that sign never flips within TimesFM despite spanning an
eff-dim range that brackets Chronos's own neutral/helps point (8.67) means
`effective_dim` is not obviously *sufficient* on its own to predict sign,
only correlated with magnitude — H-B (the ratio `dict_size/effective_dim`)
and H-C (tokenization) are not ruled out by this result and remain live
until Chronos-T5-Base's own depth range is run as the second-architecture
replication/refutation §22.0 already calls for.

**Run mechanics.** Real-data augmentation (Monash) succeeded at every
depth with no silent fallback — `n_train_rows=19440` (15440 benchmark +
4000 real) identical across all 5 targets, `bootstrap_catalog` pooling 152
series across the same 12 domains each time. `training_budget` identical
across depths (`epochs_configured: 60`, `epochs_run: 144`,
`n_optimizer_steps: 720`, `aux_dead_steps_used: 20`). Combined wall-clock
≈2181.8s (≈36.36 min: 1986.8s main training + ~195s recovering
ground-truth alignment for 3 targets after a launcher-script gap — see
below), GPU 4 (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4`, bf16), idle before launch.

**One ad hoc-run artifact, not a recipe or code defect:** the launcher
script reused `full_report_run_large`'s activation store read-only (as
instructed, to avoid re-extraction) but never wrote a `meta.parquet` into
the new run directory — a file `ground_truth_alignment` needs and that the
`extract` pipeline stage normally produces. `run_sae`'s own `try/except`
caught this per-target as a `WARNING` rather than crashing (§2.5's
degrade-loudly-not-silently in action, though a log line is exactly the
"not loud enough" shape §11.20 already flagged), so the first 3 targets'
ground-truth alignment initially came back empty; copying in the (bit-
identical, deterministic-given-unchanged-inputs) `meta.parquet` from
`full_report_run_large` fixed the remaining 2 live, and the first 3 were
recovered post hoc by reloading their saved checkpoints and re-calling
`ground_truth_alignment` read-only, with no retraining and no recipe
change. The numbers in the table above are unaffected either way. Worth
remembering for the next ad hoc script that reuses a store outside the
full pipeline: it needs `meta.parquet` copied in alongside the store, not
just the store itself.

**Next step this leaves open, named by §22.0 itself:** run the same
depth-sweep design against Chronos-T5-Base's own depth range as the
second-architecture check.

### 22.1 Crosscoder variants beyond V2 — V3, V5, V6

**Parked:** V3 (explicit shared/private parameterization, ~150 lines + a
block-size sweep, 2–3 days), V5 (frequency-aware dictionary, V5a half a day /
V5b two days), V6 (Matryoshka / multi-resolution, 2–3 days). Full original
write-ups: `ROADMAP_ARCHIVE.md`.

**Why.** §6.2.1's pre-registered decision rule has already fired against V1,
with a bootstrap CI off zero on the *losing* side (V1 0.2787 vs V0 0.3204,
diff −0.0417, CI [−0.0693, −0.0137], p=0.002 at 46,382 rows). The rule's own
escape clause — *"if no variant beats V0, that is the result"* — is now the
reading the data supports. Each of V3/V5/V6 is an attempt to reverse a result
the repo pre-committed to accepting, at 2–3 days each, and none of the three
addresses the *specific* failure mode V1 exhibits. V2 (BatchTopK) does, which
is why V2 alone stayed in the queue.

**Un-park trigger.** V2 flips clause 2 (beats V0 on `gt_alignment_shared` with
a CI excluding zero). If a jointly-trained dictionary can be made to win at
all, the ceiling is worth chasing and V5 goes first — it is the only one of
the three with a TSFM-native rationale rather than an imported-from-NLP one,
and the benchmark labels seasonality exactly, so it is the only one this repo
is uniquely positioned to test. V3 and V6 stay parked even then unless V2's
scorecard says specifically that the split is still artifact-dominated (→ V3)
or that feature absorption is visible (→ V6).

### 22.2 Architecture breadth — G3, G4, G5, G6, G7

**Parked:** the mixing-profile abstraction for attention-free models (G3),
MoE routing as an axis (G4), state-space patching semantics (G5), black-box /
hosted models (G6), supervised baselines as controls (G7). ~8 sessions total
as sequenced in the original Wave E.

**Why.** §19's landscape table is a genuinely useful *diagnosis* — it names
the real models (TTM, Lag-Llama, SSMs, API-only services) that fall outside
the envelope instead of naming abstract categories, and it stays in §19 for
exactly that reason. But building for them is engineering against demand that
does not exist: nobody has asked this repo to analyze a mixer, and the five
integrated adapters already cover the architectures the repo's founding
research questions are about. G1 (declared-and-enforced capability tiers)
stayed in the queue because it is cheap and it makes every one of these
cheaper later; the rest is speculative platform work.

**Un-park trigger.** A specific model someone actually wants analyzed. Then
take exactly the one class it breaks, one per session, G1 first. G6
(black-box) is the cheapest and would come first on that trigger, since
tier-0 (`predict()`-only) analyses — L0, calibration, H7's shift envelope —
already work without any capture surface.

regardless, and by the time it has, the value of automating the five commands
is much lower than the value of whatever else that session could have done.
**Kept in the live queue instead:** E7b (install docs — ✅ done 2026-08-18;

**Un-park trigger.** A second person tries to run the pipeline. That is not a
figure of speech — it is the event that makes E1's value real and that will

**Why.** Each is GPU/wall-clock-bound rather than thought-bound, and none of

**Un-park trigger.** A finding whose CI is genuinely too wide to act on, or a
writeup that needs one headline number at full scale. Then run exactly that

### 22.8 Rejected outright (do not re-propose)

Kept from §20's original preamble, because a rejection with a reason is worth
more than the space it takes:

- **Bigger probe families (MLPs, transformers) on intermediate
  representations.** A stronger probe answers "is the information present"
  more *permissively*, which weakens every decodability claim. Linear probes
  are the right tool precisely because they are weak.
- **t-SNE / UMAP galleries of activation space.** `CLAUDE.md` §5's single most
  important rule already forbids quantitative use of embedding coordinates,
  and a gallery invites exactly that.
- **An LLM-written narrative summary of the report.** The report's value is
  that every sentence traces to an artifact. Generated prose breaks that and
  cannot be audited.

### 22.9 The one ordering constraint worth keeping (preserved verbatim)

From the original §22, because it is the argument that decided §22.3 and it
should survive the section that replaced it:

> Do not run Wave F before Wave A. A one-button tool that hands a stranger a
> depth-axis figure comparing 80%-of-TimesFM against 80%-of-Chronos's-encoder,
> with no coverage number and no noise floor, is worse than the current
> five-command tool — because it removes the expert who would have known not to
> believe it. That is §16's own argument about §15's P1 items, applied one level
> up: **equal grounds is a prerequisite for automation, not a refinement of
> it.**

Generalized, now that most of Wave A has landed: **legibility and equal
grounds gate automation, not the other way round.** F1's remaining call sites
(§18) and J5/J2/J6 (§21) come before anything in §22.3.
