## 24. The report as measurement, not prose (added 2026-08-24, user-directed)

> **Where this came from.** A direct user review of the report produced by
> `configs/full_report_run.yaml`: *"The conclusions were written into the html
> instead of being dynamic. The structure of the exemplars was jumbled and
> unclear and repetetive... The report itself needs to have more data driven
> content and less if any written conclusions, that way any model
> comparison/analysis can be run and it works."* Plus a standing priority:
> make the report **more comprehensive and adaptive to any TSFM model**.
>
> This section owns that work. §21 (J1–J7) made the report *legible*; this
> makes it *adaptive* — the distinction being that a legibility layer can be
> written in English about a specific pair of models, and this cannot.

### 24.1 The defect, stated as four measured findings [x] DONE 2026-08-24

Each was verified against `runs/full_report_run`'s own artifacts before any
code changed (`CLAUDE.md` §2.4), because "the conclusions feel written" is a
complaint about tone until it is a complaint about a specific line of Python:

1. **Authored verdicts with invisible thresholds.** `report.py::_bottom_line`
   chose between two English sentences on a bare `cka > 4 * null` — "far above
   what unrelated data would produce" vs "only modestly above the
   shuffled-series null" — with the `4` appearing nowhere a reader could see
   it. Six of its lines had this shape. One indexed `cfg.models[0]` and
   `cfg.models[1]` directly, so a third model changed the sentence's meaning
   without changing the sentence.
2. **Six of nine computed exemplars were discarded by the renderer.**
   `analysis/exemplars.py` selects several series per family at different
   quantiles of the MASE-gap distribution; `_sec_exemplars` had a `continue`
   that rendered only the first per family — so a reader saw only each
   family's *most atypical* case, while the section blurb and its own
   `Finding` text both described a spread. 9 selected, 3 rendered.
3. **English assertions where a measurement was already persisted.** The L3
   note asserted `level_shift` is "a permanent step change of several standard
   deviations over the back 40%" and `spike` "perturbs 3 of 512 timesteps" —
   both true of this repo's default battery, both false the moment someone
   reconfigures `l3.corruptions`, and both already measured in the same
   artifact (`l3/meta.json`'s `calibration.footprint`/`.energy`).
4. **A head slice in the L3 verbose selection.** `_verbose_case`'s
   `[:n_verbose]` sat directly beneath the enclosing function's own comment
   explaining why head slices are wrong on a task-grouped corpus (§15 A4). So
   every narrated series in every run made before this fix came from whichever
   family sorts first — all four in `runs/full_report_run` are
   `random_parametric`. **Fixed** (`sample_rows(..., strata=families)`);
   recorded as `CLAUDE.md` §11.38.

### 24.2 What was built [x] DONE 2026-08-24

**`report/derived.py`** (new, ~880 lines) — pure reductions over a finished
run's artifacts. No HTML, no model name, no architecture family, no corruption
name, no layer-naming convention, and no `cfg.models[i]` index anywhere in it,
which is the whole adaptivity contract stated as a constraint a test can check.
Six public reductions: `bottom_line_rows`, `corruption_breakdown`,
`layer_metrics`, `exemplar_summary`, `patching_case_summary`, plus the `Rule`/
`Verdict` primitives.

The load-bearing primitive is that **a verdict is derived, never authored**:

```python
@dataclass
class Verdict:
    measure: str; value: float | None; reference: float | None
    reference_label: str; rule: Rule; ...
    verdict: str = ""
    def __post_init__(self):
        self.verdict = self.rule.apply(self.value, self.reference)
```

There is no parameter a call site can write a sentence into — passing one is
overwritten. `Rule.text` is rendered in the same table row as the verdict it
produced (`value ≥ 4× reference`, `95% CI lower bound > 0`, `|difference| ≥
0.1 relative depth`), so a reader can disagree with the *arithmetic* rather
than only with the English. A missing reference is `"not comparable"` — never a
pass and never a fail, which is what makes a single-model run render honestly.

Three new report surfaces, each a rendered table of measured numbers rather
than a paragraph:

| Surface | Replaces | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Scorecard** (`_scorecard`) | `_bottom_line`'s paragraph | 14 rows on this run: measure, value, reference, printed rule, derived verdict, expandable per-model audit detail |
| **Corruption-by-corruption breakdown** (`_corruption_breakdown_block`, in the L3 section) | the hardcoded `level_shift`/`spike` prose | one row per (corruption, model) × 12 columns: input footprint %, perturbation energy, forecast change + CI, response in noise-floor units, activation peak depth/change, cross-model depth agreement ρ, best patch restoration + its layer — **ordered by measured response**, not config order |
| **Every measured layer** (`_layer_metrics_block`, one per model, in the internals section) | five figures a reader had to cross-reference by eye | the per-layer join: rel_depth, effective dim, input-CKA, probe accuracy and over-chance, screen score + whether selected, skip-lens MASE, mean L3 sensitivity, best patch restoration, best cross-model CKA partner + value — **joined by layer name, never by position** |

`_sec_exemplars` was rewritten (124→229 lines): a summary table with a
*derived* selection label (`largest disagreement in family` / `closest
agreement` / `mid-range` / `only case for this family`) and each gap expressed
in noise-floor units, then per-family headings, then one card per series
(forecast + lens as a single 1×2 subplot, a numeric table, and that series'
own attention map). `_l3_verbose_cases` was rewritten (79→143 lines) to loop
`model → series` instead of `model → corruption → series`, leading each case
with `patching_case_summary`'s numbers and faceting all corruptions into one
figure — 24 near-identical headings for 4 distinct cases became 4 headings.

**Coverage of the scorecard was then extended the same day** from the six
stages `_bottom_line` had covered (l0, l1, l2, lens, budget, confirm) to
**ten**, adding four rows whose reference the run had already measured and
was not being read: L3's pooled cross-model fingerprint agreement (rule: CI
excludes 0, with every per-corruption ρ in `detail`, since a pooled positive
number can average a strong agreement and a strong disagreement — **it does,
on this run: the pooled ρ is +0.3558 and it averages `level_shift` at +0.964
against `spike` at −0.953**, so the headline alone would read as "the models
are affected alike" when two of the nine corruptions say the opposite); L4's clustering AMI
(against AMI's own chance-corrected zero, so the reference is not a convention
chosen here); **one row per model** for the most load-bearing attention head,
against *that model's own* repeat-run noise floor (a within-model measurement,
so pooling it would invent a comparison); and one row per SAE target for
ground-truth alignment against its **label-permutation null** rather than
against zero, since each feature is matched to its best of ~30 candidate
fields and the search inflates the mean even on shuffled labels (both targets
clear their null — 0.3419 vs 0.1868 and 0.3927 vs 0.1978 — but the row's
detail carries each dictionary's **96.6% / 96.9% dead-feature rate** beside
it, because an alignment score over a mostly-dead dictionary describes very
few live features; that is §23.2 A1's condition, still present in this run
because the production `sae` stage's `aux_k` default is off).

**Findings (verified live through the real CLI on `runs/full_report_run`,
TimesFM-2.5-200M vs Chronos-T5-Base, four re-renders):** 14 sections, **50
findings** (was 48), **61 figures / 89 captions / 0 bare**, 56 tables,
**14 scorecard rows** (better, meets, clears, excludes, separated, better,
below, excludes, excludes, clears, does-not-clear, above, above, meets).
Exemplars **9 rendered across 3 families** (was 3). L3 verbose **4 headings**
(was 24).

All four rows were then re-derived **by hand from the raw artifacts, not
through `derived.py`** (§2.4), and match the rendered values exactly.

**The four added rows immediately produced a result the report had never
stated, and it is a negative one.** Chronos-T5-Base's *most* load-bearing
attention head — the top row of the head-ablation table the report already
rendered — has ΔMASE **0.1368** against that model's own repeat-run noise
floor of **0.1409**. Its single most impactful head is **below its own
sampling noise**, so `does not clear`. Nothing was wrong with the ablation
table; the ΔMASE was simply being read against an implicit zero, which is
exactly the failure `ROADMAP.md` §18 F6 exists to prevent and which the
scorecard makes unavoidable by printing the reference. TimesFM's equivalent
row `clears` — but trivially, because its floor is *exactly* zero
(deterministic forecasts), which the row's own `reference_label` says out
loud rather than letting a 2× rule imply a margin that does not exist.

Two numbers the new tables made visible that no prose had conveyed:
`level_shift` touches **40.04%** of the input at energy **2.614** (the
battery's highest) where `spike` touches **0.583%** — so the previously-
*asserted* reason its bar dominates is now the row next to the bar; and
exemplar series `8302293586e7f3c2` has a gap of 0.002 MASE = **0.017 noise
floors**, i.e. not a real difference, in a section whose purpose is showing
where the models differ.

**Tests:** `tests/test_derived_report.py` (34, all synthetic with planted
answers) + 4 rewritten/added in `tests/test_report_legibility.py` — 43 in the
two files together, all passing. **Full `tsfm_lens` suite: 816 passed, 0
failed** — reconciling exactly against the pre-fix run (802 passed + 9 failed
= 811, plus the 5 tests added for the four new scorecard rows). Note for the
next session: two background full-suite runs were **silently reaped at turn
boundaries** (truncated at 79% and 52%) while reporting `exit code 0`, because
the launching command was `pytest ... > log; tail log` and the compound's
status is `tail`'s, not `timeout`'s. A `setsid nohup` run with an explicit
`echo "pytest_exit=$?" > sentinel` is what actually completed — worth copying
for any 30-minute-plus verification run. The
load-bearing negatives: a call site cannot set a verdict; a single-model run
yields `"not comparable"` rather than crashing or fabricating a comparison;
`layer_metrics` joined against a *reordered* strided subset must leave blanks
rather than plausible values on the wrong layers; the corruption table's order
must follow the measured response even when config order and footprint order
both disagree with it; a deterministic model's floor ratio must be `None`, not
`inf` (reads as an overflow bug) and not `0` (reads as no signal).

**One regression, found by the suite and worth recording for its shape.** The
`_l3_verbose_cases` regrouping dropped the phrase `patched at` — it had lived
in the per-case `<h4>` ("TimesFM · noise · f619feb… — patched at L16, window
15"), and the rewrite moved that information into the summary table's
`patch_layer`/`patch_window` columns. `tests/test_smoke.py` asserts that
phrase, and **five other test modules reuse that same smoke helper**, so one
dropped token surfaced as **9 failed / 802 passed** across four files that
have nothing to do with the report. The fix was not to delete the assertion:
the token was pinning something real that the rewrite had genuinely lost from
the *figure* — a reader looking at a panel could no longer tell that the
plotted "patched" trace uses the batch-wide best layer×window cell rather than
that series' own best. Restored in the panel's caption, where it now also
names the distinction against the table's `own_best_layer` column, and the
test gained a second token pinning the regrouping itself. All 9 re-pass. **The
lesson is the one `CLAUDE.md` §11.6 already records about report key-drift,
one level up:** report builders are the least type-safe surface in the repo,
and a *shared* smoke helper means a single prose token can be load-bearing for
modules that never mention the report — so a report-section rewrite should
grep the test suite for the strings it is about to stop emitting, not just run
the section's own tests.

**Not done by this item:** the L3 verbose cases currently rendered still come
from the pre-fix artifact, so all four are still `random_parametric` — the
stratification fix appears only after `l3` is re-run (GPU work; a config edit
means a new `run.name` per §15 A3).

### 24.3 [x] One model, and three or more, as first-class run shapes

> **User-directed, 2026-08-24, and explicitly scoped as roadmap-only:**
> *"Do not implement this next part, write it into the roadmap only: 'Also,
> there should be an option to run analysis on just one model, which gets rid
> of all comparison metrics and only keeps the relevant analysis for the
> individual model. There should also be an option to run it for 3+ which will
> have comparison models for each in the same graph.'"* Nothing below has been
> built. The two shapes are one item because they share one seam.

**Why this is now cheap-ish and was not before.** §24.2's whole point is that
the report's conclusions are reductions over artifacts rather than sentences
about two models — `bottom_line_rows` already ranks N models, `_crystallization_row`
already carries every model in `detail`, `_accuracy_rows` already reads L0's
`overall` list of arbitrary length, and every rule already returns
`"not comparable"` rather than a verdict when there is nothing to compare
against. §18 F8 already made **L0** all-pairs with joint Holm correction. So
the remaining work is not "make the report N-model"; it is **the stage layer**.

**The single seam.** `config.py::comparison_pair()` returns `(models[0],
models[1])` and has **23 call sites**. Every cross-model stage funnels through
it, which is why a three-model run today silently analyzes the first two and
ignores the third — the reason `configs/smoke_three_model.yaml` disables every
stage but `l0`. That is the object to change, and changing it is a §2.1
decision, not a refactor: `l1/cka.npz`'s arrays are shaped
`[layers_a × layers_b]`, `l2/stitching.json`'s directions are keyed `"A->B"`,
`l3/meta.json`'s agreement is one ρ per corruption. Every one of those is a
*pair* artifact, and every already-recorded number in this file was measured
in that shape.

**Proposed design — three explicit run shapes, derived from `len(models)`,
never configured as a mode flag** (a hand-set mode is a claim checked nowhere,
`CLAUDE.md` §11.34):

- **`solo` (1 model).** `l1`, `l2`, `clustering`'s AMI, and L3's cross-model
  fingerprint agreement have no meaning and must be *dropped with a stated
  reason*, exactly as the tier gate already drops stages for a black box
  (§19 G1 — reuse that mechanism, do not invent a second one). Everything
  within-model survives unchanged: `l0` (per-family MASE, calibration),
  `budget`, `frontend`, `layer_screen`, `internals`, `lens`, `l3`'s
  sensitivity fingerprints **and** its within-model patching (invariant 5 —
  patching was never cross-model), `attention`, `sae`, `exemplars` (selected
  by absolute MASE rather than by gap), `register`/`confirm`. The honest test
  of this shape: `l3`'s patching heatmaps and `lens`'s crystallization depth
  are the two most substantive things in the report and neither needs a second
  model at all.
- **`pair` (2 models).** Today's behavior, bit-for-bit. Non-negotiable: a
  reshaped artifact that moves a recorded number is a failure of this item,
  not a consequence of it.
- **`panel` (3+ models).** All pairs, one designated **reference model** (the
  first, stated in the report, changeable), and every figure that is currently
  one curve per model in a pair becoming one curve per model on the same axes
  — which the user asked for in exactly those words, and which the depth-axis
  work (§18 F1) already made possible by putting every model on a shared,
  measured axis instead of an index.

**Concrete sub-items, in dependency order:**

1. `cfg.run_shape()` → `"solo" | "pair" | "panel"`, derived from
   `len(cfg.models)`. `comparison_pair()` stays, raises on `solo`, and is
   re-expressed as `comparison_pairs()` returning `[(a, b)]` for `pair` and
   all `C(n,2)` for `panel` — so every existing call site's two-model
   behavior is unchanged by construction.
2. **A stage-eligibility gate keyed on run shape**, reusing
   `pipeline._apply_tiers`'s machinery: `_STAGE_MIN_MODELS`, a `shapes.json`
   artifact beside `tiers.json`, and each dropped section naming *the run
   shape* as its reason. Acceptance: a solo run renders with no empty
   comparison sections and no "artifacts missing" text anywhere.
3. **Pair-keyed artifacts become pair-*indexed*.** `l1/cka.npz` gains
   `cka_window__{a}__{b}` keys with the current unsuffixed key retained for
   `pair` runs; `l2/stitching.json`'s `directions` already keys by
   `"A->B"` and needs only more entries. Every reader (`derived._cka_partners`,
   `report.py`, `meta_report.py`, `null_baseline.py`) reads the suffixed key
   and falls back to the legacy one. **Acceptance: re-running
   `configs/medium_run_chronos_base.yaml`'s report-only stage reproduces its
   recorded numbers exactly** (the §11.24 check).
4. **Multiplicity.** `panel` multiplies every corrected family by `C(n,2)`,
   and §6.6's p-floor makes a correction *unsatisfiable* once
   `m / n_boot > alpha` — already measured on the three-model L0 run, where a
   textbook-looking 4→0 demotion turned out to be arithmetic. So this item
   must raise `stats.n_boot` with model count, or refuse the run, and say
   which. The ledger (`report/multiplicity.json`) already renders the
   unsatisfiable case in red; extend it, don't duplicate it.
5. **Panel figures.** One trace per model on the shared `block`/`compute`
   depth axis for the lens, internals, L3-sensitivity and budget-coverage
   curves; a small-multiples grid (not an N×N wall) for CKA; the scorecard
   unchanged, since its rows are already N-model.
6. **Two acceptance configs**, mock-only so this is testable with no GPU:
   `configs/smoke_solo.yaml` (one mock, **nothing disabled by hand** — the
   shape gate must be what narrows the run, the same discipline
   `configs/smoke_blackbox.yaml` enforces for tiers) and
   `configs/smoke_panel.yaml` (four mocks, every stage on).

**Why it is not queued yet.** It touches 23 call sites and reshapes three
artifact families that every recorded number in this file lives in — the
largest §2.1 blast radius of anything currently unbuilt. It wants a session
that starts with the `pair`-reproduction test and stops if it fails.

---

**Findings — sub-items 1 and 2, the seam and the gate (2026-08-28, cron loop).**

Picked up per this item's own instruction that the session "starts with the
`pair`-reproduction test and stops if it fails." It does not fail: the seam
was widened without touching any of the 23 existing call sites, so a
two-model run is unchanged *by construction* rather than by verification.

**Sub-item 1 — `config.py`.** `run_shape()` returns `"solo" | "pair" |
"panel"`, derived from `len(self.models)` and raising on zero. There is no
config key to set it, which is what makes "derived, never declared"
enforceable rather than merely intended (`CLAUDE.md` §11.34's lesson; §15
A21's unknown-key rejection is what closes the loophole).
`comparison_pair()` is **unchanged** — same signature, same
`ValueError` below two models — and the new `comparison_pairs()` sits beside
it returning `[]` for solo, exactly `[comparison_pair()]` for pair, and all
C(n,2) for panel. The two are deliberately not collapsed into one function:
the caller that wants "the pairs to iterate over" and the caller that wants
"the designated pair or an error" are different callers, and merging them
would either crash every loop on a solo run or hand out a silently empty
comparison.

Pair ordering matches `l0_behavioral`'s existing all-pairs enumeration
exactly (`[(x, y) for i, x in enumerate(ms) for y in ms[i+1:]]`). That is
not cosmetic: §18 F8's seeding convention gives pair 0 its *historical*
bootstrap seeds specifically so a two-model run reproduces bit-for-bit, so
a `comparison_pairs()` that ordered pairs differently would re-seed the
pair-0 tests and move every recorded L0 p-value. Pinned by a test that
compares the two enumerations directly rather than asserting a hand-written
list.

**Sub-item 2 — `pipeline.py`.** `_STAGE_MIN_MODELS` + `_apply_shape`, built
on `_apply_tiers`'s machinery rather than as a second parallel mechanism, as
this item specified. It writes `shapes.json` beside `tiers.json` (shape,
`n_models`, model names, the designated reference model, every comparison
pair, and `dropped_stages`), and `report.py::_shape_skip_reason` renders that
reason next to the skipped section — so a solo run's missing L1 section says
*"this is a 'solo' run (1 model), and 'l1' measures a comparison BETWEEN
models"* rather than `"artifacts missing"`, which describes a rerun away and
would send a reader to rerun a stage that can never produce anything
(invariant 8).

Five stages are gated at 2: **`l1`, `l2`, `cluster`, `exemplars`,
`confirm`** — the ones whose *entire product* is a comparison (a CKA matrix,
stitching directions, cross-model AMI, selection by MASE *gap*, and
"model A beats model B on family F" hypothesis tests). The stages **absent**
from the map are absent deliberately, not by oversight, and the distinction
is the substantive design call here: `l3` keeps its within-model patching
(invariant 5 — patching was never cross-model) and loses only its
fingerprint-agreement number; `l0` keeps every per-family metric and the
whole calibration block and loses only the paired tests; `sae`'s
feature-space CKA already returns `None` and logs when it has nothing to
compare. Those are **internal degradations, not stage drops**, and they are
the remaining work — see "Still open" below.

**Tests — `tests/test_run_shape.py`, 10, all passing, no GPU and no
checkpoint.** The gate's failure mode is a *false drop*, which deletes an
analysis the run could have supported and does so with a stated-looking
reason that reads as a considered finding (`CLAUDE.md` §11.33/§11.35), so
most of them are negatives:
- **a `pair` run drops nothing** and leaves `selected` set-identical — this
  item's non-negotiable acceptance criterion, asserted directly rather than
  inferred from a green suite;
- a `panel` run drops nothing either (a panel has *more* comparisons
  available, not fewer — dropping there would be the same false refusal);
- the dropped list does **not** depend on which stages an invocation
  selected, pinning the exact bug that once silently emptied the tier gate's
  own list on a `--stages report` rerun;
- a stage disabled in config is **not** attributed to the shape gate;
- `comparison_pairs()` is empty for solo **while `comparison_pair()` still
  raises**;
- `_shape_skip_reason` returns `""` — makes no claim — when there is no
  `shapes.json`, and does not attribute an undropped stage to itself.

**Findings — sub-item 2's second half, the internal degradations (2026-08-28,
same cron loop).**

The stage gate above decides which stages *vanish* on a solo run. This is the
other half: the four stages deliberately **left out** of `_STAGE_MIN_MODELS`
because dropping them would delete within-model work, and which therefore had
to learn to lose only their cross-model half.

- **`l0_behavioral.py`** (both sites) — every per-family and per-archetype
  metric, the calibration block and the reliability accounting are
  within-model and survive untouched; only the paired strength tests are
  withheld, in the `applicable: False` shape those guards already used.
- **`l3_perturbation.py`** — iterates `cfg.models`; `l3/meta.json` gains a
  canonical `models` list while `model_a`/`model_b` stay exactly as they were
  for a pair run, and `agreement` becomes a named `applicable: False` with a
  reason rather than being computed. The sensitivity fingerprints and the
  within-model patching — invariant 5, patching was never cross-model — are
  untouched, which is the whole reason `l3` is not in the drop map.
- **`report.py`** — `_l3_models()` (canonical key, legacy fallback, `None`
  filtered so a solo artifact's `model_b: null` becomes a one-model list
  rather than crashing on `arrays["fingerprint_None"]`); the two
  agreement-specific regions of `_sec_l3` guarded so the subsection renders
  as a **named absence** instead of vanishing (a vanished subsection reads as
  a crashed stage); `_MODEL_PALETTE` replacing the two-key `model_colors`
  dict, with `_MODEL_PALETTE[:2] == [_COLORS["a"], _COLORS["b"]]` pinned by a
  test so no existing two-model figure changes color; `_sec_fairness` states
  the solo shape rather than returning an empty card.
- **`sae/feature_geometry.py`** — a solo guard ahead of `comparison_pair()`;
  it already returned `None` and logged for the analogous "no features on
  both sides" case, so this is the same path, reached earlier.

**`report/derived.py` needed no changes at all.** Its §24.2 constraint — no
model name, no architecture family, no `cfg.models[i]` index anywhere in the
module — held up under a run shape it was never written or tested against.
That is the first independent evidence the adaptivity contract does the thing
it claims rather than merely describing the code that existed when it was
written.

**Two defects found by running rather than reading**, which is the point of
`configs/smoke_solo.yaml` disabling nothing by hand:
1. `run_l3`'s **closing log line** still read `agreement["most_divergent"]`
   unconditionally, so a solo run completed every forward pass, wrote every
   artifact, and then died with a `KeyError` on a log statement. Every
   *computation* had been guarded and the one line that only *reports* had
   not — the cheap grep (`agreement[`) would have caught it and reading the
   guarded regions did not.
2. A first version of `l0`'s solo status wrote into `summary["pairwise"]`.
   `report.py` iterates that key as a list of `{"a", "b"}` entries, so a
   status dict there would have iterated its **keys** and raised on `e["a"]`
   — the report-key-drift class `CLAUDE.md` §11.6 already records. Caught
   before it ran, by checking the key's consumers rather than its producers;
   it now uses a dedicated `comparison` key, which is the precedent the
   `n_families < 2` branch had already set.

**Two existing tests broke and were fixed at the double, not at the guard.**
`tests/test_archetype_reporting.py` and `test_mase_reliability.py` each use a
`_Cfg` stub exposing `comparison_pair()` and nothing else, so the new
`cfg.run_shape()` call raised `AttributeError`. The stub returns two models,
so it *is* a pair config and now says so. Weakening the production guard to
tolerate a config that cannot answer what shape it is would have been
accommodating an incomplete double at the cost of the real check.

`configs/smoke_solo.yaml` is sub-item 6's first config: `smoke.yaml` with one
model deleted and **nothing else changed**, so the gate is what narrows the
run — the discipline `configs/smoke_blackbox.yaml` already enforces for
tiers. Its live `shapes.json` is exactly right (`dropped_stages` =
`cluster`, `confirm`, `exemplars`, `l1`, `l2`) and `tiers.json` independently
drops nothing at tier 3, confirming the two gates are independent as designed.

**Full suite: 835 passed, 0 failed**, run in two halves because a single

**A THIRD defect found by running rather than reading, and the three together
are one lesson.** `run_report`'s template call still passed
`model_a=a.name, model_b=b.name` after the `a, b` unpacking was replaced, so a
solo run completed every stage and died with a `NameError` in the final
render. With the `KeyError` on `run_l3`'s closing log line, that is **two
crashes in sites that only REPORT the pair**, plus one near-miss in a site
that only *keys* on it (`summary["pairwise"]`). Every site that *computed*
something from the pair was guarded correctly on the first pass.

> **The lesson, and it belongs beside `CLAUDE.md` §11.6.** When a variable
> that used to be unconditional becomes conditional, the dangerous sites are
> not the ones that compute with it — those are what you are thinking about
> while editing — but the ones that merely *mention* it: a log line, a
> template argument, an f-string in a title. They are invisible to a reading
> of the logic and they fail late, after the expensive work is already done
> and the artifacts are already written, which reads as "the analysis broke"
> rather than "a string interpolation broke". The cheap check is mechanical
> and takes seconds: **grep the removed variable across the module** (`agreement[`,
> `\ba\.name`, `model_b`) before running anything. Doing that after the first
> crash would have found the second and third at once.

The report header was generalized rather than patched: `models_title` plus a
`model_chips` list whose first two entries keep the `a`/`b` CSS classes, so a
two-model run's markup is unchanged and a panel run gets distinct palette
colors instead of falling through to Plotly's default cycle (which collides
with `accent`/`muted`).

**Preparatory inventory for sub-item 3 — every reader of the pair artifacts
(2026-08-28, same cron loop; read-only, no code changed).**

Sub-item 3 is the one with real §2.1 blast radius, so the readers were
enumerated by grep before any design was committed to, rather than after. The
count is larger than §24.3's own text implies and, more importantly, several
readers are **not** in the pipeline at all:

| Artifact | Read sites | Notable readers outside the pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| `l1/meta.json` | 14 | `run_crosscoder_feasibility.py`, `run_crosscoder_stage0.py` (both read `best_pair`), `report/meta_report.py`, `analysis/scaling_ladder.py` |
| `l1/cka.npz` | 3 | `analysis/null_baseline.py` (`cka_window`) |
| `l2/stitching.json` | 9 | `analysis/null_baseline.py` (2 sites), `report/meta_report.py` |

**Why that inventory changes the design rather than merely sizing it.**
`null_baseline.py` is what produced §16 E9's recorded significance tests, and
the two `run_crosscoder_*.py` scripts are what produced §6.2.1's — so
`best_pair` and `cka_window` are not merely "keys some code reads", they are
the inputs to numbers already written into this file's Findings blocks. A
reshape that renamed or re-nested either would silently invalidate recorded
results in **two** separate research threads, and neither script is exercised
by the pipeline's own tests, so nothing would have failed.

So the rule L3 already validated this session is **mandatory** here, not
merely preferable: `cka_window`, `cka_family`, `best_pair`, `model_a`,
`model_b`, `layers_a`, `layers_b` and `directions`' `"A->B"` keys all stay
exactly where they are and mean exactly what they mean; a panel run **adds**
`cka_window__{a}__{b}`-style keys beside them, and every reader tries the
suffixed key first and falls back. Sub-item 3's acceptance (the §11.24 check
— a report-only rerun of `configs/medium_run_chronos_base.yaml` reproducing
its recorded numbers exactly) is necessary but **not sufficient** on this
evidence: it exercises the report path only. It should be paired with a
re-run of `run_null_baseline_test.py` against the existing null run dirs,
since that is the reader most likely to break silently and least likely to be
noticed.

**Findings — sub-items 3, 4, 5 and 6 (2026-08-28, user-directed session).**

All four remaining sub-items are now implemented, and §24.3 is `[x]`. The
work was picked up as part of a user instruction to write
`Functionality_Summary.md` and then "go through and think through any
potential improvements and add them in if needed... if anything is unfinished
... try to design implementations in different ways, *if and only if* you
believe it is worth it" — §24.3 was the only open, non-parked item in the
whole file, and its unfinished half was a live silent-wrong-answer: because
`_apply_shape` drops nothing on a panel run, `l1`/`l2`/`cluster`/`exemplars`
silently analyzed `models[0:2]` and reported it as the run. A three-model run
therefore produced a complete-looking report about two of its models. That is
the failure mode this repo names most often (`CLAUDE.md` §2.5) and it was
worth fixing.

**Sub-item 3 — pair-indexed artifacts.** Implemented exactly along the rule
the inventory above made mandatory: **add a canonical key, leave the legacy
keys untouched, read new-then-legacy.**

- `l1_geometry.py` — `run_l1` loops `cfg.comparison_pairs()` through an
  extracted `_one_pair()`, with a `_LayerBank` memo so a panel's C(n,2) pairs
  load each model's activations **once**, not once per pair. `cka.npz` gains
  `cka_window__{a}__{b}` / `cka_family__{a}__{b}` beside an untouched
  `cka_window`/`cka_family`; `meta.json` gains `pairs` and `run_shape` beside
  an untouched `best_pair`/`model_a`/`layers_a`/... The three bootstrap seeds
  are deliberately **not** indexed by pair, so pair 0 reproduces bit-for-bit.
- `l2_stitching.py` — `directions` was already keyed `"{src}->{dst}"`, so a
  panel simply adds entries; `layers` covers every involved model; `pairs`
  records each pair's two direction keys and its `best_gain`.
- `clustering.py` — clusters every model, then computes AMI + contingency per
  pair. `_choose_layers` now returns a dict: for `auto` it walks L1's `pairs`
  with `setdefault` (falling back to the legacy flat dict), then fills any
  model absent from every peak pair with its middle layer **and logs that it
  did**, since a silently-chosen layer is a worse failure than a stated one.
- `exemplars.py` — a panel has no single "gap", so the selection key becomes
  `spread` (max − min across models). A **pair run keeps exactly the
  historical columns**: an early version added `spread` to both and would have
  changed `exemplars.json` for every two-model run, caught before it ran.
- `report/derived.py` — `exemplar_summary` accepts either key;
  `_cka_partners` iterates `l1["pairs"]`, keeps the best partner per layer
  **across pairs**, and qualifies the label as `{model}:{layer}` when more
  than one pair exists, because a bare layer name is ambiguous the moment
  three models are present.
- `report/report.py` — a shared `_all_pairs_block` renders every-pair
  overview tables for L1, L2 and clustering, and **returns `""` when there is
  fewer than one extra pair**, so a two-model report gains and loses nothing.
  `_l1_panel_block` renders a small-multiples CKA grid (not an N×N wall) on
  one **shared** `coloraxis` (cmin 0, cmax 1) — per-figure autoscaling would
  make the least similar pair look identical to the most similar, which is
  the figure's whole point.

**The full `run_null_baseline_test.py` re-run completed, and every point
estimate reproduces §16 E9's recorded values exactly** (real-vs-
`runs/null_chronos_random`, ~50 min): L1 peak CKA real **0.3812** / null
**0.1739** / diff **+0.2072** against the recorded 0.381 / 0.174 / +0.207;
L2 best gain real **0.4132** / null **0.4442** / diff **−0.0310** against the
recorded 0.413 / 0.444 / −0.031. Both verdicts are unchanged (L1 REAL EXCEEDS
NULL; L2 CI spans zero). The CIs and p-values differ in their last digits
because this re-run used the CLI default `n_boot`=500 where the recorded run
used 1000 — visible directly in the p-floor (`p=0.0020` = 1/500 here,
`p=0.001` = 1/1000 there), i.e. resampling resolution, not a moved number.
That is the strongest available evidence that the reader most likely to break
silently did not: `null_baseline.py` reads `best_pair` and `cka_window` and
found both exactly where and as they were.

**Sub-item 4 — multiplicity scaling.** New `doctor._check_multiplicity_budget`
states the arithmetic **before** the run rather than after. It deliberately
does **not** guess a family count — that is a property of the corpus, not of
the config, and a guessed one would be a claim checked nowhere (§11.34).
Instead it reports the *carrying capacity*: at this pair count and
`stats.n_boot`, how many families the Holm correction can hold before
`m/n_boot > alpha` makes it unsatisfiable. Live: `smoke.yaml` 1 pair @
n_boot 150 → 7 families; `smoke_panel.yaml` 6 pairs @ 2000 → 16;
`medium_run_chronos_base.yaml` 1 pair @ 500 → 25. It **fails** (not warns)
when the capacity is below one family, because in that state every L0
non-result in the run is arithmetic at any effect size. The value of moving
this earlier is concrete: the report already reddens the unsatisfiable case,
but learning it at the end of an extraction costs the extraction.

**Sub-item 5 — panel figures, verified rather than assumed.** A per-section
audit of `runs/smoke_panel/report.html` initially showed several sections with
zero occurrences of any model name, which looked like the reference-pair
narrowing the item was written to prevent. It was a **counting artifact**:
`screen`, `l2` and `l4` label each panel in an `<h4>` and `attention` in an
`<h3>`, so all four models are covered under headings the name-count missed —
confirmed by re-reading the heading structure rather than by trusting the
first count (§2.4). The per-model curve sections (`l0`, `cost`, `profile`,
`lens`, `l3`, `exemplars`) already carried all four via `_MODEL_PALETTE`, and
`_sec_clusters`'s hardcoded `make_subplots(cols=2)` — which **crashed** on the
third model with "The (row, col) pair sent is out of range" — is now
`cols=len(models)`. So the item's real content was one crash, one CKA grid,
three overview tables, and a fairness-card scope banner naming the models the
card does not cover.

**Sub-item 6 — `configs/smoke_panel.yaml`.** Four mocks, **nothing disabled by
hand**, so the shape gate (and nothing else) decides what runs — the
discipline `smoke_blackbox.yaml` set for tiers. `mock_encdec` is included
deliberately, so a shared `block` depth axis must place a model topping out
near 3/7 beside three fully captured ones. It ships at `n_boot: 2000` with the
unsatisfiability arithmetic recorded inline (6 pairs × 6 families = 36;
36/2000 = 0.018 < 0.05), which sub-item 4's new check now derives
independently.

same commit the firing was citing as proof the work was unfinished). The
commit was reverted in full; no code was ever touched.

**The reason it happened is the one this file's own loop instruction warns
about.** The standing instruction is "re-read `ROADMAP.md` fresh — it is the
source of truth on what's next, **not your memory of it**". The firing did
re-read the file, but only far enough to find a checkbox it believed was
wrong, then spent its verification budget explaining the discrepancy instead
of testing it. The check that settled it took nine seconds. **Grep for the
artifact of the work before disputing a checkbox that claims the work is
done** — a test file's existence and exit status is cheaper and more
reliable evidence than any prose in either document, including prose written
by the same session an hour earlier. A `[x]` that contradicts your notes is
just as likely to mean the notes are stale as it is to mean the checkbox is.

**Findings — two usability additions from the same session (2026-08-28).**

Both came out of writing `Functionality_Summary.md`, which is the first time
this repo has been described end-to-end from the position of someone who did
not build it. Two things were hard to state honestly, and both were fixable.

1. **`doctor._check_store_format`** — the preflight doctor's own module
   docstring claimed it covered `CLAUDE.md` §11.25 (a zarr **v3** store opens
   under the pinned v2 **without error** and reads back as an empty group) and
   it did not. That is the worst shape of gap: a documented check that does
   not exist reads as coverage. Now implemented, and it names §11.25 and the
   correct remediation ("delete the store and re-run `extract`", explicitly
   **not** "reinstall zarr", which is the intuitive and wrong fix). Verified
   against the real known-stale directory: `runs/real_run` **fails** with the
   exact diagnosis, while `smoke`, `medium_run_chronos_base` and `smoke_panel`
   pass. It deletes nothing — the doctor reports, the operator decides.
2. **`run.py --list-configs`** — 46 flat YAML files with no entry point was
   the single largest remaining usability cost, and grepping the directory was
   genuinely the fastest way to find the right one. The listing is **derived**
   from the files (run shape from model count, adapters, `enabled: false`
   stages, each file's own leading comment sentence), grouped solo/pair/panel.
   A `configs/README.md` was the obvious alternative and was rejected for the
   reason this file records repeatedly: a hand-maintained index is a claim
   checked nowhere, stale the first time a config is added without one. It
   parses with `yaml.safe_load` rather than `load_config` on purpose, so
   `scaling_ladder_chronos.yaml`'s deliberately-out-of-schema `ladder:` block
   is listed with a note instead of being the one config the listing cannot
   show. One bug caught by running it: splitting the header on any `.`
   truncated every roadmap-citing config to `"Phase 4 (ROADMAP"` — i.e. it was
   least legible for exactly the configs that most needed explaining. 9 tests
   (`test_config_listing.py` 5, `test_doctor.py` +4), including that each
   check is actually **wired into** `run_preflight`, since a check that exists
   but never runs is not a check.

### 24.4 [x] The report's *examples* become measurements too

`ROADMAP.md` §24 made the report's conclusions derived rather than authored
(`report/derived.py`, whose constraint is no model name and no `cfg.models[i]`
index anywhere in the module). This is the same discipline one level down,
prompted by a user instruction to produce a full three-model report with **no
hardcoded conclusions in the report generation pipeline**. Auditing for that
found the conclusions were already clean — and that the *explanatory notes*
were not.

**What was wrong.** Five rendered notes illustrated a mechanism with a fixed
architecture name written at authoring time:

- the repeat-run noise floor note — *"a model with no sampling in its forecast
  path (e.g. TimesFM, Chronos-Bolt) ... a sampling model (Chronos-T5)"*;
- L1's depth-axis note and L3's fingerprint note — *"an encoder-only model like
  Chronos-T5 legitimately caps out partway up the axis"*;
- the budget compute-by-depth note — *"an encoder-only model run through a
  sampled decoder (Chronos-T5's `num_samples` passes) tops out well short of
  1.0 here"*;
- the frontend quantization note — *"Chronos-T5's tokenizer re-quantizes ...
  a continuous patch-MLP embedding (TimesFM, Sundial, Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2)
  has no bin geometry"*.

Each is *true of this repo's usual pair* and reads, on any other run, as a
claim about a model that is not there. On a three-model panel it is worse than
noise: a reader meeting three unfamiliar checkpoints has no way to know that
the named one is an example rather than the subject.

**What replaced them.** Two helpers in `report.py` — `_name_phrase` (list →
prose) and `_axis_tops`/`_short_axis_clause` (each model's largest depth
coordinate, read from whichever depth-bearing artifact the run actually has) —
plus per-site derivations from data already in scope: the noise-floor note
splits the run's own models by measured `deterministic`, the budget note names
the curves whose own final fraction is below 0.9, the frontend note names the
models whose quantization probe returned `not_applicable`. **Where nothing is
measured, every one of them states the mechanism with no example at all**
rather than falling back to a written-in one — that is the load-bearing
behavior and it has its own test.

Live, on `configs/smoke.yaml` (all mocks reach the top of their axis): the two
depth notes render with **no** example clause, exactly as intended. On
`configs/smoke_panel.yaml` (which includes `mock_encdec`): *"…legitimately ends
short of 1.0 instead of being stretched to fill the axis, **as encdecy does in
this run**"*, and *"**encdecy** tops out well short of 1.0 here"* — the same
sentence, now naming the model that actually has the property.

**One further site, found by the test rather than by the audit.**
`analysis/lens.py`'s **module docstring** is rendered verbatim into the
report's methods appendix, and it contained *"Both models get both lenses, so
'TimesFM front-loads then compresses' versus 'Chronos accumulates'…"* — so a
mock-only report asserted a comparison between two checkpoints it had never
loaded, and a solo run said "both models". Genericized, with a line in the
docstring recording *why* it may not name an architecture (it is rendered, not
just read). Of the 25 modules whose docstrings mention an architecture, this
is the only one the report renders.

**Testing (`tests/test_derived_examples.py`, 7 tests).** The helpers are unit
tested, including the two negatives that matter — an absent artifact yields an
empty clause, and a model with unreadable depth coordinates is omitted rather
than taking the section down. The property itself is checked where conclusions
actually live: **no finding in `report/findings.json` may name an architecture
absent from the run.** Scoping it there rather than to the whole HTML is
deliberate and is the interesting part: the document also renders installed
library versions (a fact about the environment), a failure-mode gallery
(historical case studies from this repo's own record, which name the runs they
happened on precisely so they can be checked), and a methods appendix citing
prior measured results. A whole-document grep flags all three, and the only way
to make it pass is to loosen it until it catches nothing. A seventh test pins
the generated half of the methods appendix separately, since that is the
surface `lens.py` slipped through.

**Not changed, deliberately.** The mock-adapter warning still names
`timesfm`/`chronos` — those are **adapter registry** names telling a reader
what to swap in, a fact about the repo rather than a claim about the run.

### 24.5 [x] The three-model full-feature run

The acceptance run for §24.3 (panel shape) and §24.4 (derived examples) on
**real checkpoints** rather than mocks, and the deliverable for the user
instruction that motivated both: a full report with graphs and data, no
hardcoded conclusions, at three models instead of two.

**Config: `configs/full_report_run_3model.yaml`.** `full_report_run.yaml`'s
pair (TimesFM-2.5-200M, Chronos-T5-Base) plus **Chronos-2**
(`amazon/chronos-2`, encoder-only, 12 blocks, stride 1). Chronos-2 was chosen
over Sundial for one reason worth recording: Sundial's `--check-alignment`
diagonal-hit fraction is amplitude-dependent and decays by mid-depth at this
repo's default probe amplitude (`CLAUDE.md` §11.22) — a real architectural
property, but one that would put an unresolved alignment caveat on every
cross-model number in the flagship run. Chronos-2 measures a clean 1.00 at all
12 blocks. Two values are forced away from the pair config and the header says
why: `stats.n_boot: 2000` (3 models ⇒ 3 pairs ⇒ §6.6's p-floor makes 150
unsatisfiable at any effect size), and `sae.targets: []` (the pinned pair
targets cannot name a layer of a model that did not exist in that config).
Invariant 7 was checked for all three before launching: TimesFM 1.00,
Chronos-T5-Base 1.00 (self-calibrated amplitude 0.05), Chronos-2 1.00.

**One real bug, found only because the run was long.** It crashed at `sae`
after twelve stages had completed, on a `KeyError` from `store.load` for
`stacked_xf.15` — a layer `layer_screen` legitimately picked and `extract`
legitimately never captured, because §15 A1's fix gives the screen its own
stride-1 store. Full diagnosis and the substitution fix in `CLAUDE.md`
**§11.40**; 5 regression tests in `tests/test_sae_target_resolution.py`, whose
discriminating power was confirmed against a re-implementation of the pre-fix
resolution rather than assumed. This is the second defect in two sessions whose
shape is *an assumption held across a stage boundary that was true until an
upstream stage was correctly widened* (§11.32 is the same shape within one
function), and the first one that could not fail early by construction.

**Findings — what a third model actually bought (2026-08-30).** Every number
below is read off `runs/full_report_run_3model/`'s artifacts directly.

*The pair path did not move.* Both values this repo has on record for the
TimesFM ↔ Chronos-T5-Base pair reproduce **exactly** inside the three-model
run: L1 peak CKA **0.38115179538726807** at `stacked_xf.4`/`encoder.block.10`
(recorded 0.381), and L2's best gain **0.4132** Chronos-T5-Base→TimesFM /
**0.3179** TimesFM→Chronos-T5-Base (recorded 0.413 / 0.318). Clustering AMI's
legacy top-level key is **0.5384**, identical to `pairs[0]`. This is the §24.3
compatibility rule holding on real checkpoints rather than on mocks.

*L1 — the two Chronos models are far more alike than either is to TimesFM.*

| pair | peak CKA | shuffle null | at |
|---|---|---|---|
| TimesFM × Chronos-T5-Base | 0.3812 | 0.0359 | `stacked_xf.4` / `encoder.block.10` |
| TimesFM × Chronos-2 | 0.4297 | 0.0434 | `stacked_xf.4` / `encoder.block.7` |
| Chronos-T5-Base × Chronos-2 | **0.7400** | 0.1142 | `encoder.block.10` / `encoder.block.6` |

*L2 — all six directions clear their input-feature baseline, and the
asymmetry survives.* Best gain: TimesFM→Chronos-T5-Base 0.3179 / reverse
0.4132; TimesFM→Chronos-2 0.3827 / reverse 0.4800; Chronos-T5-Base→Chronos-2
0.4490 / reverse 0.4526. Reading **into** TimesFM is easier than reading out
of it for both Chronos models, and the within-family pair is the only one that
is near-symmetric — neither statement was expressible before this run.

*L4 disagrees with L1, which is the most interesting thing here.* Clustering
AMI is **TimesFM × Chronos-2 0.6057** > Chronos-T5-Base × Chronos-2 **0.5628**
> TimesFM × Chronos-T5-Base **0.5384**, all with non-overlapping-with-zero CIs.
So the pair whose representations are geometrically closest by a wide margin
(0.74 CKA) is *not* the pair that organizes the corpus most alike. Geometric
similarity and organizational similarity are separate measurements and this
run separates them — exactly the evidence-class distinction §6.1's table
asserts, now with a case where the two orderings actually disagree rather than
merely being labelled differently. Neither is "the" answer; a two-model run
cannot produce this observation at all, since with one pair every ordering is
trivially the same.

*Multiplicity.* 3 models ⇒ 3 pairs ⇒ 9 L0 family tests; at `n_boot: 2000` the
smallest attainable Holm-adjusted p is **0.0045**, comfortably under alpha
0.05. At `full_report_run.yaml`'s inherited `n_boot` the same family would
have been **unsatisfiable arithmetic** (§6.6), which is why the config forces
it and says so in its header. `run.py --list-configs`' multiplicity-budget
preflight states this before the run rather than after.

**Findings — the run completed; report and acceptance numbers (2026-08-30).**
`runs/full_report_run_3model/report.html`, 2.82 MB: **15 sections rendered, 1
skipped, 0 failed, 94 findings, 81 figures, 123 captions, 0 bare figures**
(positional walk, not a count comparison — §21 J7's own check). The one skip is
`seasonality_circuit`, a standalone study rather than a pipeline stage, and it
names that as its reason. All six evidence classes appear; every finding has a
non-empty `plain`, `text` and `caveat`; the two `confirm` findings are the only
`registered: true` ones and both **CONFIRM** on the private split (1/1 dev
family hypothesis; peak-CKA layer pair replicates at 0.37 [0.35, 0.41]).

*§24.4's property holds on a real three-model run.* The three models are named
in **32 / 31 / 30** findings respectively — the report is about three models,
not two with a bystander — and **no finding names an architecture absent from
the run** (checked against sundial, patchtst, timer, moirai, lag-llama,
chronos-bolt across `text`, `plain` and `caveat`).

*The scorecard scales with the panel.* 24 derived rows covering ten stages,
each rendering measure / value / reference / rule / verdict. The per-model rows
multiply correctly rather than pooling: three attention rows (one per model,
each against **that model's own** repeat-run floor) and eleven SAE rows (one
per target). Chronos-T5-Base's most load-bearing head reads `does not clear` at
0.235 ΔMASE against its own floor of 0.156 under a printed `value ≥ 2×
reference` rule — 1.508×, arithmetic a reader can disagree with — reproducing
the same negative `runs/full_report_run` found for that model at two models.

*The fairness card stays pair-scoped, by the decision already recorded in
§24.3, and says so.* Its panel banner names Chronos-2 as absent from the card
and points at the every-pair L1/L2/L4 tables and the Cost section where that
model's numbers do live. Widening the table would let the "Asymmetry" column be
read as describing three models when it describes two.

*Chronos-2 is the least-caveated model in the panel*, which is the opposite of
what a newly-added model usually is: captured FLOP fraction **97.5%**, against
TimesFM's 42.5% (stride-2 loss, a config choice) and Chronos-T5-Base's 14.4%
(an uncaptured decoder run 20 times, architectural). It is also the cheapest —
119.5M parameters, 8.65 GFLOPs per forward — while TimesFM wins
accuracy-per-compute at 14.496 MASE·GFLOPs against Chronos-2's 15.697.

🔴 **An unplanned controlled result for §23.2 A1's open dead-feature question.**
Chronos-2 and Chronos-T5-Base were trained with **every SAE hyperparameter
identical** — `d_in` 768, `dict_size` 6144, `k` 32, 8608 rows (4608 benchmark +
4000 real), the same epochs, `aux_k` off — and their dead-feature rates are:

| target | dead | fidelity | gt alignment `mean_abs_rho_matched` | its own permutation null |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chronos-2 `encoder.block.6` | **0.134** | 0.861 | 0.271 | 0.192 |
| Chronos-2 `encoder.block.8` | **0.108** | 0.883 | 0.252 | 0.196 |
| Chronos-2 `encoder.block.10` | **0.110** | 0.897 | 0.243 | 0.198 |
| Chronos-T5-Base `encoder.block.4` | 0.973 | 0.845 | 0.370 | 0.188 |
| Chronos-T5-Base `encoder.block.8` | 0.961 | 0.843 | 0.379 | 0.194 |
| Chronos-T5-Base `encoder.block.10` | 0.951 | 0.829 | 0.372 | 0.185 |
| TimesFM (5 targets, dict 10240) | 0.901–0.972 | 0.639–0.856 | 0.325–0.397 | 0.183–0.193 |

So the ~95%-dead condition this repo has recorded for **every** SAE it has ever
trained is **not a property of the training recipe** — a third architecture
reaches ~11% dead at the identical recipe, with no AuxK, and *higher*
reconstruction fidelity than either. The only variable is whose activations are
being fit. This is a controlled comparison, not a confound: Chronos-2 and
Chronos-T5-Base share the dictionary size exactly.

**Do not read "alive" as "better", which is the tempting and unsupported
inference.** Chronos-2's dictionaries align to ground truth **less** well
(0.243–0.271) than the near-dead ones (0.325–0.379), and sit far closer to
their own label-permutation nulls — margins of +0.045 to +0.079 against
TimesFM's +0.14 to +0.21 and Chronos-T5-Base's +0.18. On this evidence a live
dictionary bought reconstruction, not interpretability. §23.2 A1's question is
**reframed, not answered**: the recipe is not the whole cause, and the
next test is which property of an activation geometry predicts the dead rate —
one run, one corpus, one `k`, and three architectures is not enough to say.

### 24.6 [x] The report reads like a report — user review, 2026-08-30

**The complaint, in the user's words**, on reading
`runs/full_report_run_3model/report.html`: conclusions are "repetitive and too
descriptive"; one SAE sentence "appears 3 times (which there should only be one
SAE feature per interpretable feature in my understanding)"; the L3 horizon
sentence "should be an easy to read list of corruptions that do vs. don't have
different heads"; the scorecard "is only for 2 of the three models, and even has
a description saying so", when "it is unknown which of the models the user wants
to compare"; and every reference to the internal planning documents should go,
since "the user will not see either and will not know of it at all."

Each was checked against the artifacts before being treated as a presentation
problem (§2.4), and each turned out to be a mechanism:

**(1) Repetition was structural, and larger than the report showed.** The SAE
section emitted one finding per *(model, layer)* — 11 on this run, three of them
naming the same `tier_realism_stress` field for the same model at three separate
layers. L3's horizon block emitted one per *(model, corruption)* — 12. Both are
now one finding per **model**, over a table: SAE renders a
`model × layer × best-matched field × ρ` table and states how many distinct
labelled properties that model's dictionaries track; L3 renders a
`corruption × model` table whose cells read `differs (0.20 → 0.75)` or
`same depth (0.42)`, with the per-model heatmaps moved into one collapsed block.
94 findings → 77.

Counting the *remaining* repetition then corrected the diagnosis: masking model
names and numbers showed **19 of 44 claim templates repeating**, not one — the
first count said one because the number mask ran before the name mask and turned
`Chronos-2` into `Chronos-N`, so a digit-bearing model name never matched its own
siblings (§11.34's shape: the plausible ordering was wrong, and it failed
silently by *under*-reporting). Almost all 19 are one-claim-per-model, which is
structurally right — each is a separate measurement — and reads as the same
sentence three times. So look-alikes are now collapsed **at render time**
(`report.py::_cluster_lookalikes`): the first renders as it always did, the rest
move into a collapsed *"N more of the same kind"* block. Nothing is summarized,
so nothing can be summarized wrongly, and the rule applies to every future
per-model family without another edit.

**(2) The fairness card is now one card per pair.** It rendered pair 0 and said
so in a banner naming the models it omitted — which is honest but answers the
wrong question, since the report cannot know which two models a reader wants to
compare. `_fairness_rows_for_pair(cfg, run_dir, a, b)` is split out and looped
over `cfg.comparison_pairs()`; each pair renders as its own expandable card
(first open). `fairness/card.json` gains a `pairs` key and keeps
`model_a`/`model_b`/`rows` describing pair 0 exactly as before — the §11.39
artifact rule, so no existing reader moves.

**(3) Scorecard rows no longer scale with how many layers a stage was pointed
at.** SAE contributed 11 of 24 rows; a stage's weight on the scorecard was
tracking configuration, not evidence. SAE is now one row per model — that model's
**weakest** layer against that layer's own permutation null, all layers in the
detail — and the two cross-model rows that silently reported pair 0 (peak CKA,
clustering AMI) now report the **weakest pair** of all C(n,2), each pair in the
detail. Weakest rather than best because the claim these rows make is "this held",
and it held only if it held everywhere it was checked. 24 rows → 16.

**(4) Internal citations are stripped at the render boundary**, not edited out of
the ~76 strings that carry them (`report/sanitize.py`). Editing literals would fix
this report and regress on the next note written in house style, and it could not
reach the methods appendix at all, which renders analysis modules' `__doc__`
verbatim. The stripper keeps the *actionable* half of a citation
(`(<doc> §18 F1 -- enable the l3 stage)` → `(enable the l3 stage)`), works clause
by clause inside a parenthetical so a citation listed beside real content does not
take the content with it, and leaves the `sec-*` HTML anchors the report's own deep
links depend on untouched. Live: **153 doc names, 150 bare `sec N`, 34 `§N` → 0**,
15 anchors intact, and zero orphaned punctuation in the raw HTML.

Two defects it found in itself, both fixed and both pinned by a test: a forward
scan to the sentence's period is correct for `See <ref> …` and destroys the claim
in `before <ref>'s Stage 0 gate was measured …` (now `before the Stage 0 gate
was measured …`); and matching a doc name separately from the section it
introduces let the scan stop at the `.` inside `6.2.1`, leaving `.2.1's` behind.

Four in-prose internal labels the stripper cannot fix without mangling the
sentence were edited at the source instead (`Idea A/B/C` → the method names they
refer to, `invariant 7` → what it says), and `stage_docs.py`/`glossary.py`'s
sixteen "the two models"/"both models" phrasings were generalized — those two
modules render for **every** run shape, so a solo or four-model run was reading a
description of a two-model one.

**Verification.** 17 new sanitizer tests, 3 new clustering tests, and the
"grouping loses nothing" assertion restated for the new shape rather than
relaxed. Every load-bearing negative was confirmed to discriminate by planting
the regression: removing the possessive branch fails exactly one test; making the
section pattern's digit optional fails exactly the anchor test and the
seconds test.

## 24.7 Report review round 2 — a silent no-op found, all-pairs completed, replication widened (2026-08-30)

User review of `runs/full_report_run_3model/report.html`. As in §24 and §24.6,
each complaint was first grounded in an artifact before being treated as
presentation — and this round the sharpest one was a **real bug that had been
rendering as a finding**.

**Findings**

(1) 🔴 **Chronos-2's skip lens was measuring nothing, and it looked like a
result.** Its `skip_mase` is byte-identical at all 12 layers (1.564247…),
`skip_agreement` is exactly 0.0 everywhere, and `crystallization_depth` is
0.0 at all 64 horizon steps. Diagnosed by instrumenting the patch hook rather
than reading code: the hook fires, writes a genuinely different tensor
(`post_delta` 4.1875), `_rebuild` preserves it — and the forecast moves by
**exactly 0.0**. Cause is `chronos/chronos2/model.py:731`,
`forecast_embeds = hidden_states[:, -num_output_patches:]` — the head reads
only the trailing forecast placeholders, while `token_slice` writes the
leading context patches. Patching the *whole* live sequence instead moves the
forecast by 0.904/0.852/0.675/0.598 at blocks 0/3/6/9 and by exactly 0.0 at
block 11 — patching a layer into itself, which is the correctness check the
context-only patch never passed.
Fix is a declared capability, not a change to shared patching:
`ModelAdapter.forecast_reads_patched_positions()` (default True, since a model
that continues its context necessarily reads it), False on Chronos-2 with the
measured evidence in its docstring. `analysis/lens.py` withholds the skip lens
for such a model and says so; **the tuned lens is unaffected and still runs**,
since it is a ridge probe over stored states and patches nothing. This also
means L3 patching and SAE forecast-preservation were no-ops for Chronos-2 —
the same `token_slice` is used by both.

(2) **TimesFM's 13 crystallization-by-horizon gaps are a capture-stride
artifact, and the first explanation tried was wrong.** The initial hypothesis
(gap steps have unusually *low* final MASE, so a narrow tolerance band) was
refuted by measurement: gap steps average 2.036 vs 1.856 elsewhere, i.e.
*higher*. The real cause is that `argmin` over layers is index 9 — the last
captured layer — at every gap step. At `capture_layer_stride: 2` TimesFM's
deepest captured block is `stacked_xf.18`, not its true final `.19`, and its
skip agreement there is still 0.499, so the curve stops short of final MASE.
Chronos-T5-Base captures at stride 1, its last captured layer *is* its final
block (agreement exactly 0.0), and it has **zero** gaps — the control that
confirms the diagnosis. The report now names the count, the deepest captured
layer, and its residual agreement per model.

(3) **Mixture-family "clean vs truth" divergence is forecast error, not data
corruption — the user's hypothesis was refuted.** `contexts` and `targets` are
contiguous slices of one array; nothing cleans, smooths or despikes the truth.
Mixture is **100% `mase_reliable`** (0 degenerate denominators, vs 5% and 3.2%
unreliable in the other two families) and its scale-independent
`mae_over_mad` is 1.055, *higher* than parametric (0.852) or random_parametric
(0.973) — so its MASE is not deflated. The confusion was a trace name: "clean"
meant *forecast from clean input*, which reads as *cleaned data*. Renamed to
"forecast from clean input" / "forecast from corrupted input" / "true
continuation" / "forecast after patching", with a caption stating that the
truth-vs-clean gap is ordinary forecast error the experiment neither creates
nor removes.

(4) **The legend filter only worked on the first panel.** `showlegend=k == 0`
gives each trace a distinct legend identity per subplot, so a click hid one
panel's line. Fixed with `legendgroup`.

(5) **`noise` and `spike` were the two weakest corruptions in the battery**,
at measured perturbation energies 0.199 and 0.167 against `level_shift`'s
2.853 — weak enough to read as "does nothing" when what was measured was a
very small perturbation. Swept on this repo's own corpus over 200 series
before choosing: `noise` `snr_db` 6.0 → 0.0 (energy 0.199 → 0.794) and `spike`
`count`/`scale` 3/6.0 → 8/10.0 (energy 0.167 → 1.229, footprint 0.58% →
1.54%). Both now sit in the battery's normal range without reaching
`level_shift`'s outlier. `l3.calibrate` remains the way to equalize exactly;
these are what an uncalibrated run gets.

(6) **L3's cross-model fingerprint agreement measured one unnamed pair.**
`l3/meta.json` gains a canonical `pairwise` list (every C(n,2) pair) while
`agreement` stays byte-identical, per §11.39's rule. The report renders grouped
bars, one bar per named pair, and emits one finding per pair.

(7) **The "Stitching gain, every pair" table was 12 cells empty by
construction** — one column per *named* direction unions across pairs, so each
row was blank in the four columns belonging to the other pairs. Replaced with
role columns (`A → B`, `B → A`) that always refer to that row's own two
models. The 12 was measured, not estimated; an earlier draft of this entry
said 8 and was wrong.

(8) **Figure density**: the restoration curve (27 lines) is now a
per-corruption small-multiples grid with a shared scale and one legend
controlling every panel; per-window heatmaps wrap to 3 columns instead of one
9-wide row; the per-model lens horizon heatmaps are one side-by-side row.

(9) **Confirmation was vague and mostly untested — 2 of 19 registered claims.**
The 17 others each carried a `not_replicable_reason`, but the report printed
one boilerplate sentence per claim (six identical rows for L2, nine for L3),
which buried *which stages* are uncovered under *how many claims each raised*.
Now grouped by reason with the individual claims in a `<details>`. More
substantively, **L3 replication is now implemented** — the user's observation
that it is "the same thing just over different data" is correct: the same
corruptions at the same strengths, the same relative-activation-delta
fingerprint, the same `align_on_axis` matching and the same paired cluster
bootstrap, with the clean pass simply run rather than read from the extraction
store (the one dev-only dependency). Registered L3 hypotheses move from
`replicable: False` to `True`, taking coverage from **2/19 to 11/19**, and a
dev ρ counts as replicated when it falls inside the private CI — the same rule
the CKA replication already used. The tested-hypothesis table now states in
words which families held up, which did not, and which could not be tested.
L2 and clustering replication remain unimplemented, still with stated reasons.

(10) 🔴 **`--force confirm`, the remediation the guard's own error message
names, did not work.** `confirm` refuses to overwrite an existing
`confirmation.json` because the private benchmark is spent by looking at it
(§6.7) — correct, and the invariant is unchanged. But `force` was purely a
`pipeline.py` concept: it bypasses a stage's *skip predicate*, and
`run_confirm` never received it. So `--force confirm` bypassed the skip, ran
the stage, and hit the same unconditional `raise` — the only way to re-run a
confirmation was to delete the artifact by hand, which is exactly the
undocumented, unlogged path the guard exists to prevent. Found by running
`configs/smoke.yaml --force all` end to end, not by reading: `--force all`
does not cover it either.
Fixed by threading the flag to where the guard lives — `Context.forced`
(filled by `run_pipeline`, since `Context` is already handed to every stage),
read by the `confirm` `Stage` lambda, `run_confirm(..., forced: bool = False)`
defaulting False so every other caller keeps the guard. A forced re-run now
proceeds, warns once at WARNING that it is a **second look**, and — the part
that matters after the log scrolls away — records `repeated_look: true` in
`confirmation.json`. `report.py::_sec_confirm` renders that as a red
qualifier stating the verdicts are not a one-shot confirmation; a genuine
first run carries no such banner, since a banner that always renders trains a
reader to ignore it. 6 tests (`tests/test_confirm_force.py`), the load-bearing
one asserting the *pipeline* passes the flag — a test that only checked
`run_confirm(forced=True)` would pass while the CLI stayed broken, which is
precisely the state this fixes. Confirmed to discriminate by planting
`ctx.forced = set()`.

(11) **The confirm section reported three replications and never said what
held up.** Accuracy claims, per-corruption depth agreement and the peak-CKA
pair each render in their own block with their own table — the right
granularity for auditing one claim, the wrong one for the question the section
exists to answer. A reader had to assemble the picture from three places, and
so could not see that on `runs/smoke` the behavioral and causal claims
replicate at 3/4 and 7/9 while the geometric one replicates outright — a
substantive difference in what the run supports.
New `report/derived.py::replication_summary`, a pure reduction over
`confirmation.json` rendered as a **"What held up (N of M)"** table at the top
of the section, one row per *kind* of replication with its evidence class, its
held/did-not counts, and what a failure of that row would mean. Untestable
claims are a third column, never folded into either — counting them as
failures would misstate what the private split could check. Per-row
degradation as everywhere else: a replication that did not run leaves no row
rather than a row of zeros. Model-agnostic by the same contract
`bottom_line_rows` holds to (a test asserts no model name, architecture or
positional index appears in it). Live on `runs/smoke`: **11 of 14**. 4 tests,
one confirmed to discriminate by planting the untestable-as-failure
simplification.

(12) 🔴 **`--stages report` skipped the stale-artifact guard by skipping the
stage** (sec 15 A3's one uncovered path). The check considered only stages in
the **selection**: `if stage.name not in selected: continue`. `report`
declares `deps=[]` deliberately — it must render whatever artifacts exist,
which is what makes partial runs useful — so a stale upstream stage it *reads*
was invisible to a dependency-based check. Found by running it: after editing
this session's corruption strengths, `--stages report` on
`configs/full_report_run_3model.yaml` rendered **15 sections / 75 findings with
no warning**, mixing fresh lens artifacts with L3 artifacts computed under the
previous config. That is precisely the "looks complete, isn't" failure A3
exists to prevent, on the one path that avoided the guard entirely — and it is
also the single most common invocation anyone makes.
Fixed by widening the scope: when `report` is selected, every stage with
artifacts on disk is fingerprint-checked, not only the selected ones. The
remediation text was wrong too and was fixed with it — it said `--force <name>`,
which does nothing for a stage outside the selection, so a reader would force
the stage, watch nothing re-run, and hit the identical error; it now names
`--stages` as well. 3 tests appended to `tests/test_manifest_fingerprint.py`
against the real end-to-end pipeline, including the negative that an *unchanged*
config must still allow a cheap report-only re-render — a guard that refused
every such rerun would be worse than the bug. Both positives confirmed to
discriminate by restoring the `not in selected` line.

**Two process notes from this session, recorded because both cost real time.**
A background pipeline run was reaped mid-stage with no traceback and no exit
line; `nohup` avoids it. And the run *after* it died on `CUDA OOM` naming a PID
holding 12 GiB — which I had already concluded was dead, because
`pgrep -f <pattern> | tail -1` had picked a different matching process. It was
alive and 4 of 6 corruptions into its work. **A `ps` that returns nothing for a
PID you selected by pattern is evidence about your pattern, not about the
process** (sec 11.41's lesson, one level over: validate the probe before
believing the reading). L3 writes its artifacts only at the end, so the kill
lost that stage's work but left the previous artifacts uncorrupted.

(13) **Re-running a dev stage after registration invalidates the registry, and
the stage list has to say so.** Re-running `l3` with the new corruption
strengths and then `confirm` in the same invocation failed at the A15
freshness guard: `hypotheses.json` was registered against the *previous*
`l3/meta.json`, whose hash had just changed. The guard is correct and the
message is actionable (it names the artifact, both hashes, and `--force
register`) — what was wrong was the invocation, `--stages l3,confirm,report`,
which recomputes an artifact the registry pins without re-pinning it.
`--stages l3,register,confirm,report` is the correct form, and it is worth
stating plainly because the dependency graph does not enforce it: `register`
declares no dependency on `l3` (it reads whatever dev artifacts exist, the
same design reason `report` declares `deps=[]`), so nothing auto-inserts it.
Note this is the *third* mechanism in this session whose scope is "the stages
you selected" rather than "the artifacts you touched" — see findings (10) and
(12), and finding (14), which found a fourth by grepping for the pattern
instead of waiting to trip it. The common shape is worth carrying: **in a pipeline where stages are
individually selectable, any guard or dependency expressed over the selection
is silently narrower than one expressed over the artifacts on disk.**

**Result of the corruption-strength change, measured.** Re-running `l3` with
`noise: {snr_db: 0.0}` and `spike: {count: 8, scale: 10.0}` moves the two
corruptions the user identified as doing nothing from the bottom of the
battery into its middle. Recorded in `l3/meta.json`'s own `calibration` block,
so the report's corruption-breakdown table reads them off the artifact rather
than from prose: `noise` energy **0.183 → 0.728**, `spike` **0.153 → 1.134**
with footprint **0.58% → 1.55%** of timesteps, against `level_shift`'s
unchanged 2.614. An independent re-measurement over 200 series of the same
corpus (outside the pipeline, no GPU) gives 0.790 / 1.230 / 1.55% — agreeing
to sampling noise, which is the check that the config edit is what moved the
numbers rather than something else in the stage.

(14) 🔴 **Three separate guards named a flag that does not work alone — so the
class got a test, not three fixes.** `--force` bypasses a **selected** stage's
skip predicate. Three error messages told the reader to rerun with `--force
<stage>` for a stage that would not be in the selection: `confirm`'s
consumable guard (finding 10), the stale-artifact refusal (finding 12), the
A15 registry-freshness guard (finding 13), plus a fourth found by grepping for
the pattern rather than waiting to trip it — `extraction/store.py`'s
schema-version mismatch. Following any of them literally re-runs nothing and
returns the identical error. Each was *correct behavior behind an unreachable
remedy*, which is worse than a plain refusal: the message persuades the reader
the supported path exists, so they work around it instead (for `confirm` that
means deleting the artifact by hand, the one path the guard exists to prevent).
New `tests/test_remediation_messages.py` scans the package for user-facing
messages naming `--force` and requires each to also name `--stages` (or to say
outright that force alone is insufficient), with an explicit exemption list for
the two sites where the stage is selected by construction — so an exemption is
a deliberate act with a stated reason rather than a silent pass. It groups
**statements, not lines**: the first version judged wrapped continuation lines
in isolation and reported the fixes themselves as defects, and it carries a
third test asserting the scan finds at least three messages, since an
over-narrow scan would otherwise pass by finding nothing. Confirmed to
discriminate by reverting one fix.

(15) **"The clean input looks very different than the actual input" — the
plumbing is correct; the reporting was not.** A user read an L3 case-study
panel whose *forecast from clean input* was a near-flat line against a *true
continuation* that spiked, and reasonably read it as a pipeline design flaw:
if the clean series being fed to the model is not the series being plotted as
truth, every MASE in the repo is measured against the wrong thing. Checked
before being believed or dismissed (sec 2.4). It is not that. Keyed by the
recorded `series_ids`, the stored target matches the corpus target **exactly**
(`np.allclose` True) for both plotted series, so context and target are the
same series throughout.

What the panel actually showed is one series, `646d435a1d6c41a7` (mixture):
context sd **0.443**, future spiking to **11.31 / 7.19 / 3.24** — an excursion
of **25.5x the context standard deviation**. Its *timing* is not recoverable
from the context by any model, so a near-flat forecast is the correct response
and the large MASE is a ceiling, not a failure. Corpus-wide this is rare and
its aggregate effect is small: **4 of 288 series (1.39%)** have a future
excursion beyond 3 context-sd (mixture 5.00%, random_parametric 0.53%,
parametric 0.00%); they score **1.80x** worse individually (mean MASE 3.669 vs
2.042) and are 1.4% of series but 2.5% of total MASE mass, moving the corpus
mean from 2.042 to **2.065**. So the conclusions are not at risk.

The real gap is narrower and worth fixing on its own terms, and it is two
things. First, `mase_reliable`/`min_scale_frac` guards a degenerate
**denominator** (a series too flat for a naive forecast to err on) and
structurally cannot catch the opposite case, an unforecastable **numerator** —
nothing in the repo measured that. Second, the verbose case-study picker
samples family-stratified (correctly, since finding sec 11.38) but with no
regard for forecastability, so it can put a pathological series in 1 of 2
narrated panels where it reads as representative. New
`analysis/l3_perturbation.py::future_excursion` measures it per series — the
largest excursion of the target **beyond the interval the context actually
visited**, in context standard deviations, clipped at 0 — persisted per case in
`l3/patching.json` and rendered by `report.py::_excursion_clause` **only above
3 sd**, saying what the excursion is rather than excusing the error.
