## 31. Layer-screen spacing removed, SAE dictionary admission gate, and a units bug in the feature×channel heatmap (added 2026-09-11, user-directed)

> **The instruction.** *"why does there need to be a gap between important
> layers if the metric already measures cross layer change in residual
> stream? please change that."* Then, on the SAE section: some dictionaries
> have low reconstruction fidelity and/or high ΔMASE, which undermines
> conclusions drawn from them — *"Logically, there should be a reasonable
> threshold of reconstruction(i.e. 0.85 or 0.9)"*, it *"shouldn't change the
> MASE too much either, but some layers have high reconstruction fidelity but
> increase the MASE an abnormal amount which seems like somewhat of a
> contradiction"*, Sundial *"has very bad reconstruction fidelity, and thus
> might be thrown out of the SAE section entirely"*, *"I wonder if it would be
> a good idea to try training other layers from the same model to replace the
> thrown out ones, and if those still don't work just move on?"*, and *"I
> would also like to have the reconstruction fidelity and change in MASE on
> held out data for each layer ... overlaying train and test reconstruction
> fidelity on the same bar."*

### 31.1 The spacing rule was wrong for this scorer, and the numbers say so

`select_work_bend` scores `change[l] = 1 - cka[l, l+1]` — a **cross-layer**
quantity — then applied `min_gap = max(1, len(layers) // (2 * budget))`,
discarding any high scorer adjacent to an already-selected layer. The user's
objection is correct on the mechanism: two adjacent high scores are two
distinct transformations of the residual stream, not one transformation
counted twice, so the R3 spacing argument (which applies to selectors scoring
a *state* at a layer) does not transfer.

**Measured on the committed selections before changing anything.** The old
rule was reproduced exactly for all four models first, then the change was
applied and diffed:

| model | old selection | new (pure top-k) |
|---|---|---|
| TimesFM | `[2, 6, 9, 15, 18]` | **`[9, 10, 15, 18, 19]`** |
| Chronos-2 | `[6, 8, 10]` | **`[8, 10, 11]`** |
| Sundial | unchanged | unchanged |
| Chronos-Bolt | unchanged | unchanged |

The clearest single case: TimesFM layer 19 scores **1.767** and was rejected
for adjacency to layer 18, while layers 2 and 6 — scoring **−0.182** and
**−0.211**, i.e. *below* the mean — were admitted in its place. Two of the
five layers every TimesFM SAE number in this repo was measured at were
selected because they were far apart, not because they were interesting.

`min_gap` survives as a config field defaulting to **1** (pure top-k) rather
than being deleted, so the old behaviour stays expressible and the artifact
records which rule produced a selection: `selection.json` now always carries
`min_gap`, including on the `_uniform_fallback` and `coverage` paths where it
is `setdefault`-ed, so an artifact cannot be silently ambiguous about it.

⚠️ **Sundial and Chronos-Bolt being unchanged is load-bearing** — it means
§31.2's layer-substitution work is not made moot by this change. The model
whose dictionaries fail hardest is the one whose layer choice did not move.

### 31.2 The dictionary admission gate — and the "contradiction" is a confound, not a defect

Each of the user's three SAE complaints was checked against
`runs/full_report_run_4model/sae/meta.json` before being treated as tone
(§2.4). All three are grounded, and the third is the interesting one:

1. **Sundial's fidelity is genuinely the run's worst** — 0.793 / 0.830 / 0.804,
   the only model with every target below 0.85.
2. **0.85 vs 0.90 is a real decision, not a rounding choice.** At 0.85, three
   of thirteen targets fail; at 0.90, **six of thirteen** do. 0.85 is the
   default for that reason, as a config field rather than a constant.
3. 🔴 **"High reconstruction fidelity but an abnormal MASE increase" is the
   window/token granularity confound, not a contradiction.** Chronos-Bolt
   `block.4` has the run's **best** fidelity (0.955) with a window ΔMASE of
   **+0.378** and a token ΔMASE of **−0.135**. For a model whose token width
   equals `alignment.window` (TimesFM) the two numbers are bit-identical; for
   a finer-tokenizing model the window number carries a broadcast loss that is
   a property of the tokenizer and independent of dictionary quality
   (`CLAUDE.md` §13's own correction chain). **So the gate reads the TOKEN
   number.** A gate on the window number would have thrown out the single best
   dictionary in the run.

`admission_verdict` records three bars — fidelity (on the held-out split where
one exists), |ΔMASE| at token granularity, and the dead-rate gate — each as
`{check, split, value, threshold, rule, passed}`, following `derived.Verdict`'s
discipline that a reader must be able to disagree with the arithmetic rather
than only with the verdict. `passed` has **three** states: `False` if any bar
failed, `None` if any bar is unmeasured, `True` only when all clear (§11.37 —
an absent measurement must not yield a confident answer in either direction).
A real failure outranks an unmeasured bar, so a known-bad dictionary cannot be
reported as merely undecidable.

**Layer substitution.** On `passed is False` under `sae.targets: auto`, the
screen's next-best **captured** layer is appended to the target list
(`_next_substitute_layer`, ordered by `_screen_ranked_captured`, never by
position) for up to `sae.layer_substitution_attempts` tries, then the target is
abandoned with a stated reason — the user's *"if those still don't work just
move on"*. Exercised end to end on mock adapters: the gate fired, substitution
ran, and it terminated when captured layers were exhausted rather than looping.

### 31.3 Held-out split — series, never windows

`split_series` partitions **series** family-stratified (§11.38 / §15 A4), and
`_rows_for_series` maps to `load_all_windows`' series-major rows. The unit
matters more than usual here: every window of one series is a slice of one
signal, so a window-level split puts near-duplicates of the training rows into
the "held-out" set and returns a fidelity indistinguishable from the training
one — i.e. it silently *disables* the check it appears to perform.
`holdout_frac: 0` reproduces the pre-2026-09-11 all-train behaviour bit for
bit, and a corpus too small to hold out 2 series says so rather than holding
out one.

The report gains `reconstruction fidelity (held out)`, `ΔMASE (token, held
out)` and `admission` columns, and the health figure's fidelity panel overlays
held-out on the **same row** as train — bar for train, diamond for held-out,
segment between them coloured as a warning past 0.05 — so the generalization
gap is a horizontal distance rather than a subtraction the reader performs.
All three columns are **dropped entirely** on a run predating the split rather
than rendered as blanks, since an empty column reads as "measured and came back
empty" (§11.37 again).

⚠️ **No SAE number has been re-measured under any of this.** The four new
`SAEConfig` fields are genuine stage inputs, so they move the `sae` stage
fingerprint (`2442f8d6c4d31bc2` → `306119f4ff8cf3c9` on
`full_report_run_4model`) and §15 A3 correctly refuses a report-only re-render
of every existing SAE run as stale. That refusal is the gate working: the
recorded artifacts were produced with no held-out split and no admission gate,
so the new columns genuinely do not exist for them. A re-run against real
checkpoints is what produces them, and it re-decides every recorded SAE number
(§2.1) — not started, and not to be started without an explicit decision.

### 31.4 🔴 The feature×channel heatmap rendered raw units while five surfaces said null-normalized

The user's complaint was *"don't leave a bunch of blank space like in feature x
channel response graph (get rid of empty rows)"*. The blankness was **not**
padding and not unmeasured cells — it was a units bug.

`report/sae_roles.py::feature_channel_matrix` appended
`max(candidates_signed, key=abs)` and never divided by `null_p95`, while its
own docstring, the colorbar title (`"signed effect<br>(null units)"`), the
hovertemplate (`"effect %{z:.2f}x null p95"`), the figure caption and the
note's limitations line all asserted null-normalization. `sae/roles.py:112`
has always divided by `null_p95` for the *same quantity* — two surfaces built
from one measurement disagreeing about its units, the §11.54 shape.

The nine channels are not commensurable raw. Measured across
`runs/full_report_run_4model`, median |value| among cells that cleared:

| channel | raw | null units |
|---|---|---|
| trend | 0.000559 | 1.037 |
| seasonal | 0.718163 | 0.987 |
| spectral_centroid | 0.367311 | 0.709 |
| level | 0.070275 | 1.497 |
| dispersion | 0.012746 | 1.023 |
| horizon_shape_near | 0.094998 | 1.778 |
| horizon_shape_far | 0.091310 | 1.847 |
| mase | 0.094675 | 1.032 |
| flatness | 0.022321 | 0.645 |

Raw, the columns span **1285×** and one shared RdBu scale is pinned by the
largest; in null units they span **2.9×**. Consequence, measured before and
after by executing both computations over the same artifacts:

| model | cells within 5% of white | rows with no visible cell |
|---|---|---|
| Chronos-2 | 70.8% → **2.2%** | 5/37 → **0/37** |
| Chronos-Bolt | 67.5% → **2.0%** | 3/32 → **0/32** |
| Sundial | 77.5% → **11.2%** | 13/55 → **2/55** |
| TimesFM | 39.4% → **4.0%** | 1/86 → **0/86** |

**Those rows were never empty.** `model_feature_channel_matrix` admits a row
only when `clears[i].any()`, so every drawn row cleared its null somewhere; a
`trend` effect of 0.000438 against that channel's own p95 of **0.000118** is
3.7× its null and was rendered white. Fixed by dividing by `null_p95` — read
from each candidate's **own** channel record rather than passed in, so a caller
structurally cannot pair one target's effects with another target's null —
which makes the five existing labels true rather than editing them to match the
defect. Verified from **rendered Plotly z-arrays**, not the diff (§11.48).

The **2 remaining** faint Sundial rows are §11.54's second site, not a residual
of this bug: a cell qualifies on its **unsigned** effect while the colour shows
its **signed** mean, so a feature moving a channel hard in both directions on
different series clears its null with a signed mean near zero. Stated in the
figure's note rather than hidden.

**Two dead imports found in the same function.** `feature_channel_matrix` and
`roles_summary_table` were imported by `_sae_roles_block` and never called —
the 2026-09-09 per-model consolidation replaced both and left the imports
behind, which is how a column maintained on the per-target table ("also moves
(× null p95)", `sae_roles.py:110`) could look wired to the report while
reaching no reader. Removed from the import; the functions stay exported and
unit-tested.

### 31.5 Tests, and three that proved nothing on first write

`tests/test_sae_channel_null_units.py` (7) and `tests/test_sae_holdout_gate.py`
(24), plus one new layer-screen test. Every load-bearing assertion was
confirmed to discriminate by planting its regression and observing the failure
— seven plants in total (raw units, train-split fidelity, unmeasured-as-pass,
position-based substitution, transposed row layout, never-dropped columns,
overlay on a separate row).

🔴 **Three fixtures were inert on first write and would have recorded a working
mechanism where none was tested** (§11.53's postscript):

1. **The family-stratification test passed with `strata=` deleted.** An
   unstratified draw of 20 from a 90/10 split happens to return exactly 2 rare
   at seed 0. Rewritten to assert proportional representation at **every** seed
   in a range — the property only stratification has; one seed's correct answer
   is a coin that landed the right way up.
2. **The substitution-ranking fixture could not tell score-ranking from "the
   last captured layer."** Its interleaved scores made the two rules agree at
   every step. Rewritten so the screen's score *descends* as store order
   *ascends*, verified by executing both rules over the fixture.
3. **The existing `test_sae_roles_report.py` fixtures carried no `null_p95`**,
   so after the fix they exercised an all-NaN path (4 new "Mean of empty slice"
   warnings) and stopped discriminating. Given per-channel nulls differing by
   ~2400×, deliberately not one shared value — a fixture with uniform nulls
   cannot distinguish a normalized matrix from a raw one scaled by a constant.

### 32.1 Complaint 1, grounded: the narrator was never ported from roles to concepts

**0 of 30 concepts in the run have a description.** Every `description` field in
`runs/full_report_run_4model/sae/concepts.json` is `null` and every
`description_generated` is `false`. This is not a generation failure — it is a
wiring gap. `run_sae_describe.py::build_evidence` builds evidence for
`kind="feature"` and `kind="role"` only, and reads
`run_dir / "sae" / "roles_injection.json"` (line 164) — the **archived**
injection-space artifact §30 superseded. So the narrator describes the artifact
the report no longer renders, and the artifact the report *does* render has
nowhere for a description to come from. `sae/concepts.py::concept_table` leaves
`description`/`description_generated` at `None`/`False` and says so in its own
docstring, correctly, because §30.7 was deliberately written design-only.

The card render loop (`report/sae_concepts.py:267–288`) is already prepared for
a description and degrades to nothing when absent:

```python
desc_html = ""
if row.description:
    gen_tag = " <i>(generated)</i>" if row.description_generated else ""
    desc_html = (f"<p class='blurb'><i>{html.escape(str(row.description))}</i>"
                 f"{gen_tag}</p>")
```

so on every run to date the card renders the statistics and **nothing else** —
which is exactly the user's report. The statistics are also rendered *first* and
the (absent) description *last*, so even once populated the card would lead with
the numbers the complaint is about.

Two further defects were found in the same pass and are separable work items:

**The names are a second statistic wearing the first one's clothes.**
`compose_name`'s mechanism 1 picks a concept's leading channel by **contrastive
z-score across all 30 peers** (`_rank_candidates(i, cleared, z)`), and then
`render()` prefixes a **magnitude tier** read off that same channel's own value
(`_magnitude_tier(float(profiles[i, chans[0]]))`, against
`_TIER_CUTS = (("dominant", 5.0), ("strong", 2.0), ("mild", 1.0))`). Those are
two different questions — *what is unusual about this concept among its peers*
and *how large is this concept's effect* — joined into one phrase with nothing
stating the relationship. §11.54 exactly.

The worked case, `Chronos-2/encoder.block.8` concept 2, named **"strong raises
flatness"**:

| channel | signed null units | z across 30 peers |
|---|---|---|
| horizon_shape_far | **+25.378** | +2.289 |
| level | −21.908 | −2.818 |
| dispersion | −21.369 | −3.585 |
| mase | −19.275 | −1.533 |
| trend | −17.380 | −2.089 |
| spectral_centroid | −8.773 | −1.736 |
| horizon_shape_near | +3.789 | −0.172 |
| **flatness** | **+2.000** | **+3.596** |

`flatness` leads because its z is the largest; the tier word "strong" is then
read off its value of 2.000 (≥ 2.0). The concept's actual dominant effect is
`horizon_shape_far` at **25.4×** its own null — 12.7× larger than the channel
the name mentions. A reader takes "strong raises flatness" as a magnitude claim.
It is a distinctiveness claim with a magnitude word attached.

Population-wide: **18 of 30 concept names never mention their own
`dominant_channel`** — 10 of those with `name_lead_diversified: true` (mechanism
2 moved the lead to avoid a collision) and **8 with it `false`**, i.e. the
z-vs-magnitude split above, not diversification. And **`"mild raises
horizon_shape_near · raises horizon_shape_far"` is used for 5 different
concepts** (26 distinct names of 30).

**The clustering produces singletons, and the quality metric rewards them.**
`sae/roles.py::_resolve_role_k` — which `cluster_concepts` delegates to —
resolves `k = int(np.clip(max(2, n_candidates // 6), 2, 8))`. Every target has
10–23 causal candidates, so `k` is **2 or 3 at all 13 targets**, and k-means on
a response space with one dominant direction splits them as one large cluster
plus a remainder:

| target | k | n_causal | silhouette | concept sizes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chronos-2/encoder.block.10 | 2 | 15 | 0.559 | 14, **1** |
| Chronos-2/encoder.block.6 | 3 | 23 | 0.392 | 19, 3, **1** |
| Chronos-2/encoder.block.8 | 3 | 23 | 0.329 | 18, 4, **1** |
| Chronos-Bolt/encoder.block.3 | 2 | 12 | 0.313 | 9, 3 |
| Chronos-Bolt/encoder.block.4 | 2 | 14 | 0.453 | 12, 2 |
| Sundial/model.layers.10 | 3 | 18 | 0.284 | 14, 3, **1** |
| Sundial/model.layers.3 | 3 | 22 | 0.121 | 11, 10, **1** |
| Sundial/model.layers.7 | 2 | 13 | **0.636** | 12, **1** |
| TimesFM/stacked_xf.10 | 2 | 12 | 0.435 | 8, 4 |
| TimesFM/stacked_xf.16 | 2 | 10 | **0.717** | 9, **1** |
| TimesFM/stacked_xf.18 | 2 | 12 | **0.674** | 11, **1** |
| TimesFM/stacked_xf.2 | 2 | 11 | 0.334 | 9, 2 |
| TimesFM/stacked_xf.6 | 2 | 16 | **0.607** | 15, **1** |

**9 of 30 concepts are singletons; 14 of 30 have ≤3 members.** The user's "only
a couple features per group" is arithmetic.

🔴 **And the metric that is supposed to catch this rewards it instead.** The
four highest silhouettes in the run — 0.717, 0.674, 0.636, 0.607 — are **all**
targets whose second cluster is a single point. A singleton has no
within-cluster distance, so its silhouette contribution is the maximum
attainable by construction; splitting one outlier off inflates the score that
gates `non_modular`. Every one of those four targets passes the 0.1
`min_silhouette` floor comfortably while describing a partition that is, in
substance, "everything, and one other thing."

describable, and removing it would change `descriptions.json`'s shape for every
existing run. Add a third branch, do not replace the second.

**A2. Add `kind="concept"`.** `Evidence.kind` is a free string, but `describe.py`
special-cases `"role"` in several places. Before writing code, run
`grep -n '"role"' tsfm_lens/sae/describe.py` and handle **every** hit — the
known ones are `_subject` (which chooses the subject noun and the plural flag),
`machine_fallback`, and `render_evidence`. A concept is a cluster of features,
exactly as a role is, so in every one of these a concept behaves as a role does:
plural, `n_atoms` members. Prefer extending the existing membership test to
`ev.kind in ("role", "concept")` over adding a parallel branch.

**A3. Build the channel dict with the §11.54 magnitude test applied.** Write
`_concept_channels(concept: dict, null_p95: dict) -> tuple[dict, frozenset]`
mirroring the existing `_role_channels` (line 261). Read
`concept["centroid_null_units"]` — it is **already in null units**, so do not
divide again. A channel enters `Evidence.channels` only when
`abs(value) >= 1.0`. This is not optional: `concepts.json` has no `clears_null`
field at concept level, and `n_members_clearing` is *"how many members cleared
this channel"* — a different question from *"does the concept's mean clear it"*,
which is precisely the pair §11.54 records as unreconcilable when rendered
adjacent. Derive `clears_null=bool(channels)` from the channels you built, never
from a field.

Channels that moved but whose direction the evidence does not support go into
`Evidence.undirected_channels`, using the same rule the role path already
applies.

**A4. Structural correlate for a cluster.** A concept has no `structural_field`
of its own. Aggregate over its members, reading the `separated` block of
`sae/meta.json` exactly as the feature path does:

- take each member feature's residualized best match;
- **drop any field `sae/ground_truth.py` refused as inseparable from provenance**
  (`fields_not_separable_from_provenance`, §11.48) — a `generator_*` correlate
  is corpus bookkeeping;
- `structural_field` = the modal surviving field among members;
- `structural_rho` = the **mean** rho over members sharing that field;
- `structural_n` = how many members share it.

When fewer than 2 members share a field, leave all three `None`. A modal field
of 1 is not a cluster property, and the narrator will state it as one.

**A5. `exemplar_profile` for a cluster.** Pool the member features' top-firing
series, then compute the same `(field, mean_over_firing_series, corpus_median)`

pass did not run — that keeps every packet built before this field existed

the role path already learned when `_role_descriptions` had to key on

writing the guard, enumerate what a concept description must not say:

- it must not name a channel outside `Evidence.channels`;
- it must not assign a direction to a channel in `undirected_channels`;
- it must not compare the concept to another concept, another model, or another
  target — no counterpart exists in the packet (§11.53 lesson 4: a guard scoped

### 32.4 Item C — one phrase, one statistic ✅ DONE (2026-09-13)

**File:** `tsfm_lens/sae/concepts.py`, `_compose_batch` / `compose_name`.

The defect is §32.1's table: the lead channel is chosen by z-score and the tier
word is read off that channel's magnitude. Fix so that a name cannot assert a
magnitude it does not have. Three candidate designs; **(c) is recommended**:

- **(a) Lead by magnitude, use z only to break ties.** Simplest; loses
  mechanism 1's whole point (names would collide more, which mechanisms 2 and 3
  then have to repair).
- **(b) Keep the z-lead, drop the tier word from it.** Render "unusually raises
  flatness" rather than "strong raises flatness". Honest, but the reader still
  never learns the concept's dominant effect.
- **(c) ✅ Recommended: the dominant channel leads, the distinctive channel
  follows.** First clause is always
  `{tier(dominant)} {verb(dominant)} {dominant_channel}`; the z-selected channel
  becomes a second clause introduced by a word that marks it as a contrast
  (`"· unusually {verb} {channel}"`), and is **omitted** when it is the same
  channel. Mechanisms 2 and 3 (diversification and shortest-unique-prefix) then
  operate on the contrast clause, which is where the distinctiveness signal
  belongs. `name_lead_diversified` stays meaningful and now describes only the
  contrast clause.

Under (c), `Chronos-2/encoder.block.8` concept 2 renders
`"dominant raises horizon_shape_far · unusually raises flatness"` — true on
both halves.

- Distinct names ≥ 26 of 30 — the current value, so diversification must not
  regress. The proven-optimal ceiling computed in §30's Stage 2 update is 26,

### 32.5 Item D — clustering that does not produce singletons, and a quality metric that does not reward them ✅ DONE (2026-09-12, correction 2026-09-13)

**Files:** `tsfm_lens/sae/concepts.py::cluster_concepts`, `tsfm_lens/config.py`.

**D1. Sweep k instead of deriving it from a ratio.** Replace the single
`k = clip(max(2, n//6), 2, 8)` with a sweep over `k in range(2, k_max+1)` where
`k_max = min(8, n // concept_min_members)`, scoring each partition by
silhouette.

**D2. Reject partitions with a cluster below `concept_min_members`** (new
`SAEConfig` field, **default 3**). This is the fix for the metric-rewards-the-
degenerate-split finding: a singleton's silhouette contribution is maximal by
construction, so the constraint has to be applied *before* the score is
compared, not after. Pick the best-silhouette **admissible** partition.

**D3. When no k is admissible, that is a result.** Set `non_modular: True` with
`reason` naming the sweep (`"no k in 2..{k_max} partitions {n} candidates into
clusters of at least {min} members"`). Do not fall back to an inadmissible
partition — §25.13 item 2's pre-registered outcome is that a dictionary which
does not partition cleanly must say so rather than have a partition forced on
it.

**D4. Record the sweep in the artifact.** Per target, add
`k_sweep: [{k, silhouette, admissible, min_cluster_size}, ...]` and
`k_selection_rule`. Without it a future reader cannot tell a k chosen by sweep
from a k chosen by the old ratio, which is §31.1's own `min_gap` lesson.

**D5. Reproducibility.** `concept_min_members: 1` plus the old ratio must
reproduce today's 30 concepts **bit for bit**, and a test must pin that. This is
what keeps every recorded concept number regenerable (§2.1).

**Acceptance:** 0 singleton concepts across the run, or the target is declared
`non_modular` with a stated reason. Expect the concept count to **fall** — this
is correct, not a regression: 9 of today's 30 are singletons and 5 targets'
entire second cluster is one point.

⚠️ **This changes every concept in the run**, and concepts are the input to
Items A, B and C. It is also a `SAEConfig` change, so it moves the `sae` stage
fingerprint and §15 A3 will correctly refuse a report-only re-render of every
existing run as stale (exactly as §31.3 records). **Do Item D last**, or accept
re-running A and C after it.

last" is superseded and kept per append-only doctrine.

- **D1/D2/D3/D4.** `tsfm_lens/sae/concepts.py::_sweep_k` sweeps `k in
  range(2, k_upper+1)` with `k_upper = min(8, n // min_members, n - 1)`, scores
  each k by silhouette on `StandardScaler`-transformed data, computes
  `min_cluster_size` **before** comparing silhouette, and picks the
  best-silhouette **admissible** k (`admissible = min_cluster_size >=
  min_members`). When no k in the swept range is admissible, returns
  `non_modular: True` with `reason` naming the sweep bounds and the floor —
  never a fallback to an inadmissible partition. Every attempted k (admissible
  or not) is recorded in `k_sweep: [{k, silhouette, admissible,
  min_cluster_size}, ...]` alongside `k_selection_rule`, both persisted on the
  target record by `run_concepts`. New `SAEConfig.concept_min_members: int =
  3`.
- **D5.** `concept_min_members <= 1` (or an explicit non-`"auto"` `k`) bypasses
  the sweep entirely and delegates to the pre-D `cluster_roles`/
  `_resolve_role_k` ratio path, guaranteeing bit-for-bit reproduction by
  construction rather than by coincidence. Confirmed against real data, not
  only the synthetic pin: re-running `min_members=1` over all 13 targets'
  `sae/*/*_ablation.json` in `runs/full_report_run_4model` reproduces the
  exact `k` and feature-id partition then on record for every target, **0
  mismatches**.

  - **NEW (default `min_members=3`), 13 targets: 4 concepts, 0 singletons,

### 32.6 Complaint 2, grounded — and the obvious fix is refuted ✅ DONE (E, F, G — G's resolution sub-fix measured and deliberately deferred; see below) 2026-09-13

The user named two panels. Both are real, and the effect is genuinely sub-pixel:

| panel | max\|with − without\| | full-panel y-range | drawn height at 132×30 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0becfd6ab2958396` · Chronos-2 feat 3327 · act 1.03 | 0.1592 | 107.102 | **0.04 px of 26** |
| `62946fb79a8606b9` · Chronos-2 feat 3440 · act 0.31 | 0.0371 | 3.558 | **0.27 px of 26** |

Three mechanisms compound:

**(a) The shared y-scale is set by the context.** `sparkline_svg`
(`report/sae_features.py:93`) concatenates context, target, `clean` and
`patched` into one `lo/hi`:

```python
stack = [y] + [np.asarray(a, dtype=np.float64) for a in (clean, patched) if a is not None]
allv = np.concatenate(stack)
lo, hi = float(np.nanmin(allv)), float(np.nanmax(allv))
```

The comment above it — *"Everything shares one y-scale so the overlays are
comparable to the series they are overlaid on"* — is a correct and deliberate
design for the *forecast* overlay. It is fatal for the *difference* between two
overlays.

**(b) 🔴 Rescaling to the forecast band does NOT fix it — measured, and this
refutes the obvious candidate.** Rescaling so `lo/hi` come only from
`target ∪ with ∪ without`, over **all 1297 panels**:

| y-scale | median drawn Δ | share under 1 px | share under 0.5 px |
|---|---|---|---|
| shared, as today | 0.18 px | **77.7%** | 69.1% |
| forecast-band only | 0.31 px | **70.8%** | 59.7% |

It moves the median from 0.18 px to 0.31 px and takes the sub-pixel share from
77.7% to 70.8%. On `0becfd6ab2958396` specifically the forecast band is **14.102**
wide against a Δ of 0.159 — 0.29 px, not a fix. **The reason is arithmetic and
general: the two forecasts are nearly identical, so any scale that shows both
forecasts is ~2 orders of magnitude larger than their difference.** Do not
implement a rescale. (An earlier working note in this session recorded a
forecast-band range of 0.175 for that panel and concluded a rescale would
recover 27 px; that number was wrong — the measured band is 14.102.)

**(c) The modal adds zero resolution.** `MODAL_ASSETS`' `open()` does
`holder.appendChild(svg.cloneNode(true))` — it clones the 132 px SVG, whose
points were already envelope-downsampled to `_MAX_POINTS = 192`, and the CSS
stretches it to `min(58vh, 380px)` with `preserveAspectRatio='none'` (distorting
the aspect ratio as well). Enlarging 12.7× takes `0becfd6ab2958396` from 0.04 px
to **0.56 px**. There is no interaction that helps, which is the second half of
the user's complaint.

**What the effects actually are**, so the fix is sized to real data — max |Δ| as
a fraction of that panel's context sd, over all 1297 panels: p10 0.0024, p25
0.0120, **p50 0.0395**, p75 0.168, p90 0.492, p99 1.166. **31.9% exceed 10% of a
context sd** and only 8.1% fall below 0.1%. So most ablation effects are real and
small — not zero, and not visible on a shared axis. The fix must give the
difference **its own axis**.

#### Item E — a difference trace on its own scale ✅ DONE 2026-09-13

**File:** `tsfm_lens/report/sae_features.py::sparkline_svg` / `ablation_cell`.

Add an optional `diff: Sequence[float] | None` parameter to `sparkline_svg`.
When supplied, draw it in a **separate horizontal band** beneath the main chart
— not on the shared scale — with its own `lo/hi` taken from `diff` alone and a
zero line. Grow the SVG's `viewBox` height (e.g. 30 → 44) and give the diff band
the bottom ~12 units. Keep the existing `clean`/`patched` traces exactly as they
are: the top band answers *"what did the model forecast"*, the bottom band
answers *"what did this feature contribute"*, and they are different questions
that were being asked of one axis.

`ablation_cell` passes `diff = with_feature − without_feature` elementwise.
Guard: if either array is missing or their lengths differ, pass `None` and draw
no band — never zero-pad to a common length.

Give the band its own CSS class (`.spark-diff`) and a distinct colour from
`.spark-clean` / `.spark-patched`.

#### Item F — print the number ✅ DONE 2026-09-13

A trace on an auto-scaled axis always fills its band, so it cannot by itself
distinguish a 1.17-context-sd effect from a 0.002 one. Print both magnitudes:

- In the `<figcaption>` (today `"with · without"`): append
  `"· Δ {max:.3g} ({pct:.2g}% of context sd)"`.
- In `data-meta` (which the modal renders verbatim): append max |Δ| **and**
  mean |Δ|, both in raw units and in context-sd units.

Express the normalized figure in **context sd**, the same denominator the
flatness work in Item H uses, so the two surfaces of this section cannot
disagree about scale. Compute it in `ablation_cell` from the arrays already in
the entry — no corpus lookup, so it cannot pair a number with the wrong series
(the property `ablation_cell`'s docstring already claims).

#### Item G — the modal re-renders instead of cloning ✅ DONE 2026-09-13 (sub-fix 2 + template-fallback plumbing shipped; sub-fix 1, the resolution boost, measured and deliberately NOT shipped — see below)

Two sub-fixes in `MODAL_ASSETS` and `sparkline_svg`:

1. **Resolution.** Emit a second, high-resolution SVG per cell into a hidden
   `<template class='spark-full'>` inside the same `<figure>`, rendered by the
   same `sparkline_svg` at a larger `viewBox` and a larger point budget (pass
   `max_points` as a parameter; 1024 for the modal, `_MAX_POINTS` stays 192 for
   the inline cell). `open()` then clones the **template's** SVG when present and
   falls back to the inline one when absent, so a cell that did not emit a
   template still enlarges exactly as today.
2. **Aspect.** The modal copy must use `preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet'`,
   not `'none'` — the inline 132×30 cell wants `'none'` (it is a sparkline
   deliberately squashed to a row height), the enlarged copy does not.

⚠️ **Measure the HTML size cost before committing.** The section renders 1297
panels; a second SVG at 1024 points each is a real size increase on a file
already at ~5.4 MB. If the measured increase is unacceptable, the fallback
design is to emit the raw arrays once per cell as
`<script type="application/json">` and re-render in JS at modal size — more code,
smaller output. Decide from the measurement, not in advance.

**Acceptance for E+F+G together:** on `0becfd6ab2958396` and
`62946fb79a8606b9` — the two panels the user named — the with/without difference
is visible without enlarging, and the printed Δ matches a value recomputed by
hand from the artifact. Verify from the **rendered HTML**, by parsing the emitted
`points` attributes and confirming the diff band's drawn vertical extent exceeds
half its band height (§11.48 — read the output, not the diff).

**✅ DONE 2026-09-13.** `tsfm_lens/report/sae_features.py`: `sparkline_svg`
gained `diff: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None`, `max_points`, `viewbox_w`,

`MODAL_ASSETS`'s `open()` now checks for `cell.querySelector('template.spark-

Sampled 113 real forecast-pair cells from

### 32.7 Complaint 3, grounded: why the flat prediction lines, and is it correct? ✅ DONE (Item H, 2026-09-14)

**First, the label.** There is no family, archetype or cluster label named
"Spiky" anywhere in the repo — families are `block_bootstrap` / `mixture` /
`parametric` / `random_parametric` / `sequential_par`, and cluster labels read
like `"random_parametric (99%) · peaked spectrum · clean"`. "Spiky" appears once
per report as prose. The complaint is therefore read as *visually spiky panels*,
and flatness was measured directly rather than via a label.

**It is widespread.** Across 1297 ablation panels (722 distinct model×series),
**49.3% have a forecast sd below 10% of their context sd**, and 36.5% below 5%.

**`future_excursion` does not explain it.** §11.45's mechanism — a target
excursion beyond the context's own observed range — was the first hypothesis and
is **refuted**: flat and non-flat panels have statistically identical excursion
distributions (median 0.000 for both; 28.3% vs 31.3% above zero).

**Context lag-1 autocorrelation does.** Spearman **ρ = 0.626, p = 5.7e-142**
between context lag-1 autocorrelation and the forecast's sd ratio. Split at the
ends: noise-like contexts (lag1 < 0.2, n=449) are flat **78.6%** of the time;
smooth contexts (lag1 > 0.8, n=526) **13.9%**.

**By archetype, it is perfectly clean** — 0% flat on every structured archetype
and a majority on every noise-like one:

| archetype | n | flat share | median MASE |
|---|---|---|---|
| clean_low_noise | 40 | **0.0%** | 3.07 |
| seasonal_dominant | 35 | **0.0%** | 0.57 |
| nonsinusoidal_seasonal | 27 | **0.0%** | 2.94 |
| multi_seasonal_complex | 26 | **0.0%** | 1.59 |
| anomaly_heavy | 50 | 40.0% | 0.76 |
| noisy_chaotic | 34 | 41.2% | 0.72 |
| ar_colored_noise | 71 | **64.8%** | 0.79 |
| intermittent_bursts | 26 | **73.1%** | 0.97 |

**And flat panels forecast BETTER, not worse.** Median MASE **0.821** for flat
panels against **1.440** for non-flat (n=373 / 349). Monotone across buckets:
sd-ratio < 0.05 → median MASE 0.770; 0.05–0.1 → 0.923; 0.1–0.25 → 1.067;
0.25–0.5 → 2.562.

**So the answer to the user's two questions is:**

1. **Is this correct behavior?** Largely yes, and this is §11.45's lesson
   generalized from a *range* to a *structure*: on a context with no
   autocorrelation to extrapolate, reverting to the mean is the MMSE-optimal
   forecast, and the MASE numbers confirm the models are not being punished for
   it — they do *better* there. A flat line on `ar_colored_noise` is a correct
   response; a flat line on `seasonal_dominant` would be a defect, and there are
   **zero** of those.
2. **Is the data too unrealistic?** No — but the corpus is deliberately
   noise-heavy, and that is a *corpus composition* fact, not a model failure.
   `ar_colored_noise`, `anomaly_heavy`, `noisy_chaotic` and `intermittent_bursts`
   together account for 181 of the 722 panels, and they are where essentially all
   the flatness lives.

🔴 **But it is not purely an information ceiling, and this is the part that
needs work.** On the **same series**, the four models differ by ~6×:

| model | median forecast sd ratio | share flat |
|---|---|---|
| TimesFM | 0.261 | 38.5% |
| Sundial | 0.106 | 45.7% |
| Chronos-Bolt | 0.067 | 56.5% |
| Chronos-2 | 0.041 | 63.9% |

If flatness were purely "there is nothing to predict", the four would agree.
They do not — Chronos-2 reverts to the mean where TimesFM does not, on identical
inputs. That is a real, unstated behavioral difference between the models, and
it belongs in the report.

✅ **The confound is CLOSED, and it was closed with data already on disk
(corrected 2026-09-12, same session).** This paragraph originally read that the
raw-model baseline "does not exist on disk and requires recomputation", on the
grounds that `l0/metrics.parquet` stores only scalars. That is true of
`metrics.parquet` and **irrelevant**: every forecast entry in every
`sae/<model>/<layer>_ablation.json` already carries an **`unpatched`** array
beside `with_feature`/`without_feature`, written by
`sae/response.py:732,837` as `adapter.predict(...)` with **no patch at all** —
the genuine raw-model forecast, kept expressly "so the SAE's own reconstruction
cost stays visible rather than being charged to the feature". The baseline was
one field away the whole time.

Measured over all 1297 panels, forecast sd ÷ context sd:

| model | raw model | SAE reconstruction | raw % flat | recon % flat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chronos-2 | 0.055 | 0.041 | 60.6% | 63.9% |
| Chronos-Bolt | 0.098 | 0.067 | 50.0% | 56.5% |
| Sundial | 0.110 | 0.106 | 47.6% | 45.7% |
| TimesFM | 0.299 | 0.261 | 34.9% | 38.5% |
| **overall** | **0.114** | **0.102** | **46.9%** | **49.3%** |

**The SAE accounts for 2.4 percentage points of the 49.3%.** The ~5.4×
per-model spread is present in the *raw* forecasts (0.055 → 0.299) before any
dictionary touches them, so §32.7's per-model flatness finding is a **model
property**, not a reconstruction artifact, and may be rendered as one. H4(ii)
below therefore costs zero forward passes.

**Addendum (2026-09-27): preprocessing ruled out; flat share traced to corpus composition.**
This was an orchestrator re-check prompted by a user question ("predictions super smoothed out — is
something wrong with preprocessing?"). It used scratch scripts outside the repo, 240–400 stratified
dev series, and stored predictions for all 965 series.

- **Preprocessing is not the cause.** `data.py::_assemble` only crops to context+horizon as float32;
  no adapter rescales its input. Native library forecasts match the adapters (median |Δ| in
  context-sd units):
  - Chronos-2: 0.0026
  - Chronos-Bolt: 0.0023
  - TimesFM native `forecast()` with all `ForecastConfig` options on: 0.028. The adapter calls
    `tfm.model.decode` directly and bypasses `normalize_inputs` / `force_flip_invariance` /
    `infer_is_positive` / `fix_quantile_crossing`.

  Flat fraction, native vs adapter: TimesFM 0.5167 vs 0.4917; Chronos-2 0.5083 vs 0.5083;
  Bolt 0.5083 vs 0.5083. The Chronos models' bf16 vs native fp32 is negligible. Sundial's native
  `generate` fails on the installed transformers (`DynamicCache.seen_tokens` AttributeError), but the
  adapter's forward path is unaffected.
- **Smoothness is by design: point = central estimate.** Sundial's single sample has sd ratio
  0.4195; the median of 20 samples has 0.161 (the target's own sd ratio is ~0.82). The single sample
  is *worse* (MASE 1.472).
- **Flat forecasts are rare on periodic contexts.** Periodic here means differenced-series ACF at
  lags ≥ 8 above 0.3 (91 of 400).

  | Model | Flat, periodic | Flat, non-periodic | MASE flat | MASE non-flat |
  |---|---|---|---|---|

  All models beat naive (1.904) and seasonal-naive (1.912) on MASE: 1.138 / 1.065 / 1.323 / 1.407.
- **The flat share is a benchmark-composition effect.** The real-derived tier is 410/965 ≈ 42% of the

### 32.7b Complaint 2, second half: 55.8% of the rendered panels are features the battery already scored as causally null ✅ DONE (Item I, 2026-09-13)

> **The question that produced this** (2026-09-12, user, on reading §32.6):
> *"why are there even any features that have little to no change from
> with/without feature? How can it activate on a series while also not moving
> it at all?"*

Measured, not reasoned. It has four separate answers and the first is a defect.

**(1) 🔴 Most of them are not "fires but does nothing" — they are features the
battery already measured as null, rendered anyway.** Of the 565 candidates the
SAE section draws overlays for, **364 (64.4%) cleared zero of the nine causal
channels**, accounting for **724 of the 1297 panels (55.8%)**. And the
relationship to the drawn effect is monotone and near-total at the bottom:

| max\|with − without\| (context sd) | panels | mean channels clearing | share clearing **zero** | median forecast flatness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| < 0.1% | 105 | 0.06 | **98.1%** | 0.183 |
| 0.1–1% | 173 | 0.44 | 82.1% | 0.023 |
| 1–5% | 440 | 1.81 | 57.7% | 0.062 |
| 5–20% | 277 | 3.47 | 31.4% | 0.127 |
| > 20% | 302 | 2.78 | 45.7% | 0.322 |

**98.1% of the panels with a sub-0.1% effect belong to features that cleared
nothing.** The battery — which scores each feature against a *matched-magnitude
random-direction* null, i.e. against removing that much of something arbitrary —
already knows these are not causal. The report renders them with the same
visual prominence as the features that did clear. So the user's "how can it
activate and not move it" is, for the majority of cases, the correct reading of
a panel that should not have been given equal billing: **the picture disagrees
with the measurement sitting next to it, and the picture is the one that is
wrong.**

Per model, share of candidates clearing zero channels: TimesFM 69.7% (140/201),
Chronos-Bolt 71.1% (64/90), Sundial 62.1% (87/140), Chronos-2 54.5% (73/134).

**(2) Activation is the length of the removed vector, but it is rendered with no
normalizer — so it is not comparable across panels.** `TopKSAE.normalize_decoder_`
projects dictionary columns to **unit norm** (`sae/models.py:57–66`), so a
feature's activation *is* the L2 length of the vector removed. What the card does
not say is what it is a length *of*. Median hidden-state norm at the four
targets the user's panels come from differs by **55×**:

| target | median ‖h‖ | median activation | atom as share of ‖h‖ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chronos-2 / encoder.block.8 | 2.62 | 0.193 | 8.0% |
| Chronos-Bolt / encoder.block.4 | 5.78 | 0.313 | 6.1% |
| Sundial / model.layers.3 | 52.77 | 13.233 | 15.8% |
| TimesFM / stacked_xf.10 | 143.25 | 23.303 | 18.5% |

So `activation 0.31` on Chronos-2 and `activation 23.13` on Sundial — both of
which the user saw in the same section — are **11.8%** and **43.8%** of their
own hidden states. The rendered numbers differ by 75×; the quantities they
stand for differ by 3.7× *in the other direction*. This is §11.57's shape
exactly: a quantity rendered without the normalizer that makes it meaningful,
where the label gives the reader no way to know.

**(3) The transfer from "fraction of the hidden state removed" to "forecast
movement" is strongly model-dependent, and that is a real finding.** Within
model, removed-fraction predicts effect well (Spearman: TimesFM +0.747,
Chronos-Bolt +0.697, Chronos-2 +0.367, Sundial +0.269; all p ≤ 2e-07). But at
comparable median removed-fractions — Sundial 15.8%, TimesFM 18.5% — the median
effect is **0.040 vs 0.275**, ~7× apart. Sundial's forecast at `model.layers.3`
is far more robust to losing any single direction than TimesFM's at
`stacked_xf.10`. Whether that is depth, architecture, or dictionary quality is
**not** determined here.

**(4) A degenerate forecast cannot move, and that is the user's first example.**
`0becfd6ab2958396` (Chronos-2, feature 3327, activation 1.031) is the
**highest-activation panel in its entire target** and removes **39.3%** of the
hidden state's norm — yet its with-feature forecast has sd = **0.001 × context
sd**, i.e. it is a constant line. Removing two fifths of the representation
still leaves a constant. This is §32.7's flatness finding meeting this one, and
it is why Item H's clause and Item I's gate are complementary rather than
redundant.

**The user's second example is the opposite case and is not a null at all.**
`62946fb79a8606b9` (Chronos-2, feature 3440, activation 0.309 — the **70th
percentile** for that dictionary, not a weak firing) moves the forecast by
**3.6% of a context sd** on a forecast that is not flat (sd ratio 0.739). That
is a small, real, specific effect that is invisible only because it is drawn at
0.27 px. **Item E/F fixes that one; Item I below fixes the other.**

#### Item I — a panel earns its prominence from the measurement beside it ✅ DONE (2026-09-13)

**Files:** `tsfm_lens/report/sae_features.py::ablation_cell`,
`tsfm_lens/report/sae_concepts.py`.

**I1. Do not render a full-prominence overlay for a candidate with
`n_channels_clearing == 0`.** Collapse those panels behind a `<details>`
(*"{n} feature(s) whose ablation did not move any channel past its own null"*)
rather than deleting them — a measured null is a result and §2.1 forbids
quietly dropping it, but it must not compete visually with a measured effect.
Read `n_channels_clearing` from the candidate record; **do not re-derive a
threshold in `report.py`** — the artifact's own count is the authority
(§31.4/§26 E's rule that the gate's verdict travels as data).

**I2. Label the activation with its normalizer.** Render activation as a
**fraction of the median hidden-state norm at that target** alongside the raw
value — `"activation 0.31 (12% of a typical hidden state)"`. The median ‖h‖ is
one reduction over the activation store and should be computed once per target
in the SAE stage and written into `sae/meta.json`, **not** recomputed in the
report (which has no store handle in a report-only rerun).

**I3. State the null the battery used, once per section.** The overlay's
implicit question is "did removing this feature change the forecast"; the
battery's actual question is "more than removing that much of an arbitrary
direction". Those differ, and only the second is a claim about the *feature*.
One sentence in the section note.

**I4. Show the reconstruction cost.** `unpatched` is in the artifact. Median
reconstruction cost is **0.139 context sd** against a median feature effect of
**0.0395** — **the SAE's own reconstruction error moves the forecast ~3.5×
more than removing an entire feature does**, and 23.0% of panels have a feature
effect under a tenth of their reconstruction cost. Draw `unpatched` as a third,
muted trace so a reader can see how much of the gap between the lines is the
dictionary rather than the feature. (`ablation_cell`'s docstring already states
the with-arm is the full reconstruction *for this reason*; the trace makes the

### 32.7c 🔴 Qwen structurally cannot answer the question that was asked — the gloss is missing, not the generation ✅ DONE (Item J, 2026-09-13)

> **The question that produced this** (2026-09-12, user, on reading the plan):
> *"So with this plan how will the descriptions of features and groups of
> features be generated? Is Qwen good at this?"*

Item A ports the narrator to concepts. Measured against the user's **original**
complaint — *"what does 'strong raises spectral_centroid' mean
qualitatively"* — **Item A alone will not fix it**, and the reason is
architectural rather than a question of model quality.

**(1) The plain-English half is a hand-written table, not generated.**
`sae/describe.py::CHANNEL_GLOSS` maps each of the nine channels to fixed
English, used verbatim by `machine_fallback` and licensed to the narrator.
Qwen *consumes* it; it never produces it. Six of the nine entries are real
translations (`dispersion` → "the forecast's spread", `mase` → "forecast
error"). **`spectral_centroid` → "the forecast's spectral centroid" is
circular** — it restates the term, which is precisely the string the user could
not interpret.

**(2) And `glossary.py` does not cover the channels.** Of the 40 terms it
defines, exactly **one of the nine causal channels appears** (`mase`). `trend`,
`seasonal`, `spectral_centroid`, `level`, `dispersion`, `horizon_shape_near`,
`horizon_shape_far` and `flatness` are **absent**. So the section's most
frequently rendered vocabulary is the part of the report with no definitions at
all — the same defect §31.6 already records for the `ΔMASE sign` and
`alignment mean abs rho` columns, at nine times the frequency.

**(3) 🔴 The guard that makes the narrator safe is exactly what forbids it from
closing this gap.** `check_text` is a **concept allowlist over the evidence
packet** — live rejection reasons include *"the answer mentioned 'level', which
is not in the evidence"*. A sentence explaining what a spectral centroid *is*
is a fact about the **metric**, not about the feature, so it is not in the
packet, so a correct guard **must** reject it. Loosening the guard to admit it
would re-open the fabrication surface §11.51/§11.53 spent ten findings closing.
**The interpretation therefore cannot come from the narrator at any model size.
It is a missing lookup table, and it must stay deterministic.**

#### Item J — a non-circular meaning for every channel, written once ✅ DONE (2026-09-13)

**Files:** `tsfm_lens/sae/describe.py`, `tsfm_lens/glossary.py`,
`tsfm_lens/report/sae_features.py::term_legend_html`.

**J1.** Add `CHANNEL_MEANING`: one plain sentence per channel, stating what the
quantity is and what a rise/fall looks like in a forecast — e.g.
*"spectral centroid: how fast the forecast wiggles. Raising it makes the
forecast choppier and more high-frequency; lowering it makes it smoother."*
Written by a human, reviewed once, **never generated**.

**J2.** Render it through the machinery that already exists: `abbr.term` +
`term_legend_html` in `sae_features.py`, so every channel name in the section
carries its meaning on hover and the legend lists all nine. This costs nothing
per-render and fixes the complaint at **every** site the channel name appears,
not only inside descriptions.

**J3.** Add the nine to `glossary.py` so the two surfaces cannot drift — same
no-drift shape `stage_docs.py`/`glossary.py` already use, with
`render_glossary.py --check` as the stale gate.

**J4.** Pass the meaning into the evidence packet as **licensed** content so a
narrated sentence may use it without the guard refusing. This is the one place
the narrator's vocabulary should be *widened*, and per §11.51 lesson 1 the
guard must be extended in the same edit.

**Acceptance:** all nine channels have a gloss; **no gloss contains its own
channel name** (the circularity test — it fails today on `spectral_centroid`);
`render_glossary.py --check` green. **Load-bearing negative:** a gloss that
merely expands the identifier (`"spectral_centroid"` → `"the spectral
centroid"`) must **fail** the test, or the test passes against the current
defect.

✅ **DONE 2026-09-13 (J1–J3 landed in an earlier firing this session; J4 —
the harder half, widening the guard in the same edit as the evidence — is
what this firing closed).** `sae/describe.py::CHANNEL_MEANING` composes one
sentence per channel from `sae/vocab.py::CHANNEL_DEFS`'s existing `what`/`high`
fields (per `CLAUDE.md` sec 11.53's "two hand-maintained vocabularies" trap —
not a fourth hand-typed table), covers all **9** channels, and
`_assert_glosses_self_consistent` enforces both non-circularity and
guard-passability **at import time**. `glossary.py` grew from 40 to **48**
entries (`channel-trend`/`-seasonal`/`-spectral-centroid`/`-level`/
`-dispersion`/`-horizon-near`/`-horizon-far`/`-flatness`, plus the
pre-existing `mase`); `render_glossary.py --check` is green.

🔴 **J4's real work was finding that widening the EVIDENCE silently defeated
an EXISTING guard test, not just extending `check_text` for new vocabulary —
CLAUDE.md sec 11.55's shape, hit while building the fix that sec 11.55
itself documents.** Three channels' `high`-clause vocabulary
(`spectral_centroid`: "choppier"/"higher-frequency"; `dispersion`: "swing
more"; `seasonal`: "more strongly periodic") is not covered by the generic
`UP_VERBS`/`DOWN_VERBS` scan at all, so rendering `CHANNEL_MEANING` into
`render_evidence` made those three words freely usable regardless of the
packet's actual sign — confirmed live: "This feature makes the forecast
smoother and slower-moving" was **ACCEPTED** on a positive-`spectral_centroid`
packet before the fix. Closed with `CHANNEL_HIGH_TERMS` (a per-channel term
table) + `_CHANNEL_HIGH_PATTERNS`, gated in `check_text` on that ONE
channel's own signed value via `_signed_channels(ev)` — mirroring the
pre-existing `QUALITY_WORSE`/`QUALITY_BETTER` channel-specific gate exactly,
not the packet-wide existential `has_up`/`has_down` scan the rest of the
module uses. Deliberately narrow: the `what` clause's bidirectional "low
means X, high means Y" framing stays unguarded, since it explains the
quantity for both directions at once and is not itself a claim about the
packet (`_assert_glosses_self_consistent` already treats it as safe to quote
whole under a positive-signed packet).

**A second, larger gap surfaced only by running the pre-existing regression
suite, not by design review**: `tests/test_sae_describe.py::
test_render_evidence_mentions_nothing_the_guard_would_forbid` (which feeds
every line of `render_evidence`'s own output back through `check_text`)
failed the moment the new "what these channels measure:" block was added —
**not** on the three `CHANNEL_HIGH_TERMS` channels, but on `level`, whose
`high` clause ("Feature raises the whole forecast") uses vocabulary ALREADY
in the generic `UP_VERBS` list ("raises"). For a packet where `level` (or
every named channel) is signed negative, showing that sentence puts a
self-contradicting exemplar directly in the narrator's own prompt — exactly
what sec 11.51's "an exemplar of fabrication sitting in the prompt is the
most direct way to teach it" warns against, and a strictly larger class of
channels than the three `CHANNEL_HIGH_TERMS` covers (any of the 9 whose
`high` clause happens to reuse already-licensed direction vocabulary:
`trend`'s "pushes...upward", `level`'s "raises", `mase`'s "WORSE (higher
error)"). Fixed at the render site, not the vocabulary: added
`CHANNEL_MEANING_NEUTRAL` (the `what` clause alone, direction-free) and
`render_evidence` now shows the full `CHANNEL_MEANING` for a named channel
only when `_signed_channels(ev)` reads that channel as non-negative and
undirected; otherwise the neutral half. `_assert_glosses_self_consistent`
gained a matching check that every `CHANNEL_MEANING_NEUTRAL` entry passes
`check_text` under a **negatively**-signed packet for that same channel —
proving the neutral half is genuinely direction-free rather than merely
untested in that direction.

**Verification, all via pytest (no ad-hoc interpreter checks left
unconverted):** 8 new tests added to `tests/test_sae_describe.py` (the

circularity coverage including the acceptance criterion's own load-bearing

### 32.7d Is Qwen good at this? — measured, and the answer is "good at one half, unreliable at the other"

Recorded so the next session does not re-litigate it. `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`
at the pinned revision, on `runs/full_report_run_4model`:

| kind | accepted | rate |
|---|---|---|
| roles | 73 / 88 | **83.0%** |
| features | 67 / 104 | **64.4%** |

(`full_report_run_large_revived`, for comparison: roles 26/28 = 92.9%, features
37/88 = 42.0%. **Report by state, never pooled** — the spread is the packet's
evidence content, not the model's mood.)

**Every rejection is a fabrication, not a style miss.** The top live reasons:
*"said 'upward', but no channel in the evidence moved upward"* (4),
*"said 'above the null', but the evidence records no channel that cleared"* (4),
*"said 'no other', but the evidence lists more than one channel"* (3),
*"mentioned 'level', which is not in the evidence"* (3), *"said 'all series',
which nothing in the evidence measures"* (3). So roughly **one feature attempt
in three asserts something the measurement does not support**, and the guard —
not the model — is what keeps it out.

**What Qwen actually contributes is paraphrase, not interpretation.** Side by
side, same evidence:

- machine fallback: *"This feature moves the far horizon of the forecast (2.14
  times the random-direction null), and also the forecast's overall level,
  strongest on series with a smaller dominant seasonal period (rho 0.26,
  n 443)."*
- Qwen, accepted: *"Patching this role reshapes the forecast's distant and
  immediate horizons, increasing its trend slope, most strongly on series with a
  larger dominant seasonal period."*

The generated sentence reads more naturally and **drops the effect size and the
rho/n**. The deterministic one is arguably the better artifact for this report.
Qwen's measurable contribution is varying "near/far" to "immediate/distant" —
real legibility value, and **zero** interpretive value, which is expected: the
packet is all it sees and the English glosses are already written (§32.7c(1)).

**This conclusion already has precedent in this repo, reached independently.**
§28.12 made `prefer_deterministic_summary=True` the default for cross-model
summaries after four consecutive regenerations each produced a *new class* of
unsupported claim, with **4 of 6 generated summaries passing every guard and 2
of those visibly wrong**, against 6 of 6 deterministic sentences correct.

✅ **DECIDED by the user, 2026-09-12 — Item A renders the DETERMINISTIC
sentence by default.** Presented with the measured trade (83% acceptance on
concept-shaped packets, every rejection a caught fabrication, and a machine
fallback that carries the effect size and rho/n the generated sentence drops),
the call is: **the card renders `machine_fallback`'s composed sentence; the
Qwen attempt is still generated, guarded by `check_text`, and persisted under
its own key for audit.** This is byte-for-byte the pattern §28.12 already chose
for cross-model summaries — `prefer_deterministic_summary=True` — reached
independently at a second site, which is the strongest evidence available that
it is the right default here.

Two things this binds Item A to, and a smaller model must not quietly drop
either:
1. **The generated attempt is still produced and still guarded.** Turning the
   narrator off entirely is NOT what was decided — the audit trail is the
   point, and it is what would justify flipping the default later on evidence
   rather than on taste.
2. **`run_sae_describe.py` must report which state each concept is in — three
   states, not two** (§11.37): rendered-deterministic-and-the-generated-one
   also passed, rendered-deterministic-and-the-generated-one-was-refused, and
   no-battery-ran. `_summary_state` in `run_sae_compare.py` is the shape to
   copy; collapsing the first two would assert a comparison that never
   happened.

**Recommendation, and it is a decision to take explicitly rather than drift
into.** Keep the narrator for **per-concept** descriptions, where the unit is
small, the evidence is concrete, and acceptance is 83%. Do **not** extend it to
section-level or cross-concept synthesis — that is where §28.12's four-round
failure lives. And do not expect a larger model to change the interpretation
picture: the limit is the packet and the allowlist, not the parameter count.
**Item J is what actually answers the user's complaint; Item A makes the answer
read well.**

🔴 **And when everything here is done, ONE of the two paths gets deleted —
carrying both indefinitely is not the plan (user-directed, 2026-09-12).** The
decision above keeps the generated sentence *as an audit trail*, and an audit
trail is scaffolding for a decision that is still open: does the narrator ever
earn the render slot? That question closes when Items A–M are done and a run's
`descriptions.json` has been read end to end at least once more. At that point
exactly one of these happens, and it is recorded here with its evidence:

- **The deterministic path wins** (the expected outcome on current numbers) —
  delete `describe_batch`, the Qwen model plumbing, `check_text`'s
  generation-facing half, and the `--device`/revision-pinning surface that
  exists only to run the weights. `render_evidence`, the packet builders and
  the machine fallbacks all stay: those are the deterministic path. A 2.9 GB
  model download and a guard that has now caught fabrications through **ten**
  distinct licensed vocabularies (§11.53) is a lot of machinery to keep warm
  for a column nobody renders.
- **The generated path wins** — then the deterministic fallback narrows to what
  a fallback is for (a refused or errored generation) and stops being a
  second, fully-parallel narrator maintained line-for-line beside the first.

What must NOT happen is the third outcome, which is what happens by default if
nobody decides: both paths carried forever, each needing its guard extended
every time a channel or evidence field is added, with the report rendering one
and the artifact holding the other. Whichever is deleted, the **finding** stays
— §28.12's four-round audit and §32.7d's acceptance tables are the record of
why, and CLAUDE.md §2.9 is explicit that deleting the code never licenses
deleting the measurement that decided it.

This is the local instance of a repo-wide rule added the same day: **CLAUDE.md
§2.9, "Scaffolding comes down once the decision it supported is made."** Read
it before deleting anything — it names what does *not* count as dead
computation (a control, a null, a permutation test, a real failure branch, a
standalone study driver whose output a human reads) and records that a
grep-based dead-code survey on this repo produced a **50% false-positive
rate**, so deadness is established by measurement, not by search. The one
grounded candidate that survey did find is written up there:
`tsfm_lens/report/sae_role_matching.py`, 581 lines with zero live importers,
kept alive solely by its own 199-line test file after §30 stage 4 superseded
`roles.json` with `concepts.json`.

### 32.11 ✅ IMPLEMENTED — the with/without lines appeared to start far off the end of the context, and it was the context that was drawn wrong

> **User report (2026-09-12):** *"Some graphs have with/without feature
> forecasts starting far above/below where the context ends, which should not
> be happening (one example is f0afa2022555dda5 but there are more). Please
> fix."*

**This is the one item in §32 that IS implemented** — the user asked for the
fix directly. Everything else here remains design-only.

**Grounded first (§2.4), and the first suspect was wrong.** The named series'
own data is fine: across its six panels the true gap between `context[-1]` and
`with_feature[0]` is **0.04 to 0.31 context-sd**. So nothing in the ablation
artifact is misaligned, and no forecast is anchored to the wrong series.

The defect was in `report/sae_features.py::_envelope`. It downsamples by
bucketing and emitting each bucket's **min and max in time order** — correct,
and deliberately so, because plain decimation deletes the spikes an
intermittency feature exists to detect. But preserving extrema does not
preserve **endpoints**, and `sparkline_svg` draws the context and the forecast
as two polylines meeting at the cut, so the context's last drawn point is
precisely where a reader sees the forecast being anchored.

**The measurement, on `runs/full_report_run_4model`'s 1297 panels:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| median seam jump | 1.80 px | **1.10 px** |
| p90 | 7.70 px | **5.20 px** |
| max | 24.80 px | 19.20 px (real) |
| panels jumping >2px (>7% of a 30px chart) | 46.4% | **29.3%** |
| correlation with the TRUE endpoint gap | 0.653 | **0.944** |

The clinching case is `7500ab0a3b48b75f` (intermittent): it ends at **0.0**
and its forecast starts at **−0.1** — a **0.09 px** jump — and was drawn ending
at **20.6**, the max of its last bucket, putting the seam **17.64 px** out on a
30 px chart. The forecast's own start was off by 0.00 px. The entire apparent
offset was the context.

**Fix.** `_envelope` now appends the true first and last values when the
bucketing did not already emit them:

```python
head = y[:1] if (np.isfinite(y[0]) and out[0] != y[0]) else out[:0]
tail = y[-1:] if (np.isfinite(y[-1]) and out[-1] != y[-1]) else out[:0]
return np.concatenate([head, out, tail]) if head.size or tail.size else out
```

**Appended, never substituted** — substituting would trade away an extreme in
the first or last bucket, which is the one thing this function exists to keep.
Costs at most 2 points of a ~170-point budget. Benefits the exemplar
sparklines too, which share `sparkline_svg`.

**Verified from rendered SVG, not from the diff (§11.48):** re-parsing every
panel's polyline points, the drawn seam now matches the seam the true endpoints
imply to within **0.098 px** everywhere (the SVG rounds coordinates to one
decimal). The residual 19.2 px maximum is `610365adc3d36cf4`, whose forecast
genuinely leaves its context by 6.55 context-sd — correctly drawn at full size.

**Tests (`tests/test_sae_features.py`), each confirmed to discriminate by
planting its regression:**
- endpoints are pinned (fails when the fix is reverted);
- endpoints are **appended, not substituted** (fails against a plant that
  writes `out[0], out[-1] = y[0], y[-1]`, which eats a leading spike);
- an intermittent context does not fake a jump at the seam (the live defect);
- **load-bearing negative:** a genuine 10-unit forecast discontinuity must
  still render >20 px, so the fix cannot be satisfied by flattening the seam.

⚠️ **One pre-existing test had to be re-indexed and one of my own fixtures was
half-inert** — recorded because it is §11.53's postscript again.
`test_envelope_keeps_extremes_in_time_order` indexed `out[0]`/`out[1]`
absolutely, which the prepended endpoint shifts; it now locates bucket 0
explicitly and says why. And the first draft of the pinning test passed with
the **tail** pin removed, because under seed 0 the fixture's last value happened
to be its own bucket's extremum — pinned for free. The fixture now asserts both
endpoints are strictly **inside** their bucket's range before testing anything.

### 32.12 Why some features render one panel instead of three — not a bug, but nothing says so 📋 NEEDS IMPLEMENTATION

> **User report (2026-09-12):** *"some features only have 1 graph instead of
> 3, why is that?"*

**Measured over all 13 targets: `n_forecasts == n_top_series` exactly, at every
one of 452 scorable candidates.** The histogram:

| panels drawn | features |
|---|---|
| 1 | 23 |
| 2 | 13 |
| 3 | 416 |

`sae/response.py::_top_series_for_feature` returns only rows where the atom is
**strictly non-zero**, and its docstring already states the reason: *"the series
it fires hardest on cannot include a series it does not fire on, and padding
the list to `k` with silent zeros would put series carrying no signal into the
very panel built to show the feature's effect."* That is right, and is §11.37's
rule applied correctly — absent is not tiny.

**So a one-panel feature fires on exactly one series in the sampled corpus**,
and its entire causal measurement rests on n = 1. These are also the weakest
atoms: mean activation on their single series runs **0.037–0.109**.

🔴 **The defect is that the report does not say this.** A reader sees one graph
where the neighbouring row has three and reads truncation — a rendering
accident — when the real content is *this feature is rare, and its numbers are
an n-of-1*. That is §11.54's shape: a correct field whose meaning the layout
misstates by omission.

#### Item K — the panel count says what it counts ✅ DONE (2026-09-13)

**File:** `tsfm_lens/report/sae_features.py::ablation_cell`.

**K1.** When `len(fcs) < 3`, append a short clause to the cell naming the
cause: *"fires on only 1 series in this sample — every number in this row is
an n-of-1."* Read it from the candidate's own `n_top_series`, never from

described as truncated rather than as rare (they are different facts, and today
the cell cannot tell them apart either).

**K2.** Pass `n_top_series` into `ablation_cell` — it is on the candidate dict
and is currently dropped at the call site.

**Acceptance:** a candidate with `n_top_series=1` renders the clause; one with
`n_top_series=8` truncated to 3 by `--keep-forecasts` renders a *different*
clause. **Load-bearing negative:** a fixture where `n_top_series=8` and
`keep_forecasts=1` must **not** say the feature is rare — deriving the clause
from the panel count alone passes every other assertion and is the bug.

**K3** (cheap, and worth more than K1): carry `n_top_series` into the row's
sort key or a column, so a reader can see at a glance that 36 of 452 candidates
are n≤2. Item I already down-ranks panels whose battery cleared nothing; this
is the same argument for a different statistic.

✅ **DONE 2026-09-13.** `ablation_cell` (`tsfm_lens/report/sae_features.py`)
now reads `entry.get("n_top_series")` directly — **K2 needed no plumbing
change at all**: `entry` passed into `ablation_cell` is already the raw
candidate dict (`report.py::_ablation_entries` returns
`{feature: candidate}` unmodified, confirmed by grepping `report.py` for
`n_top_series` and finding zero hits before this change — the field was
simply never read, not stripped in transit). ROADMAP's own wording ("dropped
at the call site") turned out to be imprecise; the correct diagnosis is
"present on the dict, never consumed."

🔴 **Before implementing, checked whether K3's "Item I already down-ranks
panels" premise holds — it does not.** Item I (§ above, "a panel earns its

second sort mode.
